These relatively featureless probability distributions coexist with pronounced delayed temporal correlations, distinguishing them from equilibrium high-temperature behavior. We further show analytically that these delay-induced near-uniform distributions emerge in a broad class of stochastic networks that lack symmetry-breaking bias fields. Introducing symmetry-breaking bias fields restores a strong dependence of the steady state on interactions with qualitatively modified behavior. Simulations of networks with five coupled spins demonstrate that these effects persist beyond minimal systems with only two spins.

authors.name: Hantao Zhang, Sidra Gibeault, Matthew W. Daniels, Philippe Talatchian, Ursula Ebels, Advait Madhavan, Mark D. Stiles

papers.title: Implementation and verification of the avalanche source in a 3D full-f particle-in-cell model of relativistic electrons for studies of tokamak disruptions
papers.summary: Tokamak disruptions may lead to the acceleration of some electrons to relativistic energies. These so-called runaway electrons (REs) can multiply exponentially via knock-on collisions with thermal electrons. As the resulting RE avalanche is exponentially sensitive to the pre-disruption plasma current, multi-MA RE beams may form in large future devices, risking severe localized wall damage. In this work, an energy and momentum conserving knock-on collision operator is implemented in the 3D nonlinear MHD code JOREK for the full-f relativistic hybrid fluid-kinetic model that describes the REs using the particle-in-cell (PiC) approach both for full-orbit and drift-kinetic markers, which will enable accurate modeling of the RE phase-space dynamics in realistic 3D electromagnetic fields. Such a self-consistent treatment of the RE avalanche and competing losses in the stochastic fields of MHD-active plasmas is required to further the understanding of RE transport and phase-space dynamics in self-consistent interaction with the 3D plasma evolution, which is needed for developing reliable predictions as well as reliable mitigation methods. To make such novel high-fidelity simulations computationally viable, a resampling technique was also implemented to restrict the number of markers. The avalanche model is verified using analytical expressions from literature and applied to a JET-like termination scenario, demonstrating its applicability to realistic 3D MHD active scenarios. Future work on porting to accelerated high-performance computing systems will be needed to cross the long time scales involved, e.g., in periodic termination and re-avalanching that could occur in large devices like ITER.

authors.name: Fiona Wouters, Hannes Bergstr\"om, Matthias Hoelzl, Guido T. A. Huijsmans, Jan van Dijk, the JOREK team

papers.title: A Transient-Network Model of Condensate Aging and Morphology Transition in Phase Separation
papers.summary: Biomolecular condensates can undergo striking changes, such as transitioning from a liquid-like to a gel- or a solid-like aggregate due to changes in molecular interactions in response to changes in the biochemical environment. The question of how modified molecular interactions lead to such a transition in the material properties and spatial organization of condensates has not yet been elucidated. To address this question, we represent the biochemical environment as a triphasic mixture comprising a liquid-like protein-rich phase, a network-like protein-rich phase, and solvent. Owing to a change in the biochemical environment, protein molecules can reversibly switch between two conformational states. In a switched conformational state, the cross-linking domains of molecules are exposed which promote transient network formation in phase separated states. We develop a transient-network model and a continuum framework that couples phase separation, molecular switching, and dynamic cross-linking to predict condensate morphology and mechanics. The transient-network model predicts that a non-aging network behaves like a Maxwell fluid. When a network slowly ages via stabilization of cross-links, it shows Maxwell-like behavior and waiting time-dependent relaxation. However, a strongly aged network shows elastic recoil like characteristic of a Kelvin-Voigt solid. Our coupled continuum model demonstrates that the interplay of molecular switching and dynamic cross-linking in network formation shapes the spatial organization of condensate phases. In summary, this work demonstrates a mechanistic route explaining how conformational switching and molecular cross-linking regulate material properties and morphology of condensates.

authors.name: Bhanjan Debnath

papers.title: Constrained estimation of rotational invariants of the cumulant expansion (RICE) for rapid tensor-valued diffusion MRI
papers.summary: Purpose: To complement 1.5-minute measurements of common tensor-valued diffusion MRI (dMRI) markers with rapid constrained fitting. Methods: Fast dMRI protocols for obtaining rotational invariants of the cumulant expansion (RICE) were paired with constrained weighted linear least squares (CWLLS) to stabilize the more fragile WLLS fit. A compact constraint set was formulated, including a novel mean-dependent upper bound on total diffusional variance. Evaluation used diffusion tensor distribution (DTD) simulations, healthy-volunteer data with a resolution-dependent SNR experiment, and a glioma patient dataset. A 5-minute q-space trajectory imaging (QTI) protocol served as a reference. Results: Across experiments, CWLLS reduced unphysical estimates and fit outliers in parameters such as microscopic FA and isotropic diffusivity variance. In simulations, it narrowed error distributions most clearly in the CSF-dominant case, while some metrics showed a bias-variance trade-off. In vivo, CWLLS removed negative variance estimates, truncated out-of-bounds tails, and reduced artifacts in fluid-contaminated voxels while preserving anatomical contrast. It also retained more stable maps than WLLS at higher resolution, although both estimators degraded in the lowest-SNR setting. Notably, the new mean-dependent variance bound was violated in 15.4% of voxels in the patient dataset, accounting for nearly half of the 32.7% that violated at least one constraint. Healthy-volunteer benchmarking showed that CWLLS completed in under 30 seconds. The constrained QTI fit required 72 minutes, making CWLLS 160 times faster. Conclusion: CWLLS for fast RICE yielded high-quality parameter maps at an online-ready computational cost. This may enhance the reliability of dMRI tissue characterization and strengthen the path toward clinical translation.

authors.name: Jinyang Yu, Oliver G\"odicke, Frederik B. Laun, Obada T. Alhalabi, Iris A. Kohler, J\"urgen Hesser, Sandro M. Krieg, Bogdana Suchorska, Heinz-Peter Schlemmer, Mark E. Ladd, David Bonekamp, Johann M. E. Jende, Tristan A. Kuder

papers.title: Absolute frequency measurement of the $^{40}$Ca$^{+}$ clock transition using a GNSS link to the SI second
papers.summary: We report the absolute frequency measurement of the $4s$ $ ^{2}S_{1/2}\leftrightarrow 3d$ $^{2}D_{5/2}$ $^{40}$Ca$^{+}$ clock transition with respect to the SI second. To perform this measurement, a link between our laboratory in Innsbruck and the clocks realizing the Coordinated Universal Time at the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) in Braunschweig was installed and characterized using the Global Navigation Satellite System GNSS. The comparison between our clock and the ones at PTB was done using the Precise Point Positioning technique. After the evaluation of the systematic shifts, the measured transition frequency is 411 042 129 776 400.4$\pm$0.6 Hz with a fractional uncertainty of 1.5 $\times$ 10$^{-15}$. The stability of the clock measurements was also corroborated by comparing two different calcium ion clock experiments, which share the clock laser source at our institute. Furthermore, after careful evaluation of the trap-drive induced ac magnetic fields, we estimate ac Zeeman shifts on the $D_{5/2}$ sublevels and reevaluate the Land\'e g-factor of the $3d$ $^{2}D_{5/2}$ level to be g$_{5/2}= 1.200329(1)$.

authors.name: M. Guevara-Bertsch, M. K. Joshi, M. I Hussain, R. Blatt, C. F. Roos

papers.title: Harnessing Machine Learning for Ultrafast Science in Facility Settings: Opportunities and Challenges
papers.summary: Ultrafast science is rapidly evolving from a collection of specialized laser experiments into a facility-scale, data-intensive research endeavour. High-repetition-rate femtosecond and attosecond sources, synchronized multidimensional diagnostics, and increasingly nonlinear laser-matter interactions now generate heterogeneous data streams whose volume, speed, and complexity often exceed the capacity of conventional manual workflows. This chapter examines how machine learning can become an enabling layer for next-generation ultrafast facilities, with emphasis on the Extreme Light Infrastructure (ELI) ecosystem. We discuss the scientific drivers for artificial-intelligence-assisted experimentation, propose a facility-scale digital architecture spanning acquisition, ingestion, storage, analytics, machine learning, adaptive feedback, and user interfaces, and review representative examples from ELI ALPS, ELI Beamlines, and ELI-NP. The central thesis is that machine learning should not be treated merely as an offline data-analysis tool; rather, when constrained by physical insight and embedded in robust data infrastructure, it can support real-time diagnostics, surrogate modeling, anomaly detection, experimental optimization, and progressively autonomous discovery workflows.

authors.name: Mousumi Upadhyay Kahaly, Ishraq Md Anjum, Davorin Peceli, Zsolt Diveki, Subhendu Kahaly

papers.title: Brilliance for adaptive computational research in accelerator physics
papers.summary: Computational research requires repeated decisions about models, calculations and the interpretation of results. We introduce Brilliance, an agent that combines large language models, reusable physics expertise and numerical simulation to construct and revise investigations in accelerator physics. Starting from a detailed expert-specified request, Brilliance develops an ideal storage-ring lattice meeting the specified emittance ceiling and sampled nonlinear-acceptance criteria after revising optics that fail particle-tracking tests. Further scientist-guided exploration produces a candidate with a natural emittance of 6.51 pm rad and millimeter-scale transverse acceptance, while exposing unresolved momentum-acceptance limitations. Using measured responses from the High Energy Photon Source, Brilliance also performs offline optics calibration consistent with an independent specialist analysis. An expert-module ablation examines how reusable domain knowledge influences research choices and outcomes. Here, we demonstrate a practical route to scientist-agent collaboration in sustained numerical research.

authors.name: Jinyu Wan, Yu Zhao, Wei Bao, Ying Li, Hao Zhong, Xiaohan Lu, Yi Jiao

papers.title: Unmasking Compensating Errors in Numerical Weather Models: A Process-Additive Neural Network Approach
papers.summary: This work introduces a Process Additive Neural Network (PANN) framework to disentangle compensating biases in atmospheric models, where errors in different physical processes can offset each other and obscure their origins. Using a single-column model, each PANN branch represents the tendency error associated with a separate physical process, and the summed branch outputs approximate the total error relative to a reference tendency. Once trained successfully, the branch outputs are expected to provide process-level error attributions and, when averaged, estimates of process-level bias. Initial experiments focus on cloud-related processes in OpenIFS SCM case studies, where cloud and convection tendencies are strongly coupled and compensation is difficult to diagnose using standard approaches. The aim is not to replace human interpretation of physical processes, but to extend it to regimes where model complexity, process interaction, and compensating errors make direct diagnosis difficult. By providing a physically structured form of machine-learning interpretability, PANN can help connect complex model behaviour with process-level explanations. This work supports both improved understanding of compensating errors and the development of more physically consistent weather and climate models.

authors.name: Yuiko Ichikawa, Edward Groot, Jack Atkinson

papers.title: A self-organizing mechanism for collective foraging: recruitment cascades couple Levy search to a clustered maximum-entropy resource field
papers.summary: Foraging recruitment is modeled as a contagion: an agent that finds a resource triggers a linear-threshold cascade on the group's communication network. Because activation is degree-normalized, crowding shuts the cascade off, so the swarm aggregates on a resource and then disperses to explore again. Acting on the cascade moves agents in space, and that motion rewires the network, so recruitment and exploration are one coupled process; removing this coupling alone abolishes the self-limitation. Recruitment spreads only within a connectivity window, bounded below by percolation onset and above by degree-blocking. The swarm self-organizes to the near-critical edge of this window -- self-organized quasi-criticality: recruitment sits near but below the critical point without settling onto a clean, size-invariant critical state, and the activity spectrum has a finite correlation time (Lorentzian-like, not 1/f), consistent with local rather than global criticality. Recruitment raises harvest up to 2.7x over solitary search on sparse, clustered resource fields and loses (down to 0.37x) on abundant or uniform ones; because resources generically aggregate, the favourable regime is the common one. The empirically motivated Levy search and the resource field it exploits are both least-committal: the search a maximum-caliber walk, and the field a maximum-entropy point process whose generic, aggregation-set sign is clustered (attractive). The search exponent that maximizes harvest tracks the field's fractal dimension (a heavier-tailed, more ballistic search for more strongly clustered fields). These are one coupled mechanism: heavy-tailed Levy exploration crosses the field's sparse voids while recruitment cascades exploit its clusters, so one maximum-entropy geometry binds exploration and recruitment into a single self-organizing cycle.

authors.name: Galen J. Wilkerson

papers.title: Instability of streaky high-supersonic boundary layers over cooled walls
papers.summary: We investigate the instability of streaks induced by free-stream vortical disturbances in cooled-wall high-supersonic boundary layers. Distinct types of instability modes are identified: modified Mack second modes, a newly discovered varicose secondary-instability mode and sinuous or varicose secondary-instability modes akin to those in incompressible boundary layers. Unique characteristics of the new secondary-instability mode are that its eigenfunctions concentrate in valley regions and feature intense temperature fluctuations near the wall. The streaks in high-supersonic boundary layers destabilise the three-dimensional secondary-instability modes, but suppress the growth of the modified Mack second modes, both radiating and non-radiating. The suppression of radiating modes amounts to a reduction of the two-dimensional noise they emit. Numerical results indicate that, unlike streaks in adiabatic-wall boundary layers, whose instability concentrates in low-speed peak regions away from the wall, the secondary instability of streaks in cooled-wall high-supersonic boundary layers occurs both in low-speed peak regions and in high-speed valley regions.

authors.name: Dongdong Xu, Pierre Ricco, Elena Marensi, Xuesong Wu

papers.title: Hard X-ray/Soft gamma-ray Laue Lenses for High Energy Astrophysics
papers.summary: The study of the celestial phenomena in the hard X-ray/soft gamma-ray band(20 keV--1 MeV) is very intriguing but also very difficult to be performed with the needed sensitivity. In this review I will discuss the astrophysical importance of the soft gamma-ray astronomy, its difficulties to solve its issues with the current instrumentation, and a possible solution achievable using focusing Laue lens. Concerning these instruments, I will discuss their functioning principle, how to achieve a high reflection efficiency, their imaging properties, the current feasibility studies, the technological developments and observation prospects.

authors.name: Filippo Frontera

papers.title: Finite-size scaling theory of R\'enyi thermal entropy for second-order, first-order, and weakly first-order quantum phase transitions
papers.summary: Establishing the nature of a quantum phase transition in finite-size simulations---whether continuous, first-order, or weakly first-order---is a fundamental challenge in quantum many-body computation. The weakly first-order transition is particularly elusive: its anomalously large correlation length invariably mimics a continuous critical point at accessible system sizes, and no unified finite-size scaling theory has existed to distinguish these scenarios under realistic computational constraints. In this work, we address this problem by introducing a finite-size scaling framework based on the R\'enyi thermal entropy (RTE) and its derivative (DRTE). We derive the finite-size scaling forms for the RTE and DRTE at continuous, first-order, and weakly first-order quantum phase transitions, and show that the DRTE isolates the universal contribution of the free energy and strengthens the characteristics of various phase transitions in finite sizes. Using quantum Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate accurate data collapse and extraction of critical exponents at (2+1)-dimensional O($N$) critical points. Most importantly, the DRTE provides a definitive signature of weakly first-order transitions at visitable sizes---a zero-crossing and a double-peak structure---which we observe in the debated deconfined quantum criticality candidates such as the $J$--$Q$ and SU(8) $J_1$--$J_2$ models. Our approach offers a general, order-parameter-agnostic, and numerically efficient diagnostic tool, resolving long-standing ambiguities between continuous and weakly first-order scenarios in the finite size simulations.

authors.name: Zhe Wang, Yanzhang Zhu, Chunhao Guo, Bin-Bin Chen, Yi-Ming Ding, Zenan Liu, Zheng Yan

papers.title: Chromatic Calorimetry -- A Novel Approach to Validate Energy Resolution and Particle Discrimination
papers.summary: Chromatic calorimetry (CCAL) analyses particle detection by utilizing scintillators with distinct emission wavelengths to measure the longitudinal energy deposition of particle showers in high-energy physics, improving particle identification (PID) and energy resolution. By stacking scintillators in order of decreasing emission wavelength, CCAL enables layer-specific energy measurements, analyzed via amplitude fractions ($f_i = A_i / \sum_j A_j$) and center of gravity ($\langle z_{\text{cog}} \rangle = \sum_i z_i E_i / \sum_i E_i$). This thesis presents results from two CERN Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS) experiments conducted in 2023 and 2024, complemented by GEANT4 simulations of a quantum dot (QD)-based CCAL design, to validate its potential for future colliders such as the Future Circular Collider (FCC).

authors.name: Devanshi Arora

papers.title: CNN on `Top': In Search of Scalable & Lightweight Image-based Jet Taggers
papers.summary: While Transformer-based and standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be the best performers in classifying different types of jets, they require substantial computational power. We explore the scope of using a lightweight and scalable version of EfficientNet architecture, along with global features of the jet. The end product is computationally inexpensive but is capable of competitive performance. We showcase the efficacy of our network in tagging top-quark jets in a sea of other light quark and gluon jets. The work also sheds light on the importance of global features for both the accuracy and the apparent redundancy of the network's complexity.

authors.name: Rajneil Baruah, Subhadeep Mondal, Sunando Kumar Patra, Satyajit Roy

papers.title: Tree tensor network states represent low-energy states faithfully
papers.summary: Extending corresponding results for matrix product states [Verstraete and Cirac, PRB 73, 094423 (2006); Schuch et al. PRL 100, 030504 (2008)], it is shown how the approximation error of tree tensor network states (TTNS) can be bounded using Schmidt spectra or R\'{e}nyi entanglement entropies of the target quantum state. Conversely, one obtains bounds on TTNS bond dimensions needed to achieve a specific approximation accuracy. The result implies that efficient TTNS approximations exist if $\alpha<1$ R\'{e}nyi entanglement entropies for single-branch cuts obey an area law, as in ground and low-energy states of certain gapped systems on tree graphs.

authors.name: Thomas Barthel

papers.title: Stability and mixed phases of three-component droplets in one dimension
papers.summary: We explore the ground state properties and excitation spectra of one-dimensional, three-component bosonic mixtures, where two majority components form a self-bound droplet coupled to a third, minority component. Within a self-consistent Lee-Huang-Yang framework, we identify distinct mixed self-bound droplet phases and characterize their phase transitions through variations of either the particle number of the majority components or the intercomponent coupling. The ensuing phases demonstrate that the minority component is untrapped, partially trapped, or fully trapped by the majority droplet species. These states are characterized by their binding energies captured by the chemical potentials and their low-amplitude excitation spectrum, including mode crossings at the particle-emission threshold. We further derive effective reduced models in the high-imbalance limit, which accurately reproduce the numerically computed ground states, while providing analytical insights into the role of quantum fluctuations. Our results establish the stability and structure of mixed droplet phases provide experimentally relevant signatures for their identification.

authors.name: I. A. Englezos, E. G. Charalampidis, P. Schmelcher, S. I. Mistakidis

papers.title: Cost scaling of MPS and TTNS simulations for 2D and 3D systems with area-law entanglement
papers.summary: Tensor network states are an indispensable tool for the simulation of strongly correlated quantum many-body systems. In recent years, tree tensor network states (TTNS) have been successfully used for two-dimensional systems and to benchmark quantum simulation approaches for condensed matter, nuclear, and particle physics. In comparison to the more traditional approach based on matrix product states (MPS), the graph distance of physical degrees of freedom can be drastically reduced in TTNS. Surprisingly, it turns out that, for large systems in $D>1$ spatial dimensions, MPS simulations of low-energy states are nevertheless more efficient than TTNS simulations. With a focus on $D=2$ and 3, the scaling of computational costs for different boundary conditions is determined under the assumption that the system obeys an entanglement (log-)area law, implying that bond dimensions scale exponentially in the interface area of the associated subsystems.

authors.name: Thomas Barthel

papers.title: Bidirectional teleportation using scrambling dynamics: a practical protocol
papers.summary: We show that quantum information scrambling can enable a generic SWAP gate between collective degrees of freedom in systems without universal local control. Our protocol combines a Hayden-Preskill type recovery scheme, associated with the black hole information paradox, with quantum teleportation and runs them in parallel and in opposite directions, enabling bidirectional exchange of quantum states through global interactions alone. This approach cleanly distinguishes the roles of information spreading, entanglement, and chaos for enabling both coherent state transfer and recovery. We propose an experimental realization using the Dicke model, which can be realized in optical cavity and trapped-ion platforms, highlighting the utility of holography in designing practical quantum gates.

authors.name: Amit Vikram, Edwin Chaparro, Muhammad Miskeen Khan, Andrew Lucas, Chris Akers, Ana Maria Rey

papers.title: Density Modulations of Zero Sound
papers.summary: We study the density modulation of an interacting Fermi gas caused by the uniform motion of an impurity at zero temperature. For strong enough interaction among Fermi atoms, the modulation propagates thanks to the excitation of the collective zero sound mode if the impurity speed is above the zero sound threshold. We are able to assess, via a semi-analytic evaluation, the extent of the zero sound contribution to the density oscillation over and above the incoherent background of particle-hole excitations. Given the strong dependence of the results on the features of the gas interaction potential, we also analyze how they vary depending on its strength, range and shape.

authors.name: Leonardo Pisani

papers.title: Clustering without geometry in sparse networks with independent edges
papers.summary: The coexistence of sparsity and clustering (non-vanishing average fraction of triangles per node) is one of the few structural features that, irrespective of finer details, are ubiquitously observed across large real-world networks. This fact calls for generic models producing sparse clustered graphs. Earlier results suggested that sparse random graphs with independent edges fail to reproduce clustering, unless edge probabilities are assumed to depend on underlying metric distances that, thanks to the triangle inequality, naturally favour triadic closure. This observation has opened a debate on whether clustering implies (latent) geometry in real-world networks. Alternatively, recent models of higher-order networks can replicate clustering by abandoning edge independence. In this paper, we mathematically prove, and numerically confirm, that a sparse random graph with independent edges, recently identified in the context of network renormalization as an invariant model under node aggregation, produces finite clustering without any geometric or higher-order constraint. The underlying mechanism is an infinite-mean node fitness, which also implies a power-law degree distribution. Further, as a novel phenomenon that we characterize rigorously, we observe the breakdown of self-averaging of various network properties. Therefore, as an alternative to geometry or higher-order dependencies, node aggregation invariance emerges as a basic route to realistic network properties.

authors.name: Alessio Catanzaro, Remco van der Hofstad, Diego Garlaschelli

papers.title: Unified Theory of Spin and Orbital Inverse Faraday Effects in Rashba Metals
papers.summary: The inverse Faraday effect (IFE) offers a promising route toward optical control of magnetic moments in quantum materials. Yet experiments on spin-orbit-coupled metals indicate that no single microscopic mechanism suffices, implicating orbital currents alongside spin polarization. We derive both responses in a disordered Rashba metal using quantum kinetics and diagrammatics with impurity-renormalized optical vertices, providing the first unified diagrammatic derivation of spin and orbital IFE. Treating impurity scattering consistently, our number-conserving kinetic formulation restores full phase-space derivatives and the optical magnetic field neglected in earlier treatments. We connect nonlinear orbital magnetization to absorptive linear optical conductivity, revealing that the magnetic Lorentz force supplies half the orbital response. Our unified treatment resolves both channels across the Rashba resonance: spin IFE changes sign as frequency increases, while the orbital IFE dominates, keeping the direction of the total magnetization unchanged.

authors.name: Jaglul Hasan, Maxim Dzero, Chandan Setty

papers.title: Scalable Generative Sampling and Multilevel Estimation for Lattice Field Theories Near Criticality
papers.summary: Sampling lattice field theories near criticality is severely hindered by critical slowing down, which makes standard Markov chain methods increasingly inefficient at large lattice volumes. We introduce a multiscale generative sampler, inspired by renormalization-group ideas, that models the Boltzmann distribution through a coarse-to-fine hierarchy across length scales. At each level, a conditional Gaussian mixture model captures the main local dependence of newly introduced variables on the already-sampled coarse field, while a masked continuous normalizing flow refines the remaining conditional structure. Coarse levels encode the dominant long-wavelength modes, and finer levels progressively add short-distance fluctuations. In addition, because the architecture preserves coarse fields exactly during refinement, it provides exact restriction maps at no additional computational cost and directly enables asymptotically unbiased Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) variance reduction. For the two-dimensional scalar $\phi^4$ theory near criticality, the method achieves integrated autocorrelation times orders of magnitude smaller than Hybrid Monte Carlo (HMC) on large volumes, maintains high importance-sampling efficiency relative to other generative baselines, and reproduces asymptotically unbiased physical observables in statistical agreement with long HMC simulations.

authors.name: Ankur Singha, Jacob Kauffmann, Elia Cellini, Karl Jansen, Shinichi Nakajima

papers.title: Spin State versus Potential of Zero Charge as Predictors of Density-Dependent Oxygen Reduction in M-N-C Electrocatalysts
papers.summary: Metal-site density strongly influences oxygen reduction activity and selectivity in M-N-C electrocatalysts, but the descriptors that predict these trends remain under debate. Here, we compare spin state and the potential of zero charge (PZC) as predictors of density-dependent oxygen reduction behavior in Fe-N-C and Co-N-C catalysts. Using constrained-magnetization calculations combined with Landau analysis, we find that the ground-state magnetic moments vary only weakly across a broad range of metal-site densities, suggesting that magnetic descriptors alone cannot account for the pronounced performance changes. In contrast, explicit-solvent simulations reveal systematic density-dependent shifts in PZC, which alter the interfacial electric field and thereby modulate field-sensitive adsorption energetics of ORR intermediates. Incorporating these PZC shifts into a pH-field-coupled microkinetic model captures the density-dependent activity trends and reproduces the experimentally observed increase in two-electron selectivity at lower site densities under acidic conditions. Experimental PZC measurements further support the predicted trend. Within the investigated Co-N-C and Fe-N-C series, PZC-dependent electrostatics consistently rationalize the density-dependent ORR trends, whereas the examined magnetic descriptors show comparatively weak variation.

authors.name: Di Zhang, Zixun Yu, Fangzhou Liu, Yumeng Li, Jiaxiang Chen, Xun Geng, Yuan Chen, Li Wei, Hao Li

papers.title: Squeezing Enhancement Through Resonant Interference in Multi-ring Resonators
papers.summary: We develop a non-perturbative description of squeezed light generation in an arbitrary lossy structure consisting of multiple coupled microring resonators. This is applied to two ring photonic molecules where the interference of the fields in the coupled rings leads to a modification in the resonance spectrum near a shared resonance. Considering a dual-pump degenerate squeezing scheme under a five resonance approximation, we investigate two methods to suppress parasitic four-wave mixing contributions and compensate for group velocity dispersion within a primary resonator through hybridization effects with a second auxiliary resonator. In the former case, this comes from an effective splitting of the unwanted resonances supporting parasitic four-wave mixing interactions that add thermal noise to the desired degenerate squeezed state. For sufficiently strong coupling between the resonators, we demonstrate near complete suppression of such parasitic processes, resulting in near unit fidelities with the corresponding output state that would arise were the parasitic interactions neglected. In the latter case, the hybridization effectively shifts a pump resonance, realigning the desired dual-pump four-wave mixing process and leading to a significant enhancement of the signal generation and output squeezing.

authors.name: M. Sloan, J. E. Sipe

papers.title: Metamaterial tactile displays with programmable virtual pixels
papers.summary: Tactile displays present information by supplying localized mechanical signals across their surface, but conventional approaches often require an actuator to be positioned at every location where feedback is provided, limiting resolution and increasing complexity. Wave-mediated tactile displays exploit wave transmission to generate virtual pixels using far fewer actuators, but are constrained in resolution by the intrinsic dispersion characteristics of the display medium. Here, we show how this constraint can be overcome by applying metamaterial physics to engineer wave transmission in a rigid plate using an optimized lattice of resonators. The resulting system exhibits a slow-wave dispersion branch that reduces the wavelengths available for constructing virtual pixels, thereby enhancing display resolution by an order of magnitude. We demonstrate a metamaterial tactile display driven by eight peripheral actuators that is capable of generating localized virtual tactile pixels at any surface location with centimeter-scale resolution. The location, timing, and waveform of each pixel can be specified computationally, and the output bandwidth, 75-400 Hz, spans a substantial portion of the tactile frequency range. In four perceptual experiments, participants localized, explored, and discriminated multi-pixel patterns comprising transient and sustained vibrations with accuracies ranging from 95.3% to 100%. This research provides metamaterial engineering methods that enable the design of tactile displays driven by few actuated degrees of freedom, with implications for many future application areas.

authors.name: Gregory Reardon, Max Linnander, Dustin Goetz, Neeli Tummala, Yon Visell

papers.title: Machine-learned particle flow as a foundation model for collider physics
papers.summary: The workflow from particle collision to physics analysis passes through a series of reconstruction steps that are traditionally modular and disconnected, with no shared representation linking low-level detector data to high-level analysis tasks. We show that casting event reconstruction as a machine learning problem naturally produces such a shared representation. We repurpose a machine learning model trained for particle-flow reconstruction (MLPF) to perform three distinct analysis tasks: jet flavor identification, jet energy regression, and missing momentum regression. By appending the per-particle latent representations learned during reconstruction as additional input features, we substantially improve over baselines that use conventional particle-level features alone. We further demonstrate that a single linear layer trained using only the latent representations achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art baseline architectures, and outperforms the baseline for missing momentum regression with approximately 35 times fewer parameters. These results demonstrate that the latent representations learned during reconstruction encode essential physics information needed for downstream analysis, establishing MLPF as a foundation model and offering a concrete step toward an end-to-end pipeline from detector data to physics analysis.

authors.name: Farouk Mokhtar, Joosep Pata, Michael Kagan, Javier Duarte

papers.title: Stable Ballistic Prograde Cyclers in the Three-Body Problem
papers.summary: We report the first continuous families of stable, ballistic, prograde cycler orbits in the circular restricted three-body problem: periodic trajectories that alternately undergo temporary capture and orbit each primary. We construct continuous families of symmetric cyclers from intersections of the stable and unstable manifold tubes of the $L_1$ Lyapunov orbit and exhibit stable examples across more than two orders of magnitude in mass ratio, from the Sun-Jupiter regime to the equal-mass limit. Linear stability separates naturally into planar and out-of-plane components. A planar-stable branch of every computed family is created simultaneously with a hyperbolic branch in a saddle-center bifurcation of the return map at the family's maximal Jacobi constant, while out-of-plane instability occurs only through isolated parametric resonances. Every computed family contains a subfamily that is linearly stable to both planar and out-of-plane perturbations. These stable cyclers persist into the full three-body problem for sufficiently small third mass. We conjecture that saddle-center birth is universal among cycler families, suggesting that stable cyclers are a generic feature of three-body dynamics.

authors.name: Shane D. Ross, Michael Roberts-Tsoukkas

papers.title: Attosecond delay metrology beyond the photon coherence time with spectrally resolved Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometry
papers.summary: Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometry enables delay estimation at the quantum precision limit but is traditionally constrained to path differences within the coherence time of the interfering photons. Here, we demonstrate single-shot path-delay sensing using spectrally resolved HOM interference, achieving a precision near the measurement Cram\'er-Rao bound over an operating range of approximately $\pm$300 um, removing the conventional dynamic-range limitation imposed by the photon coherence window. By extracting delay information from the spectral interference fringes of spectrally entangled photon pairs, we retain near-optimal sensitivity over an operational range exceeding the photon coherence time by over two orders of magnitude. Using one million detected photon pairs, we achieve a time-delay precision of 13 attosecond (4 nm), while real-time operation (at 1 Hz) with 2000 detected photons yields 330 attosecond (100 nm) precision. Because the estimator relies on fringe periodicity rather than absolute coincidence rates, the method is intrinsically robust to variations in interference visibility, eliminating the need for recalibration. As a practical demonstration, we measure the thickness of a nominally 300 um transmissive target with nanometer-scale precision. These results mark a significant step towards deploying quantum-enhanced HOM interferometry for high-precision displacement sensing in real-world applications.

authors.name: Yingwen Zhang, Kyle Jordan, Duncan England, Vincenzo Tamma, Ebrahim Karimi, Benjamin Sussman

papers.title: Butterfly Effects in Turbulence: A Unified View through the Finite Size Lyapunov Exponent
papers.summary: The ``butterfly effect'', introduced over half a century ago by Edward Lorenz, has shifted from a cornerstone of dynamical systems to a popular metaphor, yet its true physical manifestation in fully developed turbulence spans a spectrum of phenomena from standard sensitivity on initial conditions to the recently established concept of Eulerian spontaneous stochasticity. Here, we propose an attempt at a systematic synthesis that brings these different but interconnected ideas together within the unifying framework of the Finite Size Lyapunov Exponent (FSLE). The FSLE describes the growth rate of perturbations as a function of their scale, enabling a comprehensive characterization of the multiscale physics of turbulent flows. Using the FSLE and the Sabra shell model, extended to include thermal noise, we bridge the classical, small-scale Lyapunov regime with predictability at large scales and its interpretation in terms of Eulerian spontaneous stochasticity. Moreover, using the FSLE and the Kraichnan model, we also illustrate the closely related phenomenon of Lagrangian spontaneous stochasticity. To complete the spectrum of butterfly effects, we also examine the ``literal butterfly'' scenario of localized, sub-dissipative perturbations.

authors.name: Victor de Jesus Valad\~ao, Erik Aurell, Guido Boffetta, Massimo Cencini, Stefano Musacchio, Angelo Vulpiani

papers.title: Quantum Magnonics: Quantum States Generation and Applications
papers.summary: Hybrid systems based on magnons in ferromagnetic materials, such as yttrium iron garnet, have achieved remarkable development in the last decade. These include the coupling of magnons to microwave and optical photons, superconducting qubits, phonons, spins, the center-of-mass motion of a ferromagnet, etc. Here, we review both the experimental and theoretical progress in this field, focusing on the generation of magnonic quantum states and their applications in a broad range of fields. Since the strong coupling is a prerequisite for achieving coherent quantum control of magnons and preparing magnonic quantum states, we start by introducing representative strong-coupling experiments in cavity magnonics, then review a series of protocols for creating various magnonic quantum states, such as Fock, cat, squeezed, and entangled states, and discuss their potential applications in macroscopic quantum studies, quantum information science, quantum sensing, magnonic quantum devices, dark matter detection, and so on. Finally, we summarize the review and give an outlook for the future study of quantum magnonics.

authors.name: Zi-Xu Lu, Xuan Zuo, Xin-Lei Hei, Gang Liu, Zeng-Xing Liu, Qi Guo, Peng-Bo Li, Jie Li

papers.title: Machine-Learning-Accelerated Metallene Stabilization from High-Throughput Sandwich Modeling
papers.summary: Metallenes have appealing properties, but stabilizing them in a monolayer phase poses synthesis challenges. A recent experiment showed that the van der Waals squeezing method can stabilize certain metallenes in a MoS2 sandwich. This pioneering work motivates systematic studies, but such studies are experimentally impractical, while first-principles modeling remains prohibitive. Here, using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we constructed 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures containing 6 different sandwich layers and 45 metals. We performed phonon calculations, which revealed 1208 dynamically stable structures and narrowed them to 331 after structural filtering. We found that Se-based transition-metal dichalcogenides stabilize metallenes effectively. Specifically, hexagonal and buckled hexagonal crystal lattices exhibit the greatest stability. We further evaluated the thermal stability of selected heterostructures with density-functional theory molecular dynamics simulations at room temperature. By uncovering the physical and chemical factors that govern metallenes stabilization, our results provide systematic insights to guide and accelerate synthesis for future applications.

authors.name: Mohammad Bagheri, Pekka Koskinen

papers.title: Multimode Angle-Compensated Interferometer with Long Time-Bin Delay Using a Multi-Pass Herriott Cell
papers.summary: Interference of optical signals in free-space channels requires optical receivers to support many spatial modes due to atmospheric turbulence, typically necessitating adaptive optics systems. Angle-compensated interferometers offer a passive alternative, making them particularly attractive for time-bin encoded signals with delays on the order of one nanosecond. Here, we demonstrate a multimode angle-compensated interferometer design that achieves a high interference visibility for spatially multimode beams with large time bin separations. The interference of the multimode beams is enabled using an imaging multi-pass Herriott cell that enables a very long path separation with a small form-factor. The design is tested using both numerical ray-tracing simulations and proof-of-principle demonstrations. We create a prototype interferometer with a path length difference of 12ns and determine that it maintains a high interference visibility with a large field-of-view of $0.4^{\circ}$.

authors.name: Ramy Tannous, St\'ephane Vinet, Kaylee Sherk, Kimia Mohammadi, Thomas Jennewein

papers.title: Moment-based formulas for the transport coefficients
papers.summary: The coefficients of the transport equations, describing the propagation features, are particularly important in astrophysics, interplanetary physics, and experimental plasma physics. In this paper, the variable-dependent diffusion coefficients are investigated. For the momentum transport equations, we find that the coefficients are related to statistical quantities, some of which are new. In addition, these coefficients take logarithmic forms, which are different from the results derived in previous papers. For isotropic pitch-angle scattering, we also obtain a formula that takes a logarithmic form. For fractional transport equations, the coefficients expressed in terms of the moments are obtained from the governing equations.

authors.name: J. -F. Wang, G. Qin

papers.title: Multi-Threshold Sampling: Signal Space, Sampling Operators, and First Recorded Crossing-Time Distributions
papers.summary: Multi-threshold (MT) sampling records crossing times for parameter estimation and waveform reconstruction. We develop signal and observation spaces and stochastic crossing, timing, and selection operators with associated Markov kernels. Finite point measures accommodate variable crossing counts and preserve multiplicity after quantization. For nonhomogeneous Poisson photon arrivals with shared threshold noise, shared timing jitter before quantization, and identity selection, we derive exact first recorded crossing-time distributions. A Poisson series covers general admissible paths with a time-uniform truncation bound. For continuous paths, interval extrema give the exact cumulative distribution function (CDF) and a Fourier representation with contact corrections. A biexponential arrival-intensity and response model admits a two-dimensional first-crossing integral equation on arbitrary finite observation windows, with a unique bounded measurable solution and a Poisson-tail approximation bound. For continuous causal responses with finitely many analytic pieces and bounded first and second branch derivatives, we prove a conditional standard-deviation (SD) limit at first mean crossings with positive slope under relative threshold-noise and fine timing scales. For the biexponential model, its coefficient increases strictly on a parameter-uniform interval and, under a shape condition, up to the first mean peak. Scintillation experiments compare the calculated CDF and conditional SDs with independent waveform simulations on a window extending beyond the single-photon response peak.

authors.name: Ao Qiu, Qingguo Xie

papers.title: A Critical Value for the Viscosity Coefficient: Triggering Oscillatory Traveling Waves in the Pseudo-parabolic Fisher-KPP Equation
papers.summary: The pseudo-parabolic term $u_{xxt}$ serves as a canonical example of higher-order viscosity that provides effective regularization while capturing the refined physical mechanism. How it alters the dynamics of prototype equations remains a fundamental issue, which is not yet fully understood. The goal of this paper is to show that this term induces a sharp transition in traveling wave structure, via studying the pseudo-parabolic Fisher-KPP equation $$ u_t - \tau u_{xxt} = D u_{xx} + u(1-u). $$ We completely characterize how the parameter ratio $\tau/D$ acts as a critical switch: it preserves the monotonic structure of classical traveling waves when $\tau/D \leq 1$, yet it triggers a qualitative shift to oscillatory traveling waves when $\tau/D > 1$. Numerical simulations support these findings. The threshold $\tau/D=1$ thus captures the dual role of the pseudo-parabolic term: it acts as a structure-preserving viscosity when small, but when large it reflects dominant capillary hysteresis, generating the oscillations that explain the saturation overshoot, a phenomenon that contradicts classical diffusion models yet is widely observed in two-phase flow.

authors.name: Yang Cao (Dalian University of Technology, Dalian, China), Haomeng Chen (Dalian University of Technology, Dalian, China), Chunhua Jin (South China Normal University, Guangzhou, China), Jingxue Yin (South China Normal University, Guangzhou, China)

papers.title: Negative quasiprobabilities redistribute (and complex ones reduce) the information in unabsorbed photons
papers.summary: Negative Kirkwood--Dirac quasiprobabilities are credited with the quantum advantage of interaction-free measurement and postselected metrology. We test that claim on the task interaction-free measurement was designed for: learning about a sample while it absorbs as little light as possible. The quasiprobability distribution of path and output gives the linear response to a weak sample: its real part responds to absorption, its imaginary part to a phase. For a pure single photon passing once through any interferometer, the Fisher information about transmittance per absorbed photon is the direct-transmission value minus a sum of squared imaginary parts: no interferometer or readout beats direct transmission. Negativity only concentrates information in weakly lit outputs. These imaginary parts depend on the output basis, not the sample, so an optimal basis with all terms real always exists. A single photon beats direct transmission only through a phase response, which for an optical line needs a thick or inhomogeneously broadened sample, or through many passes when absorptions go uncounted, as a critically coupled resonator shows. For detecting a weak absorber, negativity gives a single-shot advantage that does not accumulate over repeated trials. The advantage that accumulates comes from outputs dark without the object, and needs no negativity.

authors.name: Jonte R. Hance

papers.title: Optimal linear-optical interferometers for unitary t-designs in a multi-photon Fock space
papers.summary: We investigate the construction of unitary \(1\)-designs and two-photon designs on programmable linear-optical interferometers. Using the frame-potential loss as the optimization objective, we identify architectures that reproduce the relevant Haar moments with considerably fewer programmable phase shifters than required for universal linear optics. For unitary \(1\)-designs, we provide an exact construction and prove that the minimum number of programmable phase shifters within the considered layered architecture is \(2(d-1)\), where \(d\) is the number of optical modes. Numerical optimization confirms this parameter count over the tested range of dimensions. For two-photon designs, defined by first-moment matching in the symmetric two-photon representation of \(U(d)\), we numerically investigate the resources required to achieve prescribed approximation thresholds. We benchmark the resulting ensembles using single- and two-photon transition probabilities and average channel fidelities. Furthermore, we develop a protocol for estimating the total photon number of a multiphoton Fock state using a single monitored output mode and derive the corresponding Haar-averaged photon-count moments. Our findings demonstrate that shallow interferometers can reproduce Haar-averaged observables with reduced hardware resources, while photon-number fluctuations provide a more stringent test of approximate two-photon designs.

authors.name: Robert A. Grinshtein, Ivan V. Dyakonov, Stanislav S. Straupe

papers.title: Maximum-Temperature Theorem for Nanothermometry
papers.summary: We derive a sharp upper bound on the quasi-steady temperature rise of a sensor of arbitrary shape and known thermometric volume $V_\mathrm{s}$, placed anywhere inside a region enclosed by an isothermal reference surface. The bound also requires the maximum net heat power $\dot Q_{\scriptscriptstyle \mathcal S \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}^{\max}$ crossing any closed surface within the region and a lower bound on its thermal conductivity $\kappa_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}}$. It is otherwise independent of the heat-source distribution, domain shape, and source-ensor distance. For $\dot Q_{\scriptscriptstyle \mathcal S \subseteq \mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}^{\max}=50~\mathrm{pW}$, $\kappa_{\scriptscriptstyle{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm r}}} =0.1~\mathrm{W\,m^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $V_{\mathrm s}$ equal to the volume of a $60~\mathrm{nm}$-diameter sphere, the theorem permits a maximum temperature rise of approximately $2~\mathrm{mK}$. Neither source localization nor uncertain source--sensor separation can therefore account for reported kelvin-scale intracellular readings under steady-state heat conduction. The result applies to sensors based on nanodiamonds, upconversion nanoparticles, fluorescent polymer beads, and core-shell quantum dots.

authors.name: Taras Plakhotnik

papers.title: Pump-scheme dependence of few-emitter lasers: exact multilevel correlations and photon statistics
papers.summary: Few-emitter laser models usually replace the excitation cycle of the gain medium by a single Markovian pump jump of a two-level emitter. We test this replacement with the cavity and laser-transition parameters held fixed and the two-level pump rate fitted to the same mean photon number, using an exact damping-basis continued-fraction solution of the cavity--emitter master equation for $N$ identical $d$-level emitters with arbitrary independent incoherent transitions and one cavity-coupled transition, in the known reduced space of level populations and lasing coherences. First, a pump-quantum filtration shows that the inter-emitter coherence of $\Lambda$ and ladder media starts at second rather than first order in the pump; we evaluate its leading coefficient from the exact finite-system series and map the recycling rate at which its sign changes. Second, at matched photon number, rate-limited steps in the pump cycle push the long-time output-counting Fano factor of two and three emitters well below one: for two emitters it reaches 0.66 at a mean cavity occupation of 0.3 and is still 0.74 at an occupation of one, where $g^{(2)}(0)$ is within 3% of unity, because the anticorrelation sits at delays of about half a cavity lifetime rather than at zero delay. For two and three emitters the fitted two-level model gets both statistics wrong and places the output above the shot-noise level. Against independent single-emitter lasers at the same output, the common cavity erodes rather than enhances this single-emitter effect.

authors.name: Stephan Hartmann

papers.title: Restrained Diffusion Bridges: Targeted Denoiser Training and Refinement
papers.summary: Diffusion models are often inaccurate in critical, data-sparse regions of the target distribution. Sampling from restrained distributions, biased distributions used in classical enhanced sampling to concentrate data near chosen configurations, can control where training data are collected but biases the learned distribution. We establish that this bias cancels exactly when forward noising from restrained data is conditioned on the restrained configuration at an appropriately chosen intermediate time. This allows a pretrained model fine-tuned on restrained data to achieve high accuracy in any chosen region of the target distribution, regardless of its probability, using standard denoising or flow matching objectives without importance weights. When no target data are available, Gibbs sampling enables inference from a model trained exclusively on restrained data.

authors.name: Xuanxi Zhang, Kevin S. Cheng, Weizhou Wang, Aaron R. Dinner, Jonathan Weare

papers.title: Exact thermal correlators at vanishing momenta and the black hole singularity
papers.summary: We study thermal two- and three-point functions of scalar primaries in holographic CFTs dual to AdS black branes. The three-point function arises from a cubic scalar interaction in the bulk. At vanishing external momenta, the tree-level results can be written in closed form and are exact in the operator dimensions. We reproduce them through direct CFT calculations in two dimensions. Their large-dimension expansions contain subleading exponential terms encoding the radial proper time from the horizon to the black hole singularity. These results provide an exact test of earlier WKB and saddle-point predictions for higher-point thermal correlators, confirming the proper-time signature while correcting the predicted asymptotic form.

authors.name: Kaustubh Singhi

papers.title: Satisfying Freed--Witten quantization on smooth divisors in Calabi--Yau orientifolds
papers.summary: Freed--Witten quantization conditions on several divisors wrapped by D-branes must be satisfied with one bulk $B$-field. On a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold $X$ with a holomorphic O3/O7 involution $\sigma$, we show that the common background $B_{2,+}^{\star}=\tfrac12[R]$, where $R$ is the total O7 divisor, permits Freed--Witten period quantization on the full two-cycle lattice of \emph{every smooth connected divisor}, modulo torsion. The worldvolume fluxes are chosen individually and obey the orientifold relation between each divisor and its image. The central step concerns setwise invariant divisors $D$: we prove that the bulk Freed--Witten class $\eta_D^\star=\tfrac12([R]+[D])|_D$ has integer periods on every $\sigma$-even integral two-cycle class, including inherited and autochthonous classes. Its periods on purely $\sigma$-odd classes vanish, so any remaining non-integer periods occur only on classes that are neither $\sigma$-even nor $\sigma$-odd. We show how to choose $\sigma$-odd worldvolume fluxes on these invariant divisors that make all periods integral. For exchanged divisor pairs, quantizing the flux on one member automatically quantizes its orientifold image. On invariant divisors with $h^{2,0}_-(D)=0$, the constructed flux is of type $(1,1)$ and admits a primitive representative; this includes every smooth rigid invariant divisor. We also study zero worldvolume flux on invariant divisors. For $h^{1,1}_-(X)\leq1$, we construct common bulk backgrounds satisfying every inherited intersection period on all such divisors. A binary compatibility test determines whether a common shift exists for larger $h^{1,1}_-(X)$. Non-inherited period tests then determine whether the resulting backgrounds allow zero flux on the full worldvolume lattices.

authors.name: Mudit Jain

papers.title: Goldstone theory of gluon saturation in high energy QCD: From color glass to color superfluid condensate
papers.summary: In the high energy Regge asymptotics of QCD, the rapid overpopulation of gluons leads to gluon saturation, characterized by nonperturbative semi-classical lumpy configurations of size $1/Q_S$, where $Q_S\gg \Lambda_{\rm QCD}$ is a dynamical semi-hard saturation scale. We discuss here a generalization of the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework describing this phenomenon that is obtained by carefully treating the breaking of global symmetries by the condensate. In particular, we show that the breaking of a global subgroup of color results in a Goldstone effective field theory (EFT) whose dynamics is characterized by a Goldstone decay constant $f_G = \sqrt{N} Q_S$, where $N=O(1/\alpha_S)$ is the phase space occupancy of the condensate, which is large for $\alpha_S(Q_S)\ll 1$. Further, the coupling of these colored Goldstones to collinear gluon modes leads to a depletion of the condensate, thereby modifying the static shockwave scattering framework of the CGC on timescales controlled by $f_G$. The CGC EFT on these longer time scales is a novel color superfluid. Low frequency modes with $\omega\leq \alpha_S Q_S$ in an external probe of the CGC are sensitive to superfluid dynamics, with interesting physical consequences for deeply inelastic scattering and ultrarelativistic nuclear collisions.

authors.name: V. P. Nair, Raju Venugopalan

papers.title: Schwinger Effect with a Transversal Boundary
papers.summary: We study the effect of a boundary on pair production by an electric field. In particular, we are interested in the case in which the electric field has a normal component with respect to the boundary. This is essentially more complex than pure tangential fields due to the reflection of created particles against the boundary. In this article we provide the explicit solution for the case of an instantaneous electric pulse which is spatially uniform and normal to a flat surface. We show that pair production exhibits a bulk contribution that accounts for the interference of reflected modes, in addition to a purely boundary term. To conclude, we give an expression for the total particle production due to an irrotational electric pulse in a region delimited by an arbitrary boundary.

authors.name: Santiago Christiansen Murguizur, Daniela D'Ascanio, Pablo Pisani, Ulises Wainstein-Haimovichi

papers.title: Complex phase diagram and thermodynamic supercriticality of five-dimensional four-charge AdS black holes in $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity
papers.summary: In this paper, we investigate the complex phase structure and thermodynamic supercriticality of static four-charge anti-de Sitter (AdS) black holes in five-dimensional $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity, with all four physical electric charges held fixed. A Van der Waals-like first-order small/large black hole phase transition is found to terminate at a critical point. By analytically continuing the fixed-charge thermodynamic relations, we trace the two real spinodal singularities through criticality into a complex-conjugate pair in the supercritical region. The corresponding spinodal temperatures exhibit the characteristic $3/2$ near-critical scaling, connecting the subcritical temperature splitting with the imaginary parts of the supercritical complex temperatures. We construct the associated complex phase diagram and identify a Widom-type crossover line from the real-temperature projection of the complex spinodals. This line progressively deviates from the locus of real heat-capacity maxima as the pressure increases. At higher pressures, the real heat-capacity extrema eventually merge and disappear, while the complex spinodal singularities persist. Together, these results reveal a continuous connection between critical phase transitions and supercritical thermodynamics through complex singularity structures, providing further insight into the thermodynamic phase behavior of multicharge supergravity black holes.

authors.name: Di Wu, Xiao-Dan Zhu

papers.title: Chiral edge modes from lattice Chern-Simons theory
papers.summary: It is shown that a level $k$ Abelian lattice Chern-Simons theory with continuum time and a spatial square lattice, which is a topological field theory on the latticized plane and torus, when quantized on a spatial cylinder reduces to chiral edge excitations, exactly localized on the two boundaries and carrying two commuting lattice versions of the level-$k$ $U(1)$ Kac-Moody algebra of opposite chirality. The algebras are represented on a Fock space in the noncompact theory and by a finite Weyl algebra in the compact one. We also observe that the theory has a natural framing of Wilson loops which exhibits the correct framing anomaly.

authors.name: Gordon W. Semenoff

papers.title: Static and dynamical Casimir effects in a wedge within the worldline formulation
papers.summary: We study a real massless scalar field in $d+1$ dimensions confined to a wedge of opening angle $\alpha$, in the presence of a semitransparent circular arc that may oscillate radially. Within the worldline formulation, and for an arbitrary strength $\lambda$ of the $\delta$-potential that models the arc, we expand the effective action in powers of the radial displacement $R$ of the arc. In this formulation, all the information about the media is contained in the propagator of a non-relativistic point particle, so that known results for that propagator can be used directly. At zeroth order we obtain the Casimir energy of the wedge, with Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed walls, and the contribution of the arc in closed form for arbitrary $\lambda$. We show that the worldline integrand is, point by point, the energy density obtained from the energy-momentum tensor of the scalar field with curvature coupling $\xi=1/4$; with this identification, and using dimensional regularization for the integrated quantities, we recover the known results for the wedge and for the wedge closed by a Dirichlet arc. At second order in $R$, we reduce the form factor that determines the imaginary part of the in-out effective action, and hence the probability of pair creation by the moving arc, to a one-loop expression involving the radial Green's functions of each angular sector. In the narrow-wedge limit, each angular sector behaves as a field with a mass set by the angular quantization, coupled to a moving $\delta$-mirror; for a Dirichlet arc, the pair creation spectrum of the exterior region approaches that of a planar massive mirror, while the interior region behaves as a tapered cavity. Finally, by decomposing the electromagnetic field into TE and TM scalars, we obtain the Casimir energy of wedges with perfectly conducting, perfectly permeable and mixed walls.

authors.name: C\'esar Daniel Fosco, Bruno Cardin Guntsche

papers.title: Partially Massless Condensates and Reentrant NUT/Bolt Phase Transitions in Conformal Gravity
papers.summary: We study non-Einstein Bach-flat Taub-NUT/Bolt instantons with weakened AdS boundary conditions. In particular, the next-to-leading-order coefficient in the Fefferman--Graham expansion is nonvanishing, and it sources the partially massless response in the dual conformal field theory. As in the Einstein case, the holographic stress tensor of these instantons represents a perfect fluid with vorticity. Remarkably, we identify a non-Einstein Taub-Bolt branch supporting a nonvanishing partially massless response at zero source, while preserving the full symmetry of the squashed conformal boundary. The additional holographic degrees of freedom enrich the thermodynamic phase structure, allowing the conventional NUT/Bolt transition to disappear or give way to reentrant transitions. We further show that non-Einstein Bolts can possess negative thermodynamic volume and establish the absence of negative modes of a conformally coupled probe scalar on regular Bach-flat NUT backgrounds.

authors.name: Crist\'obal Corral, Felipe Diaz, Borja Diez, Eleftherios Papantonopoulos, Per Sundell

papers.title: Gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rotating background: An eigenfunction approach
papers.summary: We construct the free gluon and Faddeev--Popov ghost propagators in rigidly rotating cylindrical coordinates using an eigenfunction approach within the Feynman gauge. Starting from the quadratic gauge-fixed QCD action, we derive the corresponding kinetic operators and obtain their spectral representations. For the gluon field, a circular polarization basis diagonalizes the vector wave operator, leading to polarization-dependent shifts in the orders of the radial Bessel functions. In the absence of radial boundaries, we explicitly recover the standard Minkowski propagator in inertial Cartesian coordinates, showing that the off-diagonal tensor components in the cylindrical basis have a geometrical origin. We then extend the construction to a finite-radius cylinder satisfying the causality condition $|\Omega|R<1$, imposing relative boundary conditions on the gluon field and Dirichlet conditions on the ghosts. The resulting discrete transverse spectra involve both Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues for the gluon modes, from which we obtain explicit spectral representations of the propagators. Our results provide a consistent framework for perturbative QCD calculations in rotating geometries, retaining the angular-momentum, polarization, and boundary effects relevant to future studies of correlation functions and radiative corrections.

authors.name: Benjam\'in Garc\'ia-Contreras, Luis A. Hern\'andez, R. Zamora

papers.title: On phases of 4d $Spin/SO$ Yang-Mills theories
papers.summary: We study the low-temperature phase diagrams of $Spin(N)/SO(N)_\pm$ Yang-Mills theories as functions of the $\theta$-parameter. In particular, for every even integer $N\geq 4$, we find a phase diagram consistent with the center/CP mixed anomaly, via the technique of mixed gauge theory. The resulting phase diagrams are in perfect agreement with the phase diagrams of $Spin(N)/SO(N)_\pm$ super Yang-Mills theory softly broken by a small gaugino mass. In the case of $Spin(4k)$ Yang-Mills for an integer $k\geq 2$, only two phases appear in the phase diagram, while in the $Spin(4)$ case the phase diagram contains four SPT phases protected by the $\mathbb{Z}_2\times \mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry. In the case of $Spin(4k+2)$ Yang-Mills for a positive integer $k$, the phase diagram contains four SPT phases protected by the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ center symmetry.

authors.name: Ryo Hamachika, Takahiro Nishinaka

papers.title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
papers.summary: We revisit an old idea that spectral flow in WZW models can be associated with certain $G$-bundles over a worldsheet. This allows us to introduce a novel method for computing correlators of spectrally-flowed vertex operators in WZW models with group $G$ and level $k$, by systematically computing the contribution from a network of line defects. Specialising to the case of $G=SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, as is relevant to AdS$_3$ string theory, we demonstrate that generic $n$-point functions of spectrally-flowed vertex operators at tree level can be rewritten in terms of an $(n+1)$-point function of $n$ unflowed vertex operators and one degenerate insertion. This is to be interpreted as an unflowed $n$-point function in an instanton background. Moreover, we conjecture that this $(n+1)$-point function can be recast as an $n$-point function of unflowed operators and we provide evidence for this. We demonstrate that the $(n+1)$-point function satisfies the same constraints from global spacetime conformal invariance as does an unflowed $n$-point function for a specific choice of spacetime coordinates that we determine. We verify that our results agree with bootstrap results in the literature. This provides the next step towards fully solving the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model.

authors.name: Nathan McStay, Ronald Reid-Edwards, Sean Seet

papers.title: A dynamical Einstein-Proca-dilaton holographic model and exotic hybrid meson resonances
papers.summary: A fully dynamical Einstein-Proca-dilaton (EPD) holographic model is developed for the exotic $J^{PC}=1^{-+}$ hybrid meson, incorporating the backreaction of the massive vector field dual to the hybrid current in the bulk. Solving the coupled EPD system yields a self-consistent gravitational background and the mass spectrum of hybrid resonances. While the soft-wall limit reproduces linear Regge behavior, the inclusion of backreaction yields quantitative shifts that improve agreement with experimental candidates. The finite-temperature regime is approached by studying black hole thermodynamics and spectral functions across the confinement-deconfinement transition, fixing the Hawking-Page temperature to $T_c \sim 150 \, \mathrm{MeV}$. Unlike non-backreacted AdS/QCD models, the dynamical background predicts a strong suppression of hybrid states already near the onset of deconfinement. These results demonstrate that gravitational backreaction has measurable consequences for both vacuum spectroscopy and in-medium properties of exotic hybrid mesons, emphasizing the relevance of a dynamical self-consistent approach in AdS/QCD.

authors.name: Bruno Toniato, David Dudal, Hudson Almeida, Roldao da Rocha

papers.title: Striped phases of N=4 SYM at finite density
papers.summary: We construct spatially modulated phases of strongly coupled $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory at finite $R$-charge density. Compactification on a three-torus and unequal background charges isolate an unstable charge-density mode. Its static threshold seeds a nonlinear branch of striped black branes in the STU model. The striped states have higher entropy than homogeneous states with the same energy and conserved charges. They connect continuously to the homogeneous branch, with an entropy excess that begins at fourth order in the modulation amplitude. These solutions provide a candidate endpoint of the charge-transport instability.

authors.name: Alex Buchel

papers.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
papers.summary: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).

authors.name: Zoltan Bajnok, Romuald A. Janik

papers.title: Higher Integrability, Generalized Symmetries, and Partially Topological Field Theories
papers.summary: We exhibit a classical link between higher Lax integrability and generalized symmetries in a non-Lorentzian higher semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory on $M\times\mathbb CP^1$. The equations of motion determine a spectrally dependent flat higher connection on $M$ whose Laurent coefficients organise an infinite hierarchy of conserved quantities. We construct a spectral family of classical $(d_M-2)$-form symmetry line defects associated with the Lax connection, establish an action-preserving deformation law, and exhibit suitable gauge-invariant probes on which the induced transformations act nontrivially.

authors.name: Luigi Alfonsi, Leron Borsten, Mehran Jalali Farahani, Hyungrok Kim, Martin Wolf, Charles A. S. Young

papers.title: Form Factors in AdS from the Worldsheet
papers.summary: We study AdS form factors describing closed strings scattering off D-branes. Assuming that these form factors admit worldsheet integral representations in terms of multiple polylogarithms, we determine their leading curvature corrections around the flat-space limit by matching their pole structure to CFT data. We focus on two examples of defects in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM: a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS 't Hooft loop, dual to a D1 brane, and a pair of giant gravitons, dual to a D3 brane. For the 't Hooft loop, the worldsheet bootstrap completely fixes the form factor, and the result passes nontrivial checks from supersymmetric localization. For the giant gravitons, the bootstrap initially leaves five free coefficients, one of which can be fixed using localization. Remarkably, imposing instead that no new operators appear in the defect channel at this order fixes all five coefficients and reproduces the localization constraint. Under this additional assumption, we therefore obtain a unique D3-brane form factor, with supersymmetric localization providing an independent check.

authors.name: Luis F. Alday, Cl\'ement Virally, Xinan Zhou

papers.title: 5-brane webs and generalised symmetries
papers.summary: 5-brane webs provide a powerful geometric description of five-dimensional quantum field theories, encoding data such as symmetries and dualities. Although the extraction of continuous 0-form symmetries from these systems is well understood, their higher-form symmetries have received less attention. We develop a microscopic prescription for determining 1-form symmetries directly from 5-brane webs. BPS Wilson lines are represented by configurations of D3-branes and $(p,q)$ strings, while their screening by local operators is realised through string junctions, Higgsing, and Hanany-Witten transitions. For webs without orientifold planes, this construction reproduces the Smith normal form prescription based on asymptotic 7-brane charges. We extend the analysis to webs containing O7- and O5- planes. For O7$^-$-planes, the resolved 7-brane charges can be incorporated into the Smith normal form, whereas for O7$^+$-planes we propose an effective charge prescription and test it in both Lagrangian and non-Lagrangian examples. For webs with O5-planes, configurations of half-D3-branes reproduce the centre symmetries of Spin gauge theories and their breaking by matter. Crucially, we find that the 1-form symmetry of an O5-plane system is not determined by asymptotic data alone, but can depend on the local structure of the brane configuration near the orientifold.

authors.name: Mohammad Akhond, Federico Carta, Sung-Soo Kim, Futoshi Yagi

papers.title: Exact Splitting of Amplitudes and One-Loop Integrands: A Classical Origin of Zeros
papers.summary: We introduce a recursion based on hidden zeros that reconstructs complete tree level scattering amplitudes and one-loop integrands at generic kinematics. The recursion takes a universal exact-splitting form: both tree amplitudes and one-loop surface integrands are expressed as sums of products of complete tree functions, with the chosen zero conditions manifest in every term. We establish this structure for cubic scalar theory, the nonlinear sigma model, and inverse string Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) functions. We derive the tree splitting formula from the equations of motion, showing that hidden zeros arise when the product of two currents solves the equations of motion, while corrections away from the zero reconstruct the full amplitude. We further show that inverse KLT is the unique extension of $\mathrm{Tr}(\phi^3)$ with higher-point non-derivative interactions that preserves hidden zeros.

authors.name: Yang Li, Laurentiu Rodina, Zhi-Zhen Wang

papers.title: Anomaly effective actions for 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories
papers.summary: We present a comprehensive analysis of the Wess-Zumino anomaly effective action of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories in components. After reviewing the coset construction of the Wess-Zumino action in the presence of an unbroken subgroup, the gauging of the conformal algebra and the Wess-Zumino effective action for non-supersymmetric conformal field theories with a U(1) symmetry in two and four dimensions, we revisit the superconformal anomalies of $\mathcal{N}=1$ conformal supergravity.
