The first method is zero-knowledge characterization, which exploits intrinsic coupler-resonator coupling to yield rapid and accurate estimates with no prior qubit or coupler spectroscopy, accelerating large scale bring-up. The second method is symmetric branch cancellation, which isolates crosstalk from other dispersive effects allowing for quantifying with high precision. Combined with an improved iterative procedure, these methods suppress residual coupler crosstalk below $5\times10^{-5}$, providing a complete route from zero-knowledge initialization to high-precision crosstalk characterization in fully tunable architectures.

authors.name: Y. Gao, A. Galicia, J. R. Guimar\~aes, Y. Haddad, Y. Liu, J. Cereijo, D. A. Volkov, H. Bhardwaj, M. Neis, M. Jerger, P. A. Bushev, R. Barends

papers.title: Experimental activation of hidden metrological steerability in quantum channels via stochastic filtering
papers.summary: Quantum steering-assisted metrology allows a trusted party (Bob) to improve local phase estimation by exploiting classical information communicated by an untrusted party (Alice). In realistic scenarios, however, the channel is subject to noise that degrades steerability and suppresses the associated metrological advantage. Here, we demonstrate that stochastic pre- and post-filtering operations can revive the violation of the metrological steering inequality (MSI) in phase-covariant amplitude-damping channels where it is initially absent, thereby activating a hidden metrological steerability and restoring their usefulness for quantum metrology. Specifically, the critical damping parameter beyond which the MSI violation is suppressed is raised from $\gamma_c \approx 0.5$ to $\gamma_c \approx 0.75$ for the largest filter strength considered. We verify this in a photonic experiment, where polarization qubits carrying the encoded phase are transmitted through an amplitude-damping channel implemented with a two-path Sagnac interferometer, and the stochastic operations are realized with glass plates at the Brewster angle. By tuning the filter strength and scanning the damping parameter over its full range, we observe the revival of the MSI violation, obtained at the cost of a reduced success probability inherent to the stochastic nature of the filtering operations. Our results establish that metrological utility and steerability can be activated through stochastic operations even when these properties are absent in the original noisy channel, extending filtering-based activation from witnesses of nonclassicality to a certified and operationally quantified metrological advantage.

authors.name: H. S. Karthik, J. Berm\'udez, D. Montoya, J. Parra-Past\'en, F. M. Quinteros, Akshata Shenoy H., M. Paw{\l}owski, S. P. Walborn, G. Lima, E. S. G\'omez

papers.title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
papers.summary: Max-Cut is a common testbed for near-term quantum optimization because it has a simple Ising Hamiltonian, established classical baselines, and a parameterized quantum circuit whose performance depends on the outer classical optimizer. This paper develops QASPA-MaxCut, a shift-phase circuit for Max-Cut that encodes graph edges through controlled $R_y$ rotations of the form $\mathrm{CX}_{ij}R_y(\theta_{ij})\mathrm{CX}_{ij}$. We derive the exact two-qubit algebra of the edge block, trace an unweighted four-vertex example, and compare one-layer QASPA-MaxCut with depth-one QAOA by exact state-vector simulation. The protocol uses seed 42, evaluates connected backbone-augmented random graphs with additional-edge probabilities $p_{\mathrm{edge}}\in\{0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7\}$, and adds nineteen custom unweighted topologies. The QASPA-MaxCut score is reported after the algorithm's classical selection stage: the four leading QASPA bit strings are evaluated by the Max-Cut objective, and the best cut is retained. The QAOA score is the expected approximation ratio after local optimization, reported as a best-of-$k$ curve over one to ten restarts. In these small exact simulations, fixed-angle QASPA-MaxCut produces reported group-mean selection ratios between $0.955$ and $1.000$, the topology-level readout is unchanged in the retained finite-shot checks under the rule $\lceil 0.03047\cdot 2^n+1016.2\rceil$, and depth-one QAOA improves with additional classical restarts while remaining lower than the QASPA selection score in the reported mean summaries. This comparison motivates further study of the classical search budget needed to obtain competitive Max-Cut samples at shallow circuit depth.

authors.name: Dmytro Sapozhnyk

papers.title: Phase-Locked Quantum Battery Charging via Dissipative Mode Selection
papers.summary: We investigate how dynamical instability and reservoir engineering can be harnessed to enhance the quality of quantum-battery charging in a bosonic two-mode system. We show that reservoir-engineered dissipative coupling selectively amplifies a single unstable quasi-dark mode, enabling phase-locked exponential charging at a reduced gain threshold, whereas coherent coupling can amplify two frequency-split unstable modes, resulting in persistent beating. This dissipative mode selection yields a near-unit ergotropy fraction and a substantially higher work-like signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), defined as ergotropy divided by the standard deviation of battery energy. Although optimizing the driving frequency enables coherent coupling to achieve faster charging and higher ergotropy power, dissipative coupling retains its advantage in the work-like SNR. An exact finite-time source-noise relation reveals that this advantage arises from a more constructive accumulation of coherent driving relative to incoherent fluctuations. Our results establish dissipative mode selection as a promising route to high-quality quantum-battery charging.

authors.name: Borhan Ahmadi, Lei Du, Andr\'e H. A. Malavazi, Shabir Barzanjeh, Adam Miranowicz, Pawe{\l} Horodecki

papers.title: Solving a non-abelian hidden subgroup problem on a trapped-ion quantum computer: the power of the measurement basis
papers.summary: The hidden subgroup problem (HSP) unifies many of the best-known quantum speed-ups. For abelian groups it is solved efficiently by weak Fourier sampling, but for non-abelian groups, which include the cases relevant to graph isomorphism and lattice-based cryptography, the right measurement basis is crucial and often unknown. We experimentally study the HSP over the $q$-hedral groups $\mathbb{Z}_q \ltimes \mathbb{Z}_p$, which interpolate between the dihedral and affine groups and mark a boundary between instances that are efficiently solvable and those that are only information-theoretically solvable. On the IonQ Forte trapped-ion quantum computer, with $p \le 7$, we implement weak Fourier sampling, strong Fourier sampling in an adapted basis, strong Fourier sampling of adjacent pairs, and forgetful abelian sampling. We demonstrate that the theoretical predictions of Moore, Rockmore, Russell and Schulman survive on a noisy device: weak sampling reveals nothing about the hidden subgroup, the adapted basis succeeds for large $q$, adjacent pairs succeed for small $q$, and forgetful sampling saturates below unit success. For $p=7$, $q=6$, the hardware exceeds the success probability of an exhaustively optimised classical algorithm for up to three oracle queries.

authors.name: Oliver O'Brien

papers.title: A Quantum Lower Bound for Triangle Finding
papers.summary: Triangle finding is a fundamental problem in graph theory that has played a central role in the development of quantum algorithmic techniques. For $N$-vertex graphs given by their adjacency matrices, a long line of work has improved the quantum query upper bound from $O(N^{3/2})$ to $O(N^{5/4})$. However, the best known lower bound has remained the elementary $\Omega(N)$ bound obtained from unstructured search. We prove the first superlinear quantum query lower bound for triangle finding, showing that $\Omega(N^{13/12})$ queries are necessary. Our result also implies the same lower bound for triangle detection and for detecting every fixed connected non-bipartite graph. The proof builds on the compressed oracle approach of Zhandry and the transfer approaches of Belovs. It compares the computation on graphs with a planted triangle to the computation on random graphs conditioned to be triangle-free, through a map on the input registers that almost commutes with every query. We average over local changes to the input while preserving its distribution, through a procedure known as conditional resampling. Our main technical contribution is a set of estimates that let us control the query error under this averaging, despite the dependence introduced by conditioning a dense graph to be triangle-free.

authors.name: Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, Xingyu Zhou

papers.title: Resource-efficient formulations of the Knapsack problem for quantum computing
papers.summary: Quantum computing has emerged as a new tool for solving combinatorial optimization problems. Quantum optimization approaches usually operate on the subclass of Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problems. Many optimization problems can be reformulated in this form, though there are often multiple ways to do so. The choice of formulation can considerably affect the performance of QUBO solvers in practice. In this work, we study QUBO formulations of the Knapsack problem, a canonical example of a problem with inequality constraints. In the standard formulation these constraints are converted into penalty terms, which requires additional slack variables. Here, we investigate three more resource-efficient approaches for formulating the Knapsack as a QUBO. The first two modify the standard formulation, either by deriving a smaller penalty constant or by reducing the number of slack variables. The third approach is a wholly different method, which avoids the use of slack variables entirely. All three approaches increase the probability of finding the optimal solution, both in simulations of the linear ramp Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (LR-QAOA) and on a D-Wave quantum annealer. The slackless method performs best, increasing success probabilities by several orders of magnitude even for relatively small problem sizes.

authors.name: Pim van den Heuvel, Vrinda Mehta, Dennis Willsch, J. A. Montanez-Barrera, Kristel Michielsen

papers.title: Finite-temperature transition-window weights on a fault-tolerant quantum computer: duplex filtering on a thermal purification
papers.summary: The excite-filter-readout framework of Kharazi et al. computes zero-temperature response windows on a fault-tolerant quantum computer from a pure ground state. We extend it to Gibbs states, where the two objects decouple: filters act on absolute energies, a thermal response on transition frequencies. The extension rests on a Liouville-space/TFD identity, explicit in the block-encoding/QSP setting: the thermally weighted transition-window weight is a spectral projection of H_0 (x) I - I (x) H_0^T onto the Schmidt (thermofield-double) purification, instance of Rall's framework. Around it we assemble a routed-SELECT block encoding (one Hamiltonian query per filter query), a conjugate-pair readout, and a four-route (duplex, bin, Fourier-LCU, METTS) compatibility analysis. The cost is multiplicative and conditional: a per-window query bound M_"AE" * (2*sqrt(d/Z_"lb")*d_"vt" + 4*d_W), with a tight signal-adaptive count, the optimal sqrt(alpha beta) degree, and a window-edge term. The preparation factor sqrt(d/Z) grows exponentially with system size at fixed temperature in positive-entropy-density systems (2.08 -> 25.7, N = 8 to 14 at beta = 2), relieved only as beta -> 0. Zero temperature is recovered for beta G >= ln(2(d-1)||D||^2/epsilon). Identities are cross-checked between independent formula paths to 10^(-16)-10^(-12) and the readout assembly is validated at matrix level under a block-encoding promise.

authors.name: Yujin Tang, Yunlong Liu, Miao Xu, Qing-Xing Xie

papers.title: Linear-time erasure recovery for quantum expander codes
papers.summary: Erasures are used to model faults at a subset of known locations in various platforms used to construct fault-tolerant quantum computers. Beyond the utility in erasure recovery, efficient decoders for erasures are useful to both understand error decoders and as a subroutine for error decoding. Classical expander codes, which belong to the family of low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, can be equipped with the Peeling decoder which works in linear time. Our main result is the algorithm Small-Set-Peeling, a quantum generalization of the classical Peeling decoder for erasures, that applies to quantum expander codes (Tillich, Z\'emor, IEEE T-IT 2013; Leverrier, Tillich, Z\'emor, FOCS 2015). This decoder can correct up to $D-1$ erasures, where $D$ is the (design) distance of the code and, importantly, is the first decoder that is guaranteed to do so in linear time. Combining with the erasure-conversion algorithm Small-Set-Find (Krishna, Livni-Navon, Wootters, SODA 2024), our result also implies the existence of a novel graph-local linear-time decoder for Pauli errors.

authors.name: Anirudh Krishna, Christopher A. Pattison

papers.title: GFlowQEC: Generative Flow Networks that Learn to Sample Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.summary: Choosing a quantum error-correcting code for a real device means scoring candidates with circuit-level simulations so slow that only a few hundred can be run. So every evaluation counts, and a search is judged by how many good codes it finds per paid evaluation. Quantum LDPC codes built from a few group elements protect many logical qubits, but good ones are rare in a huge space. We introduce GFlowQEC, to our knowledge the first generative flow network (GFlowNet) for quantum code design. It builds a code one group element at a time and learns to propose codes in proportion to a power of their score. We train it once on scores from earlier searches, freeze it, and let it propose lifted-product codes with 180 physical qubits, scored by their distances. Ranking ten of its draws per paid call, it finds more than twice as many new top-scoring codes (inequivalent to any it was trained on) as tuned parallel tempering, even when tempering starts from GFlowQEC's training codes. It finds more than three and a half times as many as a supervised screen ranking ten random candidates per call. When both rank a hundred, the screen beats GFlowQEC, and does best ranking GFlowQEC's draws. Soft Q-learning, which shares the GFlowNet's optimal policy, does as well at one noise bias and better at the other, so the gain does not depend on the GFlowNet's training loss. Trained proposers can make a budget of expensive evaluations go further when good codes are rare.

authors.name: Nuno Batista, Gabriel Falcao, Penousal Machado

papers.title: Quantum Algorithms for Molecular Response Functions: Resolvent Kernels, Time-Domain Sampling, Query Lower Bounds with Matched Single-Point Calibers, and a Six-Route Comparison
papers.summary: Quantum algorithms for molecular response functions have mostly been studied one route at a time, most prominently the indicator-binning algorithm of Kharazi et al. We compare six routes within one accounting framework and state the conversions between their resource calibers. On the resolvent route the Lorentz-broadened spectrum is exactly a resolvent expectation; at finite gamma two boundary terms, a reversal term and a permanent-dipole pseudo-line, enter a disjoint error budget. Because the kernel subnormalization is exactly 1, the published binning accounting carries a removable Theta(alpha+1+omega) factor (49.69x and 7.75x at the definitional caliber), a correction that applies to both routes. Estimating the square root of the kernel amplitude lowers the readout cost from beta^2/mu_tilde_2 to beta/sqrt(mu_tilde_2). On the time-domain route we prove a single-point amplitude-estimation theorem and convert the generalized QPE of Loaiza et al. to the same accounting. The lower bounds are Theta_tilde(1/gamma) for parameter location, Theta(1/(gamma epsilon)) for windowed values, Omega(n/gamma) inside a restricted correlation-sampling class, and Omega(1/(epsilon gamma^2)) on the Lorentzian object; in the single-circuit-resolution caliber, gamma^(-n) is a grid-coverage artifact. Six routes, their calibers, an n=2 assembly with a component-grade coherence, and a phase diagram over the tested ensembles form one accounting map.

authors.name: Yunlong Liu, Yujin Tang, Miao Xu, Qing-Xing Xie

papers.title: Optimal Holding Times for Entanglement Swapping
papers.summary: We revisit the optimization of entanglement holding times in memory-based quantum repeaters for maximizing entanglement swapping throughput under different fidelity constraints - strict, probabilistic, and mean. We consider two heterogeneous quantum links that are equipped with single or multiple memories and differ in decoherence rates, memory capacities, entanglement attempt rates and success probabilities, as well as classical communication latencies. Efficient models are developed to estimate the expected entanglement throughput and the probability density functions of the conditional wait time to swap. The models are then used to satisfy different fidelity requirements by optimizing the maximum holding times for the two links. Finally, our proposed model and approach are validated with a discrete-event quantum network simulator.

authors.name: Van Sy Mai, Richard J. La, Abdella Battou

papers.title: Probing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors
papers.summary: The near-field gravitational interaction between masses is always thought of as instantaneous, an assumption experimentally tested only up to 1.7 kHz, where measurements yield a bounds at the $10^{-5}$ s level. We propose a near-field experiment reaching up to megahertz frequencies, in which a levitated microrotor modulates a mass quadrupole and a second rotor measures the resulting gravitational tidal field as a torque. Because the detector rotor acts as a mechanical local oscillator, the megahertz signal is downconverted to a convenient band of a few hertz, and since at fixed geometry neither the torque nor the integration time depends on the rotation rate, higher frequencies are reached at no cost in sensitivity. With parameters within reach of magnetically levitated NdFeB rotors, a signal at 2 MHz yields a torque of $2\cdot 10^{-25}$ Nm, detectable in under an hour at 10 mK. Treating a possible departure from instantaneous gravitational coupling through a field relaxation time, the measured torque could constrain it at the $10^{-8}$ s level, improving on the existing bounds by more than three orders of magnitude. As a byproduct of our analysis, we derive the sensitivity of a rotor operated as a tunable high-frequency gravitational-wave detector, finding that a noise-equivalent strain around $10^{-22}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ could be achievable in the megahertz band.

authors.name: Matteo Fadel, Andrea Vinante

papers.title: Arithmetic Depth, Minimal Gate Alphabets, and Exact Program-State Resources for Single-Qubit Dyadic Programs
papers.summary: Resource analyses for quantum programs commonly provide safe upper bounds on qubits, gates, or non-Clifford operations. We study a single-qubit dyadic fragment in which the deepest exact resource layer can instead be inferred exactly. Starting from the normalized-midpoint misty-state syntax, we define dyadic program states and the real cyclotomic tower $K_D=\mathbb Q(2\cos(\pi/2^D))$. For the projective single-qubit Clifford-cyclotomic tower $\widehat G_D\subseteq SO(3)$, we prove the relative intersection law $\widehat G_D\cap SO(3,K_d)=\widehat G_d$ for $d\le D$. Combining this descent theorem with an arithmetic-closure invariant for adaptive stabilizer processing yields $\mathrm{Fdepth}(U)=\mathrm{Adepth}(U)=\mathrm{Rdepth}(U)$: the smallest real cyclotomic field containing the Bloch matrix of an exactly synthesizable channel, the shallowest dyadic gate alphabet realizing it up to global phase, and the shallowest dyadic program-state layer sufficient for exact stabilizer-assisted implementation coincide. At that common minimum, known fixed-alphabet synthesis gives minimum primitive-rotation count. We package the result as an exact static resource effect and outline a certificate-producing compiler.

authors.name: Tony Newton, Dan-Adrian German

papers.title: Using topology to reveal all mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
papers.summary: Mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) describe complementary quantum measurements: certainty in one basis gives no information about the others. In dimension six, triples of MUBs are known, but whether a fourth basis could exist remained unresolved for over three decades. OpenAI recently reported a proof that none exists. Here we use the topology of the space of complex Hadamard matrices, which describe transitions between MUBs, to characterize all sets in dimension six. We prove that every mutually unbiased triple belongs to a two-parameter family or is a single isolated triple built from the Fourier matrix. Since none of them extend to a fourth basis, this also proves that no four MUBs exist. Our proof rests on a new topological result that all order-six complex Hadamard matrices except Tao's form a connected space. Connectedness reduces the classification of triples to finitely many overlapping four-dimensional phase balls. We certify with interval arithmetic that these balls cover the space and for every pair of MUBs represented in a ball, we then determine all third bases that extend it. Dimension six is now the first non-prime-power dimension in which all sets of MUBs are classified.

authors.name: Mateo C\'ardenes Wuttig, Joseph Tindall

papers.title: Cryptanalysis of Isogeny-Based Quantum Money with Rational Points
papers.summary: Quantum money is a representative application in cryptography that utilizes quantum technology to achieve security that is unattainable with classical systems. Since the theoretical proposal by Wiesner in 1983, the most recent instantiation is the quantum money using class group actions on elliptic curves, proposed by Montgomery and Sharif in Asiacrypt'24. In this work, we propose a concrete cryptanalysis by leveraging the efficiency of evaluating division polynomials with the coordinates of rational points, offering a speedup of $O(\log^4p)$ compared to the brute-force attack. While the resulting attack still runs in exponential time, our method provides the first nontrivial algorithmic insight into their structural hardness. Furthermore, due to the algebraic properties of rational points and quadratic twists, our technique naturally yields a more efficient verification procedure for the underlying quantum money. We believe this new line of analysis opens promising directions for future research in elliptic-curve-based quantum cryptography.

authors.name: Hyeonhak Kim, Donghoe Heo, Seokhie Hong, Sangjin Lee, Suhri Kim

papers.title: LaQX: A JAX Toolkit for Neural Quantum State Simulations of Lattice Quantum Many-Body Models
papers.summary: Neural quantum states provide accurate variational representations for interacting lattice fermions and spins. Turning a new ansatz into a reproducible calculation, however, requires coordinated implementations of the Hamiltonian, sampling, optimization, observables, and accelerator parallelism. We present LaQX (Lattice Quantum simulation based on jaX), an open-source neural quantum state library based on JAX that organizes these components through common functional interfaces. Beyond ground-state variational Monte Carlo, LaQX supports excited-state calculations, Green's Function Monte Carlo refinement, adiabatic evolution, and real-time evolution with time-dependent variational Monte Carlo. It consolidates methods developed in recent high-accuracy neural quantum state studies of the Hubbard model and frustrated magnets, and the package has been used to investigate the triangular-lattice Hofstadter-Hubbard model. We document these capabilities with reproducible calculations for Hubbard, $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg, altermagnetic Hubbard, and interacting Hofstadter models. Function-oriented modules separate the scientific components and limit the source context needed for extensions by human developers and large language models. Source code, documentation, and executable examples are available at https://github.com/bytedance/laqx.

authors.name: Yuntian Gu, Chaohui Fan, Ruichen Li, Haoxiang Chen, Weizhong Fu, Yixiao Chen, Dingshun Lv, Weiluo Ren, Tao Xiang, Liwei Wang, Mingpu Qin, Xiang Li

papers.title: Estimating the generator of matrix exponential time-series
papers.summary: The achievable precision in estimating the spectrum of a time-series signal that is promised to be sparse in Fourier space deteriorates rapidly as the spectral peaks get closer together, as soon as we introduce noise. Here, we study the related task of generator estimation: estimating the generator of a matrix exponential time-series and its eigenvalues. We obtain rigorous non-asymptotic precision guarantees on genESPRIT, a practical algorithm solving generator estimation, and show that this task can be solved with precision independent of the spectral spacing. The guarantees are complemented by a Cram\'er--Rao analysis of a relaxation of the problem. In particular, in the case of unitary data with bounded additive noise with effective entrywise variance $\sigma^2$, we show that genESPRIT estimates the associated propagator matrix in Frobenius norm with precision scaling as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sigma NL^{-\frac12})$ in the length of the time-series $L$ and matrix dimension $N$, matching the corresponding spectrum-independent Cram\'er--Rao standard deviation scaling up to logarithmic factors. We prove that the matching distance error in the spectrum estimated by genESPRIT scales as $\tilde{\mathcal{O}} (\sigma^2 N^3 L^{-1} + \sigma N^{\frac32} L^{-\frac32} )$, which we compare to the lower bound on the corresponding Cram\'er--Rao bound with the asymptotic standard deviation scaling $\mathcal{O}(\sigma L^{-\frac32})$. These guarantees provide the first rigorous bounds on solving the generator estimation problem. As the matrix exponential time-series can be obtained from linearly independent vector time-series by concatenation, this work opens up a new direction in spectral estimation, which circumvents the problem of crowded spectra, under the additional assumption of linear independence.

authors.name: Jon\'a\v{s} Fuksa, Jens Eisert, Ingo Roth

papers.title: A Fully Polynomial Approximation Algorithm for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
papers.summary: Montanari's incremental approximate message passing (IAMP) algorithm [FOCS 2019; SIAM J. Comput., 2025] and the zero-temperature formulation of El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke (AMS) [Ann. Probab., 2021] find a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation to the maximum Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) energy in $C(\varepsilon)N^2$ operations for fixed accuracy, with probability tending to one as $N\to\infty$, under their respective full-support and access-model assumptions. However, it was unknown whether this approximation could be achieved with work polynomial in both $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$, together with quantitative guarantees at finite dimension. Under the same assumptions as AMS, we introduce grouped IAMP with exact Gaussian query outputs (GEG-IAMP), which is the first SK approximation algorithm with total work polynomial in $N$ and $1/\varepsilon$ and a finite-size guarantee above a dimension threshold polynomial in $1/\varepsilon$ and $\log(1/\alpha)$. More precisely, for every $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$, it returns a $(1-\varepsilon)$ approximation with probability at least $1-\alpha$ whenever $N\ge \mathsf{K}\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(e/\varepsilon)\log(\mathsf{K}/\alpha)$, using $O(N^2/\varepsilon)$ work and $O(N^2)$ storage. GEG-IAMP replaces the Onsager correction by Reeves's coupling construction [arXiv:2508.10782] and groups Euler-Maruyama steps into $O(1/\varepsilon)$ matrix-vector products. We also prove a relative guarantee for AMS IAMP with $O(N^2\varepsilon^{-3}\log^2(e/\varepsilon))$ work but a sufficient dimension exponential in inverse accuracy. By returning a fixed configuration below its dimension threshold, GEG-IAMP also provides an asymptotic fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme (AFPRAS), with an additive error independent of dimension.

authors.name: Dylan Herman, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul

papers.title: Shapiro spikes in driven quantum fluids
papers.summary: Periodic driving of a Josephson junction produces resonant transport signatures known as Shapiro spikes, conventionally described by effective circuit models. Here, we demonstrate Shapiro spikes in a neutral quantum fluid using simulations of a potential-biased atomic Josephson junction. The dc-current resonances follow the expected Bessel-function scaling, including the suppression and revival of individual resonances with increasing modulation strength. We uncover their microscopic mechanism by showing that the phase-winding frequency develops finite plateaus at integer multiples of the drive frequency. These phase-locked states are sustained by quantized-vortex nucleation and the associated $2\pi$ phase slips. Remarkably, within a locking plateau, the dc current and density transfer can reverse direction while the phase-winding frequency remains locked to the drive, giving rise to negative-mobility transport. Our results establish a microscopic link between vortex-mediated phase slips, Shapiro resonances, and anomalous transport in a neutral quantum fluid, revealing how quantized vortices convert resonant transport into phase-locked dynamics with negative mobility.

authors.name: Vijay Pal Singh, Ludwig Mathey, Luigi Amico

papers.title: Stabiliser codes over prime fields as weighted graphs and as quantum sets of lines
papers.summary: We further develop the theory of quantum stabiliser codes and its links with graph theory and finite geometry. We prove that an [[n,k,d]]_p stabiliser code over a finite field with p elements, p prime, gives rise to a graph on n-k vertices together with two disjoint independent sets of size k. Its edges are weighted with elements of a finite field of size p. If k=0, such codes are known as graph states. Second, we view stabiliser codes as so-called quantum sets of lines in projective space, allowing us to determined their minimum distance geometrically. We describe two geometrical operations to obtain new quantum sets of lines from given quantum sets of lines. As an application, we list the number of stabiliser codes up to equivalence, for given small parameters.

authors.name: Simeon Ball, G\"ulizar G\"unay, Robin Simoens, Ricard Vilar

papers.title: Dynamical Signatures of Selective Gap Closing in Multi-Dimensional Monotone Quasiperiodic Operators
papers.summary: We translate the spectral gap-closing criterion for multi-dimensional monotone quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators into a concrete dynamical protocol and verify it by large-scale numerics. For a non-principal label we construct a sampling function whose leading eigenfunction weight at the origin vanishes; a local bump then drives the residual weight through zero. The height of a weighted oscillatory time average of the origin-to-localization-center correlator exhibits a deep minimum precisely at the closing, while the site-control label remains featureless and orders of magnitude larger. The signature is robust and maps directly onto superconducting-circuit and photonic platforms.

authors.name: Leonid Parnovski, Roman Shterenberg

papers.title: Exact Mirror-Parity Selection Rule for Electron-Phonon Coupling in Two-Dimensional Crystals
papers.summary:
The electron--phonon (e-ph) interaction underlies conventional superconductivity and plays a central role in transport and other many-body phenomena in solids. Here, we derive a symmetry selection rule for e-ph scattering in two-dimensional crystals possessing a horizontal mirror plane, $\sigma_h$. For electronic states of mirror parity $s_n(\mathbf{k})$ and $s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})$, and a phonon mode of parity $\chi_
u(\mathbf{q})$, we show that the e-ph matrix element $g_{mn,
u}(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{q})$ vanishes identically unless $s_n(\mathbf{k})\,\chi_
u(\mathbf{q})\, s_m(\mathbf{k}+\mathbf{q})=+1$. The rule follows from the covariance of the phonon-induced deformation potential under $\sigma_h$, constitutes the $C_s$ case of the general group-theoretical selection rule for matrix elements, and partitions the e-ph interaction throughout the Brillouin zone into symmetry-allowed and symmetry-forbidden scattering channels. Consequently, mirror-even phonons couple electronic states of the same mirror parity, either even--even or odd--odd, whereas mirror-odd phonons couple only states of opposite mirror parity, for both intra- and interband processes. We illustrate the selection rule through first-principles calculations for the two-dimensional superconductor $\mathrm{Sc_2BCH_4}$, where mirror parity is well defined throughout the entire Brillouin zone and symmetry-forbidden matrix elements vanish up to numerical precision. We then extend the analysis to bulk $\mathrm{MgB_2}$, where the rule applies exactly only on mirror-invariant planes of the three-dimensional Brillouin zone. Moving away from these planes removes the exact mirror constraint and activates scattering channels that are symmetry forbidden when the mirror eigenvalues are well defined. Our results establish horizontal mirror symmetry as an exact and practical filter of e-ph scattering processes.

authors.name: Nicol\'as F. Barrera, Javiera Cabezas-Escares, Francisco Munoz, Carlos Cardenas, Julia Contreras-Garc\'ia

papers.title: Exact teleportation bounds for fermionic Hawking thermality beyond the single-mode approximation
papers.summary: Fermionic teleportation near a Schwarzschild horizon involves two physically distinct ingredients that are often varied together: Hawking thermal mixing and the relative composition of the right and left Unruh modes. We separate them by factorizing the reduced map of the detected exterior fermionic mode into a mode-preparation channel and a Hawking thermal channel. At fixed right-left Unruh-mode composition, we then solve a global constrained quantum-channel optimization over all two-qubit resource states whose fully entangled fraction remains at or below the standard teleportation threshold immediately before thermal mixing. A parity twirl and positivity reduce the arbitrary-state problem exactly to a two-variable quadratic optimization. The solution yields a necessary-and-sufficient activation boundary, a second exact boundary for attaining the universal optimum, and explicit optimizing states. The resulting phase diagram contains a strict no-go region, a composition-limited activation region, and a universal-bound region. The analysis converts state-specific observations of Hawking-assisted teleportation into exact channel-level bounds over the full two-qubit state space.

authors.name: Zhiming Huang

papers.title: Coherence Spreading Law in Quenched Homogeneous Bose Gases
papers.summary: We investigate nonequilibrium coherence spreading in quenched homogeneous bosonic gases both analytically and numerically. Our ensemble-averaged Gross-Pitaevskii trajectory approach and kinetic analysis confirm the linear-in-time growth of the squared coherence length, and explicitly give the spreading-law dependence on the ratio of initial energy to healing energy. When the ratio is relatively small, the squared coherence length grows at a universal rate determined by the ratio of Planck's constant to the particle mass, insensitive to interaction strength and initial momentum distributions. However, our further calculations uncover fundamental limitations to such universality and establish its phase boundaries governed by low system energies, weak interparticle interactions and many-body integrability. Our theory fully reproduces the key experimental signatures and resolves the puzzle of the dynamical origin of the recently observed universal coherence-spreading speed limit [Nature 647, 608-612 (2025)]. Going beyond existing experimental observations, we provide some testable predictions for ultracold-atom experiments and clarify the conditions for the emergence of universal coherent dynamics in nonequilibrium bosonic many-body systems.

authors.name: Yi Cao, Li-Chen Zhao, Jie Liu

papers.title: Emergent Incompressibility in Polariton Condensates for Scalable XY Spin Simulation
papers.summary: Driven-dissipative polariton networks offer a powerful analog platform for simulating continuous-spin Hamiltonians. However, their practical scalability is fundamentally limited by amplitude-phase coupling and metastable trapping in highly frustrated energy landscapes. Here, we present an \textit{in situ} dual-enhancement mechanism to address these bottlenecks without requiring external site-specific fine-tuning. First, a renormalization-group analysis based on density rescaling shows that higher-order nonlinear loss drives the condensates toward an incompressible regime, intrinsically suppressing amplitude fluctuations and enforcing phase-only dynamics. For macroscopic XY networks (up to 10,000 spins), this phase-amplitude decoupling yields a more than 50-fold reduction in energy, while simultaneously shrinking the standard deviation by a factor of six. More generally, it restores the extensive scaling of the optimized XY energy with system size. Second, to navigate the rugged, nonconvex energy landscape, we introduce weak Hermitian pulses. When implemented through a multistage protocol, these pulses enable repeated escapes from local minima and drive the system to deeper energy minima. Benchmarking shows an increasing advantage with system size, with the polariton simulator outperforming the classical Monte Carlo-SQP baseline in every sampled macroscopic realization. Our work provides a physical framework for scalable polariton analog computing.

authors.name: Chengyong Yu, Youya Xu, Xuan Ye, Yan Zhou, Sanjib Ghosh

papers.title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
papers.summary: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. We further derive an asymptotic expansion for the largest eigenvalue, improving on previous estimates and analytically confirming its linear scaling with the particle number, thereby indicating off-diagonal long-range order. For the high-index collective states, we obtain simpler expressions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, showing that the eigenvalues decay as $n^{-4}$ and that the eigenvectors become independent of the number of particles. Finally, we discuss the connection between the collective states and an effective description in terms of composite bosons, whose spectral properties suggest a behavior consistent with Tan's contact for interacting bosonic systems.

authors.name: Abel Rojo-Franc\`{a}s, Joan Martorell, Francesc Sabater, Bruno Juli\'{a}-D\'{i}az

papers.title: Magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields: a Fourier-finite difference approach
papers.summary: We study magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems for two-dimensional magnetic Schr\"odinger operators with nonuniform periodic magnetic fields and periodic scalar potentials, and develop a hybrid Fourier-finite difference discretization. A Landau-type gauge is constructed by solving a periodic Poisson equation. Under the integer magnetic flux condition, the magnetic Bloch boundary conditions are incorporated through shifts of Fourier-mode indices. The method combines link-variable-based covariant central differences in the $x$-direction with a Fourier pseudospectral discretization in the $y$-direction, yielding a Hermitian discrete Hamiltonian. The resulting eigenvalue problems are solved using a LOBPCG method. Under appropriate regularity assumptions, we establish a fully discrete consistency residual estimate of order $O(h_1^2+N_2^{-s})$. With suitable spectral separation and eigenspace dimension-preserving conditions, error estimates of the same order are derived for isolated eigenvalues and their associated eigenspaces. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence in the finite difference direction and rapid error reduction with increasing Fourier resolution, and illustrate band degeneracies and eigenstate distributions in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields.

authors.name: Xueyang Li, Yuanwei Lai

papers.title: Kardar--Parisi--Zhang density hydrodynamics in a coherent XXZ--ASEP Lindbladian
papers.summary: Coherent interactions can generate quantum correlations without changing a stationary density current. Whether that current still determines long-wavelength transport is a dynamical question. We study an XXZ chain with asymmetric Lindblad hopping, whose stationary current has the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP) form although its populations do not evolve autonomously. The current curvature and static susceptibility fix the leading Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) length and amplitude without a fitted length or amplitude conversion factor. The density-visible Liouvillian spectrum, real-space spreading, and Fourier relaxation support KPZ scaling at the finite coherent couplings studied. Central and intermediate stationary density correlations are consistent with the Pr\"ahofer--Spohn profile at this microscopic scale, with resolved finite-time corrections. Reservoir-matched classical references quantify boundary effects, while symmetric hopping recovers diffusion and reduced asymmetry produces the expected crossover. These results connect an exact nonlinear current to the observed long-wavelength KPZ transport of the physical density in an interacting open quantum chain away from the isotropic Heisenberg point.

authors.name: Yansheng Liu, Daoguang Li, Kaixiang Lu, Mingdi Xu, Lei Pan

papers.title: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy
papers.summary: This paper investigates Lorentz violation arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The violation is modeled through a modified dispersion relation parameterized by a dimensionless coefficient $\xi$ and suppressed by the Planck scale. Using high-precision spectroscopic data and a chi-squared fitting procedure that carefully accounts for theoretical uncertainties in the Rydberg constant and the proton radius, the analysis yields a 95% confidence level constraint $\xi \in [-14.3,\; 1.37] \times 10^5$. The mass scaling of the effect reveals two distinct regimes: for the lowest-order deformation, the heavy nucleus amplifies the signal, while for higher-order corrections, the lepton dominates the sensitivity. These bounds approach Planck-scale sensitivity using the simplest atomic systems, thereby circumventing ambiguities inherent in more complex quantum systems.

authors.name: A. S. Lemos, J. E. J. Matias, F. Dahia, I. P. Lobo

papers.title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
papers.summary: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.

authors.name: Kangle Li, Liujun Zou

papers.title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev--Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
papers.summary: Quantum-inspired numerical methods for partial differential equations represent discretized fields and operators as quantics tensor trains (QTT), so that their cost depends on how compressible the problem is rather than on the number of unknowns. Global spectral formulations in this setting have so far relied on Fourier bases, restricted to periodic problems, or on collocation, which does not preserve the variational structure exploited by tensor-network solvers. We introduce a QTT Chebyshev--Galerkin method that assembles and solves global spectral systems directly in compressed form, without forming the underlying arrays. Starting from the weak formulation, the method handles coupled elliptic systems with variable coefficients, smoothly mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet--Robin boundary conditions, and yields symmetric positive-definite systems suited to variational tensor-network solvers. Parameters and random inputs enter as additional coordinates, so the same construction returns the solution over an entire parameter space in a single solve. In linear elasticity, the method retains spectral convergence and reaches errors below $10^{-8}$ on a three-dimensional benchmark, beyond those attained by QTT finite differences and Q2/Q4 FEniCSx finite elements over the tested range. A six-parameter cantilever design study covering $1.7\times10^{7}$ designs is solved in a single 92~s run, and a stochastic problem with ten random coordinates is represented with $2.4\times10^{6}$ times less memory than its full coefficient array.

authors.name: Juan Jos\'e Rodr\'iguez-Aldavero, \'Angel de la Rosa Velasco, Juan Jos\'e Garc\'ia-Ripoll

papers.title: Spectral properties of twisted soft waveguides
papers.summary: We discuss a model of a soft waveguide described by Schr\"{o}dinger operator whose potential is a twisted straight channel of non-circular profile. We show that a compactly supported twist makes the operator subcritical, the property being expressed in terms of a Hardy-type inequality. On the other hand, a periodic twist raises the essential spectrum and its local slowdown may give rise to isolated eigenvalues below the essential spectrum threshold.

authors.name: Pavel Exner, David Spitzkopf

papers.title: A Counterexample to the Weak Gibbs and Regularity Conjectures
papers.summary: We provide a counterexample to the weak Gibbs and regularity conjectures. The example is a spin-one system on the square lattice with a translation-invariant nearest-neighbor interaction. At high temperatures and high on-site field strengths, it has a unique KMS state that does not have the weak Gibbs or regularity properties.

authors.name: Marius Wesle

papers.title: Quantum power iterations via tensor networks
papers.summary: In optimization, one of the well-known classical algorithms is power iterations, which recovers the dominant eigenvector of a diagonalizable matrix. Since numerous optimization problems can be formulated as an eigenvalue/eigenvector search, this algorithm features wide applicability. Operationally, power iterations perform repeated matrix-to-vector multiplications (\texttt{MatVec}) followed by a renormalization step to converge to the dominant eigenvalue/eigenvector. However, classical tensor network realizations can exhibit worst-case exponential growth of tensor ranks with the number of iterations. We propose a quantum realization offering a possible route around this bottleneck. Our method involves casting low-rank representations---MPO for matrices and MPS for vectors---into quantum circuits. Specifically, we recover a unitary approximation by variationally minimizing the Frobenius distance between a target MPO and an MPO ansatz wherein the tensor cores are constrained to unitaries. Such unitary MPOs can be implemented as quantum circuits with ancillary qubits. With appropriate initialization and post-selection on the ancillary space, we realize a single classical iteration. With our proposed methodology, power iterations can be realized entirely on a quantum computer via repeated, static circuit blocks. By exploiting Riemannian optimization and cross-approximation techniques, our methodology becomes instance-agnostic, allowing one to address black-box optimization of functions admitting low-rank tensor network representations within quantum computing. We emphasize that this work establishes the construction and analyzes its reliable operating conditions; it does not demonstrate an end-to-end computational advantage over classical tensor network optimization, which we discuss explicitly.

authors.name: V. Akshay, A. Berezutskii, Ar. Melnikov, A. Termanova, M. R. Perelshtein

papers.title: Approaching the Landauer Bound without Slowing Down
papers.summary: Finite-time memory erasure is conventionally understood to incur an additional energy cost beyond the Landauer bound. Whether this bound can be approached without taking the infinite-time limit remains open. Based on a quantum speed limit, we identify coherence between degenerate states as a resource that allows the Landauer bound to be approached at a finite operation time. For both the $2N$-state and collective spin models, we show that the minimum dissipated heat and the heat generated by continuous protocols approach the Landauer bound at finite operation times, with the corresponding finite-time penalty scaling inversely with system size. We further validate these theoretical predictions numerically for systems coupled to the Ohmic bosonic heat bath with various driving protocols. Our results reveal that operation time is a substitutable resource for approaching the fundamental thermodynamic bound of information erasure.

authors.name: Yue Liu, Chenlong Huang, Xingyu Zhang, Dahai He

papers.title: Entangled quantum trajectories in relativistic systems
papers.summary: Quantum entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, including emerging ground-to-satellite quantum communication. In such a scenario, an important challenge to be overcome is to consider entanglement between two or more quantum particles in different inertial frames, potentially experiencing relativistic effects affecting quantum correlations. In this paper, we present a consistent framework that overcomes this challenge. To this end, we establish the notion of factorizable and entangled multi-time trajectories and derive a class of Euler--Lagrange equations under the constraint of a non-entangling behavior. Comparing this restricted evolution to the solutions of the unrestricted equations of motion allows one to investigate the trajectory-based entanglement of general systems. We solve our equations for interacting particles in a Klein--Gordon-type setting, thereby quantifying the dynamic and relativistic impact of entanglement in a self-consistent manner.

authors.name: Yannick Noel Freitag, Julien Pinske, Jan Sperling

papers.title: Marginal-constrained entropy accumulation theorem
papers.summary: We derive a novel chain rule for a family of channel conditional entropies, covering von Neumann and sandwiched R\'{e}nyi entropies. In the process, we show that these channel conditional entropies are equal to their regularized version, and more generally, additive across tensor products of channels. For the purposes of cryptography, applying our chain rule to sequences of channels yields a new variant of R\'{e}nyi entropy accumulation, in which we can impose some specific forms of marginal-state constraint on the input states to each individual channel. This generalizes a recently introduced security proof technique that was developed to analyze prepare-and-measure QKD with no limitations on the repetition rate. In particular, our generalization yields ``fully adaptive'' protocols that can in principle update the entropy estimation procedure during the protocol itself, similar to the quantum probability estimation framework.

authors.name: Amir Arqand, Ernest Y. -Z. Tan

papers.title: A direct algebraic proof for the non-positivity of Liouvillian spectral values and controlling the dissipative gap of unital systems
papers.summary: Markovian open quantum systems are described by the Lindblad master equation $\partial_t\rho =\mathcal{L}(\rho)$, where $\rho$ denotes the system's density operator and $\mathcal{L}$ the Liouville super-operator, which is also known as the Liouvillian. For systems with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, it is a fundamental property of the Liouvillian that the real parts of all its eigenvalues are non-positive. Analogously, for infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, the Liouvillian as a map on trace-class operators only has spectral values with non-positive real parts. The usual arguments for these properties are indirect, using that $\mathcal{L}$ generates a quantum channel and that quantum channels are contractive. We provide a direct algebraic proof based on the Lindblad form of Liouvillians. Subtleties for infinite-dimensional systems are highlighted. For example, unbounded operators can then be eigenvectors of the adjoint Liouvillian with positive eigenvalues, corresponding to a physical instability of the system. As an illustrative application of the algebraic approach, we prove that a strict minimum can be imposed on the dissipative gap of any unital Markovian spin-$s$ or fermionic many-particle system by adding simple local dissipators. The added dissipators comprise Pauli or generalized Pauli Lindblad operators for spin systems and Majorana Lindblad operators for fermionic systems.

authors.name: Yikang Zhang, Thomas Barthel

papers.title: Quantum Information Transmission Over Quantum Relay Channels
papers.summary: Quantum relays are central to both quantum communication and distributed quantum computing, enabling long-distance transmission and modular architectures. Unlike classical repeaters, quantum repeaters preserve coherence without amplifying quantum information, relying on entanglement swapping and quantum error correction to overcome loss and decoherence. In this work, we investigate the transmission of quantum information via quantum relay channels. Our three-terminal relay model captures the trade-off between repeater-assisted and repeaterless communication strategies. Specifically, we propose a partial decode-forward strategy, in which quantum ``message system" consists of two components. The first component is decoded by the relay and then sent to the destination receiver, whereas the second component is decoded by the destination receiver without the relay's help. We analyze both entanglement-assisted and unassisted scenarios. As a special case, the full decode-forward strategy is recovered, with the relay decoding, re-encoding, and forwarding the entire message. Our framework allows for different entanglement topologies between the transmitter, the relay and the destination receiver, recovering known results on entanglement-assisted and unassisted communication. Furthermore, we discuss the interpretation of coding with quantum side information. These findings provide a foundation for designing secure, efficient, and reliable quantum networks and for realizing practical quantum repeaters and long-range quantum key distribution.

authors.name: Yigal Ilin, Uzi Pereg

papers.title: Quantum-elevated Chiral Discrimination for Bio-molecules
papers.summary: Chiral discrimination of enantiomeric biomolecules is vital in chemistry, biology, and medicine. Conventional methods, relying on circularly polarized light, face weak chiroptical signals and potential photodamage. Despite extensive efforts to improve sensitivity under low-photon exposure, classical chiral probes remain fundamentally bounded by the shot-noise limit due to quantum fluctuations. To beat these limitations, we demonstrate quantum-elevated chiral discrimination using continuous-variable polarization-entangled states as moderate-photon-flux, high-sensitivity, quantum-noise-squeezed chiral probes. We achieve a 5 dB improvement beyond the SNL in distinguishing L- and D-amino acids in liquid phase. This non-destructive, biocompatible protocol enables high-sensitivity chiral analysis, with broad implications for drug development, biochemical research, environmental monitoring, and asymmetric synthesis.

authors.name: Yiquan Yang, Xiaolong Hu, Wei Du, Shuhe Wu, Peiyu Yang, Guzhi Bao, Weiping Zhang

papers.title: Single-Photon Scattering in a Waveguide Coupled to a Giant Atom with Loss or Gain
papers.summary: This work investigates single-photon scattering in a one-dimensional coupled-resonator waveguide interacting with a giant atom with a complex on-site energy. Within the generalized projection operator formalism, we derive analytical expressions for the scattering coefficients. We find that the interference effects of a giant atom can decouple the waveguide from the atom under specific conditions, resulting in perfect transmission, distinguishing it from a small atom. Otherwise, a giant atom with loss absorbs the incident wave, whereas a giant atom with gain not only amplifies the incident wave but also leads to scattering divergence at certain energies, corresponding to spectral singularities. We explore the critical scattering dynamics associated with these singularities, and attribute the persistent wave emission to a spectral-singularity state. Furthermore, we show that the system with gain supports at least one time-growing bound state, which dominates the long-time dynamics. Due to the presence of these generalized bound states, the conventional time-independent scattering theory proves inadequate for such a non-Hermitian system in the gain regime. We verify our time-dependent theoretical predictions via numerical simulations of Gaussian wave packet scattering.

authors.name: Yu Xin, Jia-Ming Zhang, Bing Chen

papers.title: Entropic Barriers and the Kinetic Suppression of Topological Defects
papers.summary: Many quantum phases, from topological orders to superfluids, are destabilized at finite temperature by the proliferation and motion of topological defects such as anyons or vortices. Conventional protection mechanisms rely on energetic gaps and fail once thermal fluctuations exceed the gap scale. Here we examine a complementary mechanism of entropic protection, in which defect nucleation is suppressed by coupling to mesoscopic auxiliary reservoirs of dimension $M$, generating an effective free-energy barrier that increases with temperature. In the Ising chain, this produces a characteristic three-regime evolution of the correlation length as a function of temperature - linear growth, entropy-controlled plateau, and eventual breakdown - indicating a general modification of defect behavior. Focusing on two spatial dimensions, where true finite-temperature topological order is forbidden in the thermodynamic limit, we show that entropic protection can nevertheless strongly enhance stabilization at finite system size, the regime directly relevant for quantum memory and experiments. Owing to the topological character of the defects, creation and transport are independently suppressed, yielding a double parametric reduction of logical errors in the entropic toric code and enhanced coherence when the framework is extended to Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transitions. Entropic barriers thus provide a passive and scalable route to stabilizing quantum phases in experimentally relevant regimes. We propose an experimental setup for entropic toric code using dual species Rydberg arrays with dressing.

authors.name: Yi-Lin Tsao, Zhu-Xi Luo

papers.title: Quantum Cram\'{e}r-Rao bound on quantum metric as a single-observable uncertainty relation
papers.summary: The Belavkin version of quantum Cram\'{e}r-Rao bound dictates that the covariance of any set of operators is bounded by a product of the derivatives of expectation values and the inverse of quantum metric. We elaborate that because quantum metric itself is the covariance of the generators of translation in the parameter space, quantum metric in any dimension is bounded by a product of itself and Berry curvature. The generator formalism further indicates that the bound is equivalent to a single-observable uncertainty relation for systems described by multiple observables, which in the two-observable case recovers the Robertson-Schr\"{o}dinger uncertainty relation. The momentum space quantum metric and spin operators of three-dimensional topological insulators under magnetic field are used to demonstrate the validity of these bounds, and their constraints on the spread of Wannier function, absorbance in 2D, and dielectric function in 3D will be elaborated.

authors.name: Wei Chen

papers.title: Completeness for Prime-Dimensional Phase-Affine Circuits
papers.summary: Equational reasoning about circuits underpins quantum-circuit optimisation and verification. In the qubit CNOT-dihedral fragment, phase polynomials and layered normal forms support a complete equational theory. We develop the corresponding theory for prime-dimensional qudits, where basis labels, value controls, and phase exponents share prime-field arithmetic. We first describe reversible affine circuits over F_d as transformations x -> Ax + b, with an affine normal form extending Lafont's linear normal form by translations. Adjoining finite-angle diagonal phases by polynomial degree yields linear, quadratic, and cubic calculi. Their binomial-basis identities expose the mixed diagonal gates forced by affine transport. These calculi have unique phase-affine normal forms, and the resulting equational theories are complete: semantic equality coincides with derivable equality.

authors.name: Colin Blake

papers.title: Efficient Classical Simulation of Low-Rank-Width Quantum Circuits Using ZX-Calculus
papers.summary: In this paper, we introduce an algorithm for contracting (i.e. numerically evaluating) ZX-diagrams whose computational complexity is governed by rank-width, a structural graph parameter that behaves nicely under ZX rewrite rules. Our method evaluates a graph-like ZX-diagram in ~O(4^R) time, given its rank-decomposition of width R. By constructing suitable rank-decompositions, we provide a classical simulation algorithm for quantum circuits whose runtime is bounded by both ~O(2^n) and ~O(2^(t/2)), where n is the number of qubits and t is the number of non-Clifford phase gates. Thus, our method is no slower than either the naive state-vector simulation or the elementary stabiliser decomposition baseline, and in practice can be even faster when the reduced ZX-diagram has low rank-width. We benchmark our simulation algorithm against Quimb, a popular tensor contraction library, and observe substantial reductions in floating-point operations, often by several orders of magnitude, for random and structured non-Clifford circuits and for random ZX-diagrams.

authors.name: Fedor Kuyanov (University of Oxford), Aleks Kissinger (University of Oxford)

papers.title: ZX-Flow: A Flexible Criterion for Deterministic Computation with ZX-Diagrams
papers.summary: Flow criteria are used to efficiently extract computations, either in the form of measurement patterns or quantum circuits, from ZX-diagrams. Existing criteria such as causal flow, generalised flow, and Pauli flow, were all originally formulated for graph states, so they require ZX-diagrams to be in a very particular graph-state-like form. This form is easily broken by applying basic ZX rules and makes establishing some desirable properties very complicated. Here, we introduce a new "ZX-native" flow criterion called ZX-flow, formulated using a new type of decoration of a ZX-diagram we call Pauli semiwebs. These are a generalisation of Pauli webs, which have recently been used extensively in reasoning about fault-tolerant computations in the ZX-calculus. We show that ZX-flow is straightforwardly preserved by all Clifford rewrites and furthermore that a ZX-diagram has ZX-flow if and only if it is Clifford-equivalent to a graph-like ZX-diagram with Pauli flow. Finally, we show that any diagram with ZX-flow can be readily interpreted either as a deterministic measurement-based computation or as a Clifford isometry followed by a sequence of Pauli exponentials. The latter can then be efficiently extracted to a quantum circuit.

authors.name: Aleks Kissinger (University of Oxford), John van de Wetering (University of Amsterdam, Qusoft)

papers.title: Generalized Inverses of Quantum Channels: a categorical perspective
papers.summary: A quantum channel is defined as being completely positive (CP) and trace preserving (TP). While not every quantum channel is invertible or reversible, every quantum channel admits various kinds of generalized inverses such as the Moore-Penrose inverse and the Drazin inverse. A generalized inverse of a quantum channel may not itself be a quantum channel: it often fails to be CP. However, generalized inverses still play an important role in quantum error mitigation. Here, because it is often desirable for the generalized inverse of a quantum channel to be at least TP, the Drazin inverse, which is TP, is favoured over the Moore-Penrose inverse, which is not in general TP. In this paper, we take a categorical perspective on generalized inverses of quantum channels. This allows us to give a simple proof of the fact that the Drazin inverse of a quantum channel is always TP. It also allows us to show that for unital quantum channels, the Drazin inverse is also unital. We then generalize this result to dagger Drazin inverses, which allows us to show that for unital quantum channels, the Moore-Penrose inverse is both TP and unital as well. This opens the door to new applications of both the Drazin inverse and Moore-Penrose inverse in quantum information theory and, in particular, in quantum error mitigation.

authors.name: Robin Cockett (University of Calgary), Jean-Simon Pacaud Lemay (Macquarie University), Priyaa Varshinee Srinivasan (Tallinn University of Technology)

papers.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
papers.summary: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.

authors.name: Eric J. Sung, Charles A. Stafford

papers.title: Unlocking a fast adiabatic CZ gate and exact residual $ZZ$ cancellation between fixed-frequency transmons using a floating tunable coupler
papers.summary: Tunable couplers in superconducting qubit architectures enable strong qubit-qubit interactions for two-qubit gates while suppressing unwanted coupling during single-qubit operations. However, achieving low error rates for fast two-qubit gates remains challenging, as suppressing leakage and non-adiabatic errors typically requires specialized qubit, coupler, or pulse designs, often at the expense of an idling $ZZ=0$ condition. In this work, we demonstrate that a symmetric floating tunable coupler provides a natural platform for fast, high-fidelity adiabatic controlled-Z (CZ) gates. Its favorable energy-level structure eliminates the conventional trade-off between rapid conditional-phase accumulation and adiabatic evolution while preserving exact cancellation of residual $ZZ$ interaction at idling. This architecture exhibits intrinsic robustness to non-adiabatic transitions, even under simple flux modulation waveforms. To push performance at short gate durations, where maintaining adiabaticity becomes more challenging despite the favorable level structure, we introduce pulse-shaping techniques based on the instantaneous adiabatic factor that further suppress non-adiabatic errors. We experimentally realize a 24 ns adiabatic CZ gate with fidelity exceeding 99.9% and stable operation over several hours with a time-averaged fidelity of 99.878%

authors.name: Angela Q. Chen, Sarah Strong, Xian Wu, Stefano Poletto

papers.title: Demonstrating Record Fidelity for the Quantum Fourier Transform
papers.summary: We demonstrate the Parity Architecture on quantum hardware, using the quantum Fourier transform (QFT) as a benchmark. As a result, a record performance in both fidelity and qubit count is achieved using quantum processors with a native CZ-based instruction set. On the IBM Heron r3 chip, a process fidelity of the QFT algorithm of ${F \approx 10^{-2}}$ for ${N=50}$ qubits is achieved. The scaling of the speedup compared to previous swap-based methods is super-exponential $\mathcal{O}(\exp(N^2))$. Furthermore, we show that the scaling can be improved further by including iSWAP gates in the instruction set.

authors.name: Philipp Aumann, Michael Fellner, David Alber, Max Cykiert, Christoph Fleckenstein, Roeland ter Hoeven, Leo Stenzel, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Wolfgang Lechner

papers.title: Evaluating quantum circuits in the reservoir computing paradigm
papers.summary: Reservoir computing is a framework for learning temporal correlations in time series data by leveraging the intrinsic dynamics of an underlying physical system. In quantum implementations, the reservoir is commonly realised through the ergodic dynamics of nonintegrable Hamiltonian models. In our present work, we investigate the relation between reservoir performance and underlying dynamics in an analogous setting wherein a structured brickwall quantum circuit functions as the reservoir. We focus on the manner in which the choice of constituent two qubit gates influences task performance correlating the same with known results on the dynamical nature of the circuit in question. Our primary analysis involves the class of dual-unitary circuits, for which features governing the global dynamics are tunable and exactly solvable. We further study a class of circuits constructed out of non-random two qubit gates satisfying a specific solvability condition under the Cartan decomposition, for which the second moment spectrum can be determined analytically. For sufficiently large entangling power of gates, the said circuit converges to unitary designs faster than an equivalent brickwall arrangement of Haar random two qubit gates. In both cases considered, the dynamics are respectively characterised by analytically accessible exact measures of system level complexity. Our results show that reservoir performance is strongly influenced by the choice of local two-qubit operations, and that structured quantum circuits can function as effective reservoirs, where the peak performance can be accessed in relatively modest circuit depths when compared to conventional Hamiltonian reservoirs.

authors.name: Gaurav Rudra Malik, Amit Kumar Jaiswal, S. Aravinda, Sunil Kumar Mishra

papers.title: Sharp Bounds on the Eigenvalues of Kikuchi Graphs and Applications to Quantum Max Cut
papers.summary: We prove that the maximum eigenvalue of the (both signed and unsigned) Laplacian of level $k$ Kikuchi graph of any graph $G$ with $m$ edges is at most $m+k$. This confirms four recent conjectures of Apte, Parekh, and Sud. As applications, we obtain that tensor products of one and two qubit product states achieve an approximation ratio of $5/8$ for Quantum Max Cut and $5/7$ for the XY Hamiltonian. Moreover, combining our bounds with the algorithms analyzed by Apte, Parekh, and Sud, yields efficient algorithms achieving an approximation ratio of $0.614$ for Quantum Max Cut and $0.674$ for the XY Hamiltonian. Finally, we also make modest progress on Brouwer's conjecture and improve Lew's bound on the sum of the top-$k$ eigenvalues of a Graph Laplacian.

authors.name: Ainesh Bakshi, Arpon Basu, Pravesh Kothari, Anqi Li

papers.title: Detecting bipartite entanglement with PnCP maps and non-negative polynomials
papers.summary: Positive non-Completely Positive (PnCP) maps are an essential tool to detect entanglement since their characterization is a dual aspect of the separability problem. A recent algorithm proposed by Kelp et al. explains how to generate PnCP maps based on the construction of certain positive non-Sum-of-Squares polynomials. We implement this algorithm in a numerically robust way and propose a working version on GitHub. We theoretically demonstrate that the maps produced by the algorithm are indecomposable, localized on the boundary of the positive cone and show that they are inequivalent with most other known PnCP maps. We numerically investigate their entanglement power, demonstrating notably that they are capable of detecting PPT entangled states that most criteria fail to detect.

authors.name: Ga\"el Mass\'e, Mounir Rezig, Paul Catala, Santiago Scheiner, Laia Serradesanferm C\'ordoba, Enky Oudot, Damian Markham

papers.title: Hybrid Clifford Codes via Operator Algebra Quantum Error Correction and Projective Representation Theory
papers.summary: Clifford codes are a natural generalization of quantum stabilizer codes based primarily on representation theory. This class of codes has previously been extended to the setting of quantum subsystem codes. We formulate a two-fold generalization of Clifford codes, for both the hybrid classical and quantum information and projective representation theory settings. This leads to new classes of hybrid subspace and subsystem Clifford codes. We extend the fundamental representation theoretic quantum error correction theorem to include these codes, based on the operator algebra quantum error correction framework. We also discuss several examples throughout the presentation, of both stabilizer and non-stabilizer type.

authors.name: Jonas Eidesen, David W. Kribs, Andrew Nemec

papers.title: Quadratic speed-up of quantum adiabatic evolution with engineered dissipation
papers.summary: Quantum adiabatic evolution is often slowed by nonadiabatic leakage near small spectral gaps. We propose an engineered dissipative protocol that continuously relaxes these excitations during the adiabatic evolution. In the ideal limit, a spectrally filtered jump operator induces downward transitions in the instantaneous energy eigenbasis while leaving the instantaneous ground state dark. An effective avoided-crossing analysis shows that in the regime where the engineered relaxation strength is much larger than the minimum gap, the runtime scaling can improve from the closed-system behavior $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^{-2})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\Delta^{-1})$. Finite-temperature upward transitions introduce a thermal error floor, the inverse-gap runtime estimate remains applicable when the thermal excited-state population at the minimum gap stays below a fixed fraction of the target error tolerance. Numerical results show improved ground-state preparation and robustness against weak upward-jump errors over closed-system annealing. We also discuss possible superconducting-circuit implementations using structured bosonic reservoirs and the microscopic consistency requirements for realizing the effective dynamics.

authors.name: Yuanyang Zhou, Biao Wu

papers.title: All-optical Implementation of Generalized Quantum Teleportation
papers.summary: Measurement-based continuous-variable optical quantum computing inherently offers high-speed, large-scale operations, yet its practical performance remains constrained by the processing latencies and throughput bottlenecks imposed by classical electronic feedforward circuits. To overcome these limitations, we propose a loss-tolerant, all-optical feedforward (AOFF) architecture for generalized quantum teleportation, which executes programmable single-mode Gaussian operations and realizes arbitrary single-mode linear operations with two successive stages. Quantitative noise analysis under realistic device parameters demonstrates that the architecture suppresses the hardware-induced noise floor to levels potentially compatible with fault-tolerant quantum computing with Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill qubits over the range of operations required for their Clifford gates. By eliminating optoelectronic conversions, this scheme enables continuous operations with high analog bandwidth and high temporal-mode throughput that drastically reduce circuit runtime. Ultimately, this approach delivers a noise-resilient platform that reconciles operational versatility with the intrinsic speed and bandwidth of optical quantum information processing.

authors.name: Takaya Hoshi, Akito Kawasaki, Xiruo Yan, Atsushi Sakaguchi, Takumi Suzuki, Tatsuki Sonoyama, Hironari Nagayoshi, Kosuke Fukui, Kan Takase, Warit Asavanant

papers.title: Working With Measurement-Based Computations on Qudits
papers.summary: Measurement-based quantum computing is a universal model of quantum computation in which successive product measurements of an entangled resource state drive the computation. The non-deterministic nature of measurements necessitates adaptivity to ensure an overall deterministic computation. Flow structures characterise cases in which such an adaptive correction procedure is possible. Recently, flow has been defined in a setting where the resource states are prime-dimensional qudit graph states rather than the usual qubit graph states. Yet, this qudit flow definition is more burdensome to work with than analogous definitions for qubits. Here, we give a simpler definition of qudit flow and consider various useful properties of this flow, drawing on results for the qubit case. In particular, we show how to focus qudit flow and argue that focused flow is canonical.
