We improve the previous algebraic formulation to capture focused flow and use it to obtain an O(n^3) flow-finding algorithm (where n is the number of qudits), matching the best known complexity for qubit flows and improving on the previous O(n^4) result for qudits. Furthermore, we explore multiple flow-preserving transformations, thus opening a pathway to using flow for optimisation. These transformations include pivoting, removal and insertion of certain types of vertices, and reversibility of flow. Lastly, we propose an algorithmic approach to generating large qudit computations with flow, for testing or machine learning.

authors.name: Piotr Mitosek, Miriam Backens

papers.title: Quantum stochastic thermodynamics of macroscopic systems: an algebraic approach
papers.summary: We build a framework for the thermodynamics of macroscopic quantum systems. In contrast with approaches requiring access to the full density matrix, our framework relies on a coarse-grained description, based on measurement statistics of a few observables. When these observables commute, the outcomes define classical macrostates whose entropy is quantified by observational entropy, accounting for uncertainty about both the macrostate and the microstate within it. We extend this notion to non-commuting observables forming a subalgebra of the operator space, and use Jaynes' principle to define an algebra-dependent entropy interpolating between von Neumann and observational entropies. Given initial and final measurement sets, connected by internal and/or environment-induced dynamics, we derive a second law for the coarse-grained dynamics. Unlike formulations based on von Neumann entropy, our inequality captures irreversibility from both non-unitary environment-induced dynamics and internal equilibration. It takes the usual form of a positive entropy production when the system is initially at internal equilibrium, while correction terms capture nonequilibrium resources ignored by the coarse-graining. We also derive fluctuation theorems for coarse-grained thermodynamic quantities. Along a quasi-static path of measurement schemes, we identify quantum macroscopic notions of work and heat fulfilling the first and second laws, including an additional work contribution from manipulating the algebra to which the system is confined, through external constraints or quantum measurement backaction. Finally, we apply our framework to examples illustrating the impact of varying the coarse-graining scheme. Our approach unifies macroscopic and stochastic thermodynamics in a genuinely quantum framework, laying the basis for a versatile, experimentally friendly toolbox to analyze complex quantum dynamics.

authors.name: Antoine Rignon-Bret, Cyril Elouard

papers.title: Coherent control of subradiant excitations in atomic rings
papers.summary: Subradiant excitations in ordered subwavelength atomic arrays are protected against radiative decay, making them a promising platform for storing and manipulating photonic excitations. The external geometry of the array, combined with dynamical control of the atomic dipole orientation, enables localized trapping and coherent transport of these subradiant excitations. Here, we theoretically demonstrate these capabilities in ring-shaped atomic arrays. Specifically, we show adiabatic transport of a localized excitation around a single ring, coherent transfer of a single excitation between two neighboring rings with geometry-controlled selectivity, and interaction-induced conditional phase shifts between two simultaneously trapped excitations in neighboring rings. Depending on the ring geometry, these realize either an entangling iSWAP-type exchange or a controlled-phase operation with tunable conditional phase. Together, these results demonstrate the potential of ordered atomic arrays as a platform for coherent photonic quantum information processing with dissipation-protected collective excitations.

authors.name: Milena Djatchkova, Igor Lesanovsky, Beatriz Olmos

papers.title: Phase Retrievability of Super Operators and Measurements
papers.summary: We continue the study of Phase Retrieval in the Quantum Information setting in the style of \cite{liu2023phase}, in a manner which is more general in two primary ways: (a) Instead of only pure states we consider also states (and positive semidefinite operators) of bounded rank, as is done in Quantum Tomography; (b) We consider general super operators instead of only quantum channels. We show that in order to have phase retrieval with respect to positive semidefinite operators of bounded rank, it suffices to discriminate between perfectly distinguishable pairs (i.e. those with orthogonal supports). From this we prove that phase retrievability is always Lipschitz stable with respect to the trace norm, and then we use the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities to deduce stability with respect to the Bures--Wasserstein distance (thus generalizing the known stability results for phase retrieval in Frame Theory). For Hermitian-preserving super operators taking values in block-diagonal matrices, we characterize phase retrievability in terms of conditions inspired by the classical complement property from Frame Theory.

authors.name: Javier Alejandro Ch\'avez-Dom\'inguez, Jeremiah Ifeanyi Isu

papers.title: A spectral viewpoint on the single defect tight-binding chain
papers.summary: We analyze the time evolution of the nearest-neighbour tight-binding chain in the presence of a single onsite defect. Such a defect was shown to generate non-trivial transport behavior recently in the article by \textit{Acharya et al J. Stat. Mech. (2026) 043102}. The authors have used a defect technique inspired by classical random walk methods to obtain exact analytical expressions for the occupation probability and subsequently the mean and mean-squared displacement (MSD). Here we derive the same results using a spectral decomposition approach. Starting from the secular equation, we obtain the self-consistency condition for the eigenvalues and construct the corresponding normalized eigenvectors. This approach naturally separates the Hilbert space into a dark subspace, whose states have zero amplitude at the defect site and remain unaffected, and bright subspaces, whose states get modified because of the defect. Using this eigenvalue decomposition, we provide a spectral origin of non-monotonicity in the MSD. Numerical calculations for finite chains show that the analytically estimated critical defect strength is in excellent agreement with the defect strength that minimizes the MSD.

authors.name: Sayan Roy

papers.title: Rate-Fidelity Control for Wide-Area Quantum Links
papers.summary: Quantum network links must distribute entanglement at high rates while satisfying application-specified fidelity demands. However, wide-area deployed fiber links suffer from polarization drift which destabilizes end-to-end fidelity and forces periodic compensation. Current deployments often use active stabilization with fixed control policies, and improvements generally stem from advances in quantum hardware. Meanwhile, software control remains relatively underexplored. Here, we formulate quantum link operation as a joint control problem over tunable rate-fidelity tradeoffs and uncontrollable link drift. From this framework, we construct a link control protocol that dynamically adapts source pump power and polarization compensation to maximize entanglement distribution rate subject to a minimum fidelity constraint. We evaluate the protocol through trace-driven simulations driven by data from a 64 km deployed optical fiber. Compared with optimized static policies, our adaptive controller improves mean entanglement distribution rate by 14% over a 24 hour trace, without requiring any offline policy optimization. Our results show that software-based physical layer control can provide a practical mechanism for improving near-term quantum link performance without requiring additional quantum hardware.

authors.name: Connor Clayton, Cory Nunn, Quinn Carmack, Wayne McKenzie, Anne Marie Richards, Xiaodi Wu, Bobby Bhattacharjee

papers.title: Near-Optimal Mixedness Testing with Pauli Measurements
papers.summary: We consider a fundamental problem of \emph{mixedness testing}: Given $n$ copies of an $N$-qubit state $\rho$, determine whether $\rho = \mathbb{I}_d/d$ or $\|\rho-\mathbb{I}_d/d\|_1 \geq \varepsilon$ with high probability, where $d = 2^N$. In particular, we focus on performing this task with simple single-qubit measurements, i.e. measurements that are prepared independently on each qubit. We provide a nearly complete picture of single-qubit mixedness testing by showing that its copy-complexity is $\tilde{\Theta}\left(\sqrt{10}^N/\varepsilon^2\right)$. To establish our lower bound, we introduce a new measurement-dependent lower bound framework for adaptive single-copy state certification. For the upper bound, we present a randomized Pauli basis measurement protocol, which relies on a new primitive for computationally efficient uniformity testing of correlation-concentrated distributions on the Boolean hypercube. In conjunction, we provide lower and upper bounds for mixedness testing with fixed Pauli measurement protocols.

authors.name: Jayadev Acharya, Abhilash Dharmavarapu, Yuhan Liu, Nengkun Yu

papers.title: From Simple Sources to Quantum Advantage: Homomorphic Polynomial Transduction via Relative Decoding
papers.summary: Decoded quantum interferometry (DQI) and its Hamiltonian extension (HDQI) prepare states whose amplitudes are low-degree polynomials of an objective, using Fourier transforms and coherent decoding. We recast and generalize this approach as quantum state transduction through algebra homomorphisms. We transfer an efficiently preparable operator state of a degree-$D$ polynomial in a source Hamiltonian $H_A$ to the corresponding polynomial state of a target Hamiltonian $H_B=\pi(H_A)$, where $\pi$ is a unital $*$-homomorphism between the finite-dimensional source and target $C^*$-algebras. The transduction uses operator Fourier transforms and relative decoding to recover source operators rather than individual term-selection labels. The relative distance $d_{\mathrm{rel}}$ is the first degree at which source and target traces disagree. We prove that $2D<d_{\mathrm{rel}}$ is equivalent to preserving all inner products between degree-$D$ polynomials. Moreover, $d_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge d_{\mathrm{ord}}$, where $d_{\mathrm{ord}}$ is the ordinary distance used in (H)DQI, and we give families with $d_{\mathrm{ord}}=O(1)$ but $d_{\mathrm{rel}}=\Theta(n)$ and efficient decoders. Our framework replaces the complicated pilot state preparation by the more modular task of preparing a source polynomial state. DQI and HDQI arise as relation-free special cases. The framework accommodates nonuniform coefficients and noncommuting interactions and extends to fermionic and qudit systems, with applications to approximate optimization and Gibbs sampling. As evidence of advantages, for a nonlinear pairwise variant of optimal polynomial intersection where constant $d_{\mathrm{ord}}$ limits DQI-style preparations, relative decoding yields an ideal quantum score of 0.643 versus 0.606 for the best tested classical heuristic, a gap exceeding 3 percentage points.

authors.name: Zhong-Xia Shang, Daniel Stilck Fran\c{c}a

papers.title: Sublinear Copies Suffice for Fidelity Estimation with Pauli Measurements
papers.summary: We present the first worst-case, sublinear protocol to estimate the fidelity between a known target state and unknown lab-prepared state using Pauli basis measurements. More precisely, for $d$-dimensional states, we estimate the fidelity to $\pm \varepsilon$ using $o(d^{0.9675})/\varepsilon^2$ copies, which applies to all target states. Furthermore, our results establish improved guarantees for Pauli shadow tomography and Distributed Inner Product Estimation.

authors.name: Jayadev Acharya, Abhilash Dharmavarapu, Yuhan Liu, Nengkun Yu

papers.title: Energy-filtered readout preserves gap-enhanced sensing in interacting quantum dots
papers.summary: A small excitation gap makes a quantum dot a sensitive probe of a weak electric field, but the charge detector reading it can also excite it. We calculate how much of this enhancement survives continuous readout for two interacting electrons tuned through a confinement-driven crossover in a gate-defined dot. The probe is a few-level system read by a weakly coupled linear detector, with second-order transition rates and information from the mean detector current, for gaps up to a few hundred microelectronvolts, couplings up to 50 $\mu$eV and temperatures up to 100 mK. The outcome depends on the energy structure of the detector, not only its noise. A quantum point contact measures more strongly at higher bias but, once the bias energy exceeds the gap, also excites the probe; when this back-action dominates the relaxation of the probe, the optimised information rate grows only as the inverse of the gap. A sensor quantum dot with a narrow level instead reaches full strength at a bias below the gap, where a non-interacting detector cannot excite it at zero temperature. This energy-filtered readout keeps the inverse-square gap dependence of the quantum Fisher information down to gaps comparable to the level width of the detector or ten times the thermal energy. At the tested operating points, higher probe states change the sensitivities by up to 6% and the exponents by up to 0.06; coherence corrections to the populations and transduced signal are negligible, and any gain from the full detector record is unresolved within 1-2% numerical uncertainty. Under the same conditions the interacting pair gives about three times the information rate of a single electron with the same gap and detector, for contact and Coulomb-type interactions alike. The different gap dependences and optimal biases of the two detectors can be tested by bias and gate sweeps on charge-sensed double dots.

authors.name: Shirwan Abdullah

papers.title: Quantum Leakage from Shamir Sharing with Correlated Resources
papers.summary: We bound local quantum leakage from Shamir sharing uniformly over prime fields and permitted share-dependent channels. The adversary receives all outputs and a reference to a resource independent of the secret and sharing randomness. For independent device-reference pairs at fixed output dimension, we determine the exact exponent of the worst-case trace distance for two chosen secrets at every fixed reconstruction rate above one half, including its dependence on entanglement within each pair. For unentangled one-qubit leakage, this improves the sufficient rate of about $0.7334$ proved by Batra et al. Above one half, we also determine the exact exponent when an arbitrarily entangled support is tensored with single-device states elsewhere. Every fixed support fraction below the reconstruction rate gives exponential security, while a reconstruction set admits a known attack. Exponential security extends to fixed finite-memory processes with primitive transfer channels, fixed stationary chains satisfying upper operator mixing, and canonical primitive matrix product states, allowing arbitrary finite adversary extensions of the device marginal. For one-qubit outputs, fully separable resources and independent pairs whose joint output-reference states are positive under partial transpose for every share admit rates slightly below one half.

authors.name: Isaac Barouch Essayag (Yohananov), Aryeh Lev Zabokritskiy (Yohananov)

papers.title: A classical oracle separation between QMA and QMA(2)
papers.summary: We exhibit a classical oracle relative to which QMA \neq QMA(2). The separation is based on a separable Hamiltonian problem defined by signed edge constraints on a graph. The YES instances have zero-energy product states, while the NO instances, constructed using the antisymmetric subspace, have entangled zero-energy states but no low-energy product states. For the QMA lower bound, we use compressed-oracle techniques to track the information learned by a quantum computation making few queries to a YES instance. The key step is to map the resulting superpositions of partial oracle records to the NO family without significantly changing the verifier's behavior.

authors.name: Sabee Grewal, Saachi Mutreja, Kabir Tomer

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables II: NIP observables and the Todorcevic trichotomy
papers.summary: This is the second paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. For an observable of two independently prepared systems, Alice's and Bob's, we study its idealized responses: the expectation values of Alice's limiting preparations, as functions of Bob's preparations, which serve as probes, with Bob's system idealized first. We show that the observable is NIP, that is, no sequence of Alice's preparations lets Bob's probes realize every finite pattern of high and low values at a fixed positive gap, exactly when all idealized responses are of the first Baire class, pointwise limits of sequences of continuous functions; they then form a separable Rosenthal compactum. Because Alice can mix preparations, this compactum is convex, and hereditary separability forces it to be metrizable, so that NIP observables occupy three of the four topological classes defined by metrizability and Todor\v{c}evi\'c's trichotomy. Comparisons of photon numbers, of positions and of events in spacetime realize these three classes, and trees of preparations realize the seven minimal families of the Argyros--Dodos--Kanellopoulos heptachotomy. For the ferromagnetic transverse-field Ising model at positive temperature, the finite-volume magnetizations with offset longitudinal fields form a stable family when the spontaneous magnetization vanishes, and a family whose closure is first countable but not hereditarily separable when it does not.

authors.name: Eduardo Due\~nez, Jos\'e Iovino

papers.title: Magna: simulating magic state factories as cheaply as Clifford circuits
papers.summary: Classical simulation of magic state factories, including distillation, cultivation, and code switching, is challenging because of their substantial non-Clifford content. We introduce $\texttt{magna}$ (magic-state-factory assessment via global network algebra), a classical simulator that simulates such protocols as cheaply as Clifford circuits. $\texttt{magna}$ expresses the figures of merit of a protocol, namely the acceptance rate and the fidelity of the accepted states, as tensor networks, which it reduces globally by exploiting a structural correspondence with transversal gates on quantum codes. $\texttt{magna}$ further supports feedforward conditioned on arbitrary functions of mid-circuit measurement outcomes, including decoder outputs. We simulate Bravyi--Haah distillation with up to 100 output magic states at a cost that does not grow exponentially in the number of outputs, and achieve state-of-the-art sampling times for distance-5 magic state cultivation on both color codes and RP$^2$ surface codes. Finally, we validate nonlinear feedforward on a logical-level distillation protocol with 15 rounds of decoder-dependent feedforward. $\texttt{magna}$ aims to contribute to the key infrastructure for the large-scale evaluation and optimization of magic state factories.

authors.name: Yifei Wang, Yingfei Gu

papers.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
papers.summary: Coherent spin--photon interfaces for scalable quantum networks require bright optical transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent spin control. Donor spins in direct-bandgap semiconductors combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate coherent optical control of a single Cl donor electron spin in ZnSe. Resonant excitation reveals spin relaxation dynamics and measures spin coherence through coherent population trapping (CPT). Off-resonant ultrafast pulses are implemented to drive spin Rabi oscillations and demonstrate Ramsey interference. Multiple dark resonances in the CPT spectrum further reveal hyperfine coupling between the electron and the I=3/2 Cl nucleus. Together, these results demonstrate the first coherent optical control of a single donor electron spin in II--VI direct-bandgap semiconductors, establishing the essential components for exploiting optical donors in a scalable solid-state spin--photon platform.

authors.name: Yuxi Jiang, Amirehsan Alizadehherfati, Christine Falter, Jasvith R. Basani, Nils von den Driesch, Yurii Kutovyi, Jan Seelbinder, Alexander Pawlis, Edo Waks

papers.title: Analytic Solutions To Fully Quantized Parametric Amplification
papers.summary: We derive analytic expressions for observable dynamics under the fully quantized trilinear Hamiltonian, governing quantum three-wave mixing and parametric amplification. Starting from a coherent pump and vacuum signal and idler, the calculation reorganizes the Heisenberg expansion into resummed depletion and return profiles, yielding directly evaluable expressions for all 1st-, 2nd- and 3rd-order correlations. The construction uses no parametric approximation or fitted parameters. Representative numerical benchmarks show errors of order $10^{-12}$ throughout the entire pump depletion, and below $10^{-3}$ across dozens of depletion-and-back-conversion cycles, up to the first total collapse of the oscillation. The first-depletion treatment additionally provides 4th-order correlations, accommodates bright squeezed-pump inputs and reveals phenomena important to future optical quantum technologies. The framework can be extended to higher moments.

authors.name: Wanli Xing, Timothy C. Ralph

papers.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II
papers.summary: We confirm a conjecture of the first author [SODA'26] on a strong form of pseudo-telepathy for Khot's $d$-to-$1$ games: for every $d\geq 4$, every $\epsilon>0$, and every $k\in\mathbb N$, there is a $d$-to-$1$ label-cover game of classical value less than $\epsilon$ that admits a perfect quantum strategy using finite-dimensional shared entanglement with measurement contexts of radius at least $k$. As a consequence, there exist graphs whose quantum chromatic number $\chi_q$ is $3$ and whose classical chromatic number $\chi$ is arbitrarily large. This is the first super-exponential $\chi_q$ vs. $\chi$ gap, and it improves on the exponential lower bounds of Brassard, Cleve, and Tapp [Phys. Rev. Lett. '99], who produced graphs for which $\chi\geq 1.1397^{\chi_q}$, and Lalonde, who recently achieved $\chi\geq 1.1546^{\chi_q}$. To prove the conjecture, we proceed as follows. We start with a ``stretched'' version of the Mermin-Peres magic square, obtained by spacing out its equations and linking them with additional long equation wires. This operation increases the radius of the initial measurement contexts of a perfect quantum strategy for the game, while preserving classical unsatisfiability. We then apply parallel repetition to make the classical value small, and we turn the system into a pseudo-telepathic multi-layered Kneser hypergraph via a PCP construction of Dinur, Guruswami, Khot, and Regev [STOC'03]. Finally, we feed the resulting hypergraph into the reduction of Fei, Minzer, and Wang from hypergraph colouring to $4$-to-$1$ games, we establish quantum completeness of this reduction, and we show that it preserves context radius.

authors.name: Lorenzo Ciardo, Antoine Mottet

papers.title: Toric codes all the way down: decoupling translation-invariant topological CSS codes in higher dimensions
papers.summary: Topological Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) codes in more than two spatial dimensions offer features useful for fault-tolerant quantum computation, such as transversal non-Clifford gates and single-shot decoding, but a systematic understanding of them is still lacking. One approach is to decouple a code: map it to a stack of higher-form toric codes by a finite-depth local CSS-preserving Clifford circuit, possibly after adding ancillas. For translation-invariant $p$-ary CSS codes, where $p$ is prime ($p=2$ for qubits), we require the circuit to commute with the translations of a superlattice. In two dimensions, such a decoupling exists once these translations act trivially on every anyon type. In higher dimensions, excitations are sorted by their dimension into superselection layers, which can remain glued together even when translations act trivially on each layer. We show that this gluing is the only remaining obstruction: a code can be decoupled on a superlattice exactly when, after coarse-graining to it, translations act trivially on every layer and the gluing vanishes. Moreover, for a code with finitely many excitation types in each layer and $m$ nonzero layers, once translations act trivially on every layer, further coarse-graining by a factor of $p^{m-1}$ in every direction removes the aforementioned gluing. Physically, the same criterion determines when the code encodes the maximal number of logical qudits on a finite torus. Finally, we give an explicit algorithm that constructs the decoupling as a circuit of SUM (qudit CNOT) and SWAP gates.

authors.name: Mingxin He, Yifei Wang, Hao Song, Yingfei Gu

papers.title: Implications of the PXP ground-state sign structure for neural-network variational Monte Carlo
papers.summary: Positive-definite neural-network quantum states cannot directly represent the ground state of the PXP Hamiltonian, since the ground-state wavefunction carries a nontrivial relative-sign structure. Building on the chiral symmetry of the PXP Hamiltonian, we show that this sign structure is fixed exactly by the parity of the total up-spin number: a diagonal unitary transformation that assigns a sign to each spin configuration according to this parity maps the PXP Hamiltonian to its negative, rendering the transformed Hamiltonian stoquastic on the Rydberg-blockaded Hilbert space. Since the configuration graph of allowed configurations is connected, the Perron-Frobenius theorem guarantees a unique, strictly positive ground state of the transformed Hamiltonian, yielding an exact sign rule for the ground state of the original Hamiltonian in terms of the parity of the up-spin number. Variational Monte Carlo performed directly on the transformed Hamiltonian with a positive-definite ansatz therefore requires no architecture-specific modification to represent the true ground state. We evaluate the performance of this formulation using five representative neural-network quantum state architectures, SineKAN, reflection-symmetrized SineKAN, RBM, MLP, and LSTM, for different chain lengths.

authors.name: Jun Sur Richard Park, Kwangmin Yu

papers.title: Dynamical-mean-field cluster-correlation expansion of NV$^-$ spin-echo decoherence in a realistic substitutional-nitrogen bath
papers.summary: The Hahn-echo time $T_2$ of nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) ensembles in nitrogen-rich diamond follows the empirical relation $T_2\cdot$[N] = 160 $\mu$s ppm, and this relation does not depend on the magnetic field between 2 and 30 mT. Cluster-correlation-expansion (CCE) calculations solve the spin dynamics exactly within small groups of spins. When they treat the Overhauser field of the surrounding P1 centres, that is, the field that these electron spins produce, as frozen, they overestimate $T_2$ at high field by up to a factor of two. This excess was recently attributed to additional dark defects. We show that the excess comes mostly from the frozen field. In our model the P1 centres outside each cluster flip-flop in pairs: two centres exchange their spin states and conserve their total $S_z$. Kinetic Monte Carlo generates these events at golden-rule rates, which follow from the dipolar Hamiltonian without adjustable parameters, and each cluster evolves in the resulting time-dependent field. This dynamical mean field lies between the static-mean-field and mean-field-free limits. For a $^{14}$N P1 bath it reduces $T_2\cdot$[N] at 30 mT from 264 $\pm$ 16 to 188 $\pm$ 12 $\mu$s ppm and gives 167 $\pm$ 11 $\mu$s ppm at 10 mT, 1.7 and 0.4 standard deviations from experiment, with no dark spins. When each centre jumps independently, $T_2\cdot$[N] is 147 $\pm$ 9 $\mu$s ppm at 30 mT; the correlation of the flip-flop partners thus lengthens $T_2$ by 20-30 percent at high field. The Overhauser field is neither frozen nor averaged out by fast motion: 68-83 percent of its autocorrelation survives 200 $\mu$s. At 2.5 mT, where the P1 electron and nucleus hybridise, $T_2$ stays below experiment for any choice of rates. Part of the field dependence therefore remains: $T_2$ rises by a factor 1.69 $\pm$ 0.07 instead of 2.15 $\pm$ 0.08 from 2.5 to 30 mT.

authors.name: Chikara Shinei

papers.title: Quantum Noise Spectroscopy of Criticality in an Atomically Thin Magnet
papers.summary: The universality class of a phase transition dictates the behavior of low-frequency and long-wavelength critical fluctuations in a material. Studying these dynamics in thin magnetic insulators, however, remains challenging; an experimental probe must be sensitive to low-frequency, long-wavelength fluctuations while navigating the sample's small volume, inherent inhomogeneities, and fabrication limitations. Using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond, we demonstrate T$_2$ (spin-decoherence) noise magnetometry as a direct and quantitative probe of critical dynamics in a tri-layer sample of CrSBr, a two-dimensional van der Waals magnet. We observe a sharp increase in the decoherence rate of the NV spin ensemble at the sample's critical temperature, highlighting our probe's sensitivity to critical fluctuations. We demonstrate that the behavior of the NV spin decoherence rate below the critical temperature is inconsistent with fluctuations due to XY criticality in 2D CrSBr. Next, by simulating the NV spin decoherence dynamics using noise models for an Ising-type transition and fitting to our data, we quantitatively measure the dynamical and the correlation length critical exponents ($z$ and $\nu$) and demonstrate that the observed fluctuations strongly deviate from those predicted by the short-range Ising universality class. Together, these observations indicate that the transition is Ising-like but modified by long-range dipolar interactions, emphasizing the importance of easy-axis anisotropy and long-range interactions for understanding magnetism in 2D CrSBr. Our work establishes T$_2$ noise magnetometry as a quantitative probe of critical dynamics in 2D materials, opening a new avenue for studying strongly correlated phenomena at the atomically thin limit.

authors.name: Mark E. Ziffer, Francisco Machado, Benedikt Ursprung, Artur Lozovoi, Aya Batoul Tazi, Zhiyang Yuan, Michael E. Ziebel, Tom Delord, Nanyu Zeng, Evan Telford, Daniel G. Chica, Dane W. deQuilettes, Xiaoyang Zhu, James C. Hone, Kenneth L. Shepard, Xavier Roy, Nathalie P. de Leon, Emily J. Davis, Carlos A. Meriles, Jonathan S. Owen, P. James Schuck, Shubhayu Chatterjee, Abhay N. Pasupathy

papers.title: Variational formulae for entropy-like functionals for states in von Neumann algebras
papers.summary: The paper presents variational formulae for entropy-like functionals, including Segal and R\'enyi entropies, for normal states on semifinite von Neumann algebras. The considered functionals are of the form $\tau(f(h))$ where $\tau$ is a normal faithful semifinite trace on this algebra, $h$ is a positive selfadjoint operator from $L^1(\mathscr{M},\tau)$, and $f$ is an appropriate convex or concave function. The results cover both finite and semifinite algebras, and the obtained formulae generalise known results, in particular, those concerning relative entropy. Moreover, the connection between quantum entropies and the structure of abelian subalgebras is highlighted, providing new interpretations in the context of quantum information theory.

authors.name: Andrzej {\L}uczak, Hanna Pods\k{e}dkowska, Rafa{\l} Wieczorek

papers.title: Second law of thermodynamics in closed quantum many-body systems
papers.summary: The second law of thermodynamics for adiabatic operations -- constraints on state transitions in closed systems under external control -- is one of the fundamental principles of thermodynamics. On the other hand, it is recently established that even pure quantum states can represent thermal equilibrium. However, pure quantum states do not satisfy the second law in that they are not passive, i.e., work can be extracted from them if arbitrary unitary operations are allowed. It therefore remains unresolved how quantum mechanics can be reconciled with thermodynamics. Here, based on our key quantum-mechanical notions of thermal equilibrium and adiabatic operations, we address the emergence of the second law for adiabatic operations in the thermodynamics limit. We first introduce infinite-observable macroscopic thermal equilibrium (iMATE); a quantum state, including pure states, is in iMATE if the expectation values of all additive observables agree with their equilibrium values. We also introduce a macroscopic operation as unitary evolution generated by a time-dependent additive Hamiltonian, which is regarded as corresponding to adiabatic operations. Employing these concepts, we show that no extensive work can be extracted from any quantum state in iMATE through any macroscopic operations. Furthermore, we introduce a quantum-mechanical form of entropy density such that it agrees with thermodynamic entropy density for any quantum state in iMATE. We then prove that for any initial state in iMATE, this entropy density cannot be decreased by any macroscopic operations, followed by a time-independent relaxation process. Our theory thus proves two different forms of the second law, by adopting macroscopically reasonable classes of observables, equilibrium states, and operations. We also discuss the time scales of macroscopic operations in these results.

authors.name: Yuuya Chiba, Yasushi Yoneta, Ryusuke Hamazaki, Akira Shimizu

papers.title: Emergent thermal fluctuations and non-Hermitian phase transitions in open photon condensates
papers.summary: Driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein condensates of photons in optical resonators have been shown theoretically to exist as a long-lived, yet metastable state stabilized by a ghost attractor, despite continuous driving [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 053402 (2025)]. Here we analyze the properties of this metastable condensate as well as the relaxation dynamics into and out of this state by means of the Lindblad master-equation approach, treating the condensate and the equal-time, noncondensed fluctuations on the same footing. Despite its nonequilibrium origin, the quasistationary condensate exhibits thermal behavior in that the order-parameter fluctuations scale with system size as in thermodynamic equilibrium, and the photon-number distribution in multimode resonators is in excellent agreement with a Bose-Einstein distribution. A linear stability analysis further reveals the presence of several exceptional points, resulting in multiple non-Hermitian phase transitions associated with the relaxation dynamics into and out of the metastable condensate. These behaviors reconcile apparently contradictory experimental results.

authors.name: Moritz Janning, Roman Kramer, Aya Abouelela, Michael Turaev, Sayak Ray, Johann Kroha

papers.title: Relativistic Quantum Chaos in Neutrino Billiards
papers.summary: Neutrino billiards serve as a model system for the study of aspects of relativistic quantum chaos. These are relativistic quantum billiards consisting of a spin-1/2 particle which is confined to a planar domain by imposing boundary conditions on the spinor components which were proposed in [Berry and Mondragon, {\it Proc. R. Soc.} A {\bf 412}, 53 (1987)]. We review their general features and the properties of neutrino billiards with shapes of billiards with integrable dynamics. Furthermore, we review the features of two neutrino billiards with the shapes of billiards generating a chaotic dynamics, whose nonrelativistic counterpart exhibits particular properties. Finally we briefly discuss possible experimental realizations of relativistic quantum billiards based on graphene billiards, that is, finite-size sheets of graphene.

authors.name: Barbara Dietz

papers.title: Semiclassical resonances under local magnetic fields
papers.summary: We study resonances for the semiclassical magnetic Laplacian in the full plane with a compactly supported magnetic field in the framework of semiclassical complex scaling and black box scattering theory. Assuming that the magnetic field is locally constant, we prove the existence of semiclassical resonances near the Landau levels with exponentially small imaginary parts. We also prove that resonances emerge from a magnetic step discontinuity along a curved interface or a non-degenerate magnetic well, and in the vicinity of anharmonic Landau levels if the field has an isolated zero.

authors.name: Pavel Exner, Ayman Kachmar

papers.title: Hidden weak-pairing superconductivity of non-interacting anyons obeying 1/3 statistics
papers.summary: We show that a non-interacting gas of charge-$e/3$ anyons with exchange statistics $\theta=-\pi/3$ can superconduct through a hidden weak-pairing mechanism. Such an anyon gas arises naturally in doped fractional Chern insulators at filling $1/3$ or $2/3$, where projective lattice translations enforce three degenerate anyon pockets. Exploiting this three-pocket structure, we develop a flux-attachment construction in which the average statistical flux vanishes, thereby mapping the problem to three species of composite fermions (CFs) in zero effective magnetic field. We show that the anyon statistics itself, encoded in statistical gauge field fluctuations, supplies the pairing glue and drives the CFs into a $p-\mathrm{i}p$ paired state, which corresponds to a $f-\mathrm{i}f$ physical superconductor. The CF strong-pairing phase is adiabatically connected to Laughlin's picture of anyon superconductivity, where charge-$e/3$ anyons bind into charge-$2e/3$ molecules, which then lead to superconductivity. By contrast, the more natural weak-pairing phase of CFs realizes a distinct superconducting phase - its edge is characterized by a chiral central charge $c_-=-1/2$, in contrast to the prediction of integer $c_-$ for the anyon superconductor based on Laughlin's picture, thereby resolving the discrepancy between previous theories and recent numerical results. Our theory provides a natural framework for understanding superconductivity near fractional Chern insulators, as observed in recent experiments. Finally, we discuss extensions of our theory that predict new chiral superconductors adjacent to FCIs at other fillings.

authors.name: Zheng-Duo Fan, Ashvin Vishwanath, Zijian Wang

papers.title: Complexity of tensor network simulation for noisy quantum circuits
papers.summary: We aim to rigorously address how local noise affects the classical simulability of quantum dynamics benchmarked by tensor-network methods. Using operator entanglement entropy (OEE) as a unifying criterion, we prove the following: (1) For single-qubit depolarizing noise, geometry-independent $\order{1}$-layer and $\Theta(\log n)$-layer thresholds for fixed absolute and relative Hilbert--Schmidt error are established, beyond which polynomial bond dimension suffices; on 1D local circuits with a product initial input, whole-trajectory MPO approximations are constructed at fixed purified distance with $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ bond dimension. (2) For general single-qubit noise, we identify sufficient contractivity conditions for MPO approximations with constant bond dimension, in both the average and worst cases. (3) We further extend the above results to higher dimensions, yielding $\mathrm{poly}(n)$ average boundary-bond dimensions for projected entangled pair operators (PEPO) across every cut. Our results establish a rigorous connection between certain noise models, circuit types, and their classical simulability.

authors.name: Yuguo Shao, Zishuo Zhao, Song Cheng, Zhengwei Liu

papers.title: Quantum estimates for classical polynomial optimization
papers.summary: The problem of finding lower and upper bounds on multivariate homogeneous polynomials is both difficult and important given its applications to questions ranging from dynamical stability in complex potential landscapes to data analysis. From the standpoint of tensor eigenvalue theory, the question is equivalent to finding the smallest and the largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor corresponding to the given polynomial. Standard approaches outlined in the literature amount to running nonlinear iterations in search for the optimal rays along which the growth of the polynomial is fastest or slowest. Unlike the case of matrices (or their corresponding multivariate quadratic forms) convergence of such algorithms for higher-rank tensors is capricious due to the complex topography of polynomial objective functions. In this essay, a very different strategy, inspired by quantum-mechanical variational methods, is introduced for finding bounds on polynomials. The original polynomial is replaced by an operator acting in a suitably chosen (large) space of states, such that in an appropriate "classical" limit this operator approaches the original polynomial expression made of commutative variables. As a result, approximating the smallest and largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor, and thus finding bounds on polynomials, amounts to diagonalizing the resulting quantum operator, represented as a large matrix, and then inspecting the smallest and largest eigenvalues of this matrix. This approach is then successfully applied to standard test examples from tensor eigenvalue literature and other problems of interest in mathematical physics including Strichartz-type inequalities.

authors.name: Oleg Evnin

papers.title: A hybrid quantum-classical neural network for learning to route
papers.summary: This work studies hybrid quantum-classical neural networks for learning routing heuristics. Specifically, this paper asks whether small quantum neural networks can replace parameter-heavy modules inside a competitive attention-based routing model while maintaining solution quality. For the capacitated vehicle routing problem, encoder feed-forward replacement emerges as the most promising design: it reduces the number of model parameters by 56.6% while keeping the hybrid model close to the classical neural baseline at small and medium instance sizes, although the gap grows for larger instances. This work also compares to classical routing algorithms, which remain highly competitive and often superior on the fixed Euclidean test sets. Our results therefore do not indicate quantum advantage or solver dominance, but identify encoder feed-forward replacement as a viable hybrid-module compression strategy for neural combinatorial optimization.

authors.name: Marcus Rolf Peter Ritt, Alexsandro Santos da Rosa J\'unior, Marcos Vinicius Reballo, Cesar Augusto do Amaral, Fernando Augusto Caletti de Barros

papers.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
papers.summary: This is the third paper in a series that reads the dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory as properties of bipartite quantum observables. Here we study simplicity through two countable structures with simple unstable theories: the Rado graph, and the symplectic space of labels of Pauli strings of finite support, in which addition records the products of the strings and the symplectic form records their commutation. In the second structure, forking characterizes the logical errors of stabilizer codes: an error undetectable by the checks of a code is logical exactly when its type over the stabilizer labels and a complete set of logical-operator labels forks over the stabilizer labels, and the independence theorem becomes a rule for gluing syndromes. A two-valued relation between countable sets of labels defines a diagonal bipartite observable, whose real-valued theory describes Alice's probability mixtures of labels and their expected responses at Bob's probes. Mixing changes the classification: if the relation has the independence property, this theory has the tree property of the second kind. For the observable of the symplectic form, actual mixtures of checks witness this property for the response itself; for the observable of the Rado graph, every array that witnesses it for a quantifier-free formula in Bob's probe contains idealized preparations, which lie outside the original structure.

authors.name: Eduardo Due\~{n}ez, Jos\'{e} Iovino

papers.title: Three-dimensional QCA that are not stably circuits
papers.summary: We prove that the three-dimensional chiral $\Z_p$ Clifford quantum cellular automata of Haah and of Sun--Yang--Wang--Tantivasadakarn--Chen are, for every odd prime $p$, not finite-depth quantum circuits, even after tensoring with arbitrary ancillary degrees of freedom and composing with translations. Previously such statements were known only inside the Clifford category. As a consequence, the group of three-dimensional QCA modulo stabilized circuits and translations is not finitely generated. The key ingredient is a new invariant of invertible subalgebras, which we conjecture to be the square of the total quantum dimension of the hosted anyon theory, modulo rational squares.

authors.name: Bowen Yang

papers.title: Quasicrystals are Functionally Graded Materials
papers.summary: Quasicrystals exhibit long-range order without translational periodicity, posing challenges to compute their electronic properties. Here we show that a quasicrystal can be represented exactly as a periodic approximant with a spatially graded phason, establishing a connection to functionally graded materials. Building on this connection, we develop a controlled quantum theory of quasicrystals. We derive a state-dependent control parameter governed by the quantum metric of local Bloch states, determining when finite approximations are reliable. We further construct a Hamiltonian that correctly predicts Bragg gap positions, quasimomentum equivalence, and quasiperiodic eigenstates to all orders in phason strain within a finite Fourier window. We verify the theory numerically and propose a diffraction-based experimental test of the gap shift induced by phason strain. Our framework opens a route to predicting the electronic structure and functional properties of quasicrystals using methods developed for functionally graded materials.

authors.name: Michael J. Landry, Dominic Bollettieri, Akhil Sadam, Denisse C\'ordova Carrizales, Mingda Li

papers.title: Resonantly interacting $2e/3$ anyons: a controlled microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity
papers.summary: We develop a microscopic theory of anyon superconductivity that connects electronic interactions in a lightly doped Laughlin state to the universal physics of a resonantly interacting anyon gas. Using geometric quantization of Laughlin quasiholes, we derive the effective many-body Hamiltonian of dilute charge-$2e/3$ anyons, including their valley structure, dispersion, and statistical and short-range interactions, together with an explicit map between anyon and electron observables. This reduces the dilute many-body problem to a few parameters fixed by data computable from few anyon numerics. In analogy with resonant Fermi and Bose gases, we organize the dilute anyon problem around a two-body binding resonance and its relevant and marginal perturbations. For a three-valley gas of charge-$2e/3$ anyons, we identify a resonance whose long-distance theory is governed by an Aharonov-Casher anyon Hamiltonian whose magnetic field is the statistical Chern-Simons field and whose ground state is exactly solvable. Using the ground state wavefunction, we demonstrate Cooper-pair off-diagonal long-range order directly in electron coordinates and determine the pairing symmetry and vortex-lattice structure. The leading perturbations at the fixed point are a relevant pair detuning and a marginal three-body contact in the valley-singlet channel, which determine the compressibility and sound velocity. A repulsive three-body coupling is marginally irrelevant, allowing the fixed point to control a parametrically broad dilute regime near pair resonance, while attractive three-body interactions instead generate charge-$2e$ trimers. More broadly, our results show that binding thresholds between competing anyon composites host universal resonant regimes that are not captured by the lowest-energy anyon species alone, providing a new setting for controlled theories of anyon matter.

authors.name: Qingchen Li, Pavel A. Nosov, Zhaoyu Han, Si-Yuan Chen, Taige Wang, Eslam Khalaf

papers.title: Classification and Signatures of Dissipative Quantum Hall-Superconductor Junctions
papers.summary:
Fractional quantum Hall (FQH) edges with proximity-induced superconductivity can host parafermionic zero modes (PZMs), making them a promising platform for topological quantum computing. Recent experiments [G"ul et al., Phys. Rev. X 12, 021057 (2022)] measured the edge conductance from crossed Andreev reflection (CAR) between counter-propagating FQH edges separated by a narrow superconductor. The observed conductance was small and non-quantized, with two distinct behaviors: some states show temperature-independent conductance, while others show conductance that grows as temperature decreases. We explain these results by dissipation to sub-gap modes in the superconductor and present a phase diagram for the FQH-superconductor junction. We show that for Jain states, temperature-independent non-quantized conductance occurs only in the presence of an integer mode (such as at filling $
u=1\pm rac{1}{m}$, with odd $m\geq3$) strongly coupled to the dissipative channel. The predicted temperature trends qualitatively agree with the experiment, which shows temperature-independent conductance for $
u=2/3$ and integer states, but not for $
u=1/3$ and $
u=2/5$. We propose comparing $
u=4/3$ and $2/3$ to test the predicted influence of the relative chirality of integer and fractional modes.

authors.name: Evgenii Zheltonozhskii, Barak A. Katzir, Yuval Oreg, Erez Berg, Netanel H. Lindner

papers.title: Bypass Transition via the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect
papers.summary: Non-Hermitian skin lattices can directionally amplify propagating signals. Here we show that this amplification and nonlinear feedback together drive a bypass transition to self-sustained motion, familiar from shear flows. A finite local excitation can trigger sustained periodic or chaotic motion while the resting state remains linearly stable. We develop a return-map theory that predicts the triggering threshold, its scaling with directional gain, and the instability governing near-critical dynamics. The threshold decreases exponentially with chain length. Weak noise triggers sustained motion as well, with a characteristic ignition length that grows logarithmically as noise weakens at fixed observation time. Our work establishes a skin-effect route to bypass transitions, opening a new avenue for predicting and controlling nonlinear wave dynamics.

authors.name: Konghao Sun, Haiping Hu

papers.title: DefectSkills: Guiding AI agents through first-principles calculations for point defects in semiconductors and insulators
papers.summary: First-principles defect calculations can now be performed autonomously by AI agents, enabled by established computational methods and open-source Python toolkits. However, reliable and repeatable defect calculations require clear scientific and technical guidance that helps agents resolve ambiguities and avoid errors in calculation setup, execution, postprocessing, and analysis. Here, we present DefectSkills, a set of structured prompts that provides human-in-the-loop guidance to AI agents performing first-principles calculations of point defects in semiconductors and insulators using the Vienna Ab initio Simulation Package (VASP). The prompts encode human expertise and guide agents through unit-cell relaxation, electronic-structure and dielectric calculations, phase-stability and chemical-potential analysis, charged-defect supercell generation and calculations, finite-size corrections, formation-energy calculations and thermodynamic analysis, and data backup. By packaging this expertise as reusable agent skills, DefectSkills supports consistent workflow execution across agentic AI systems and reproducible defect calculations.

authors.name: Zhenkun Yuan, Yizhi Zhu, Geoffroy Hautier

papers.title: Medial Model of Elastic Curve Contacts, from Clasps to Knits
papers.summary: Materials constructed from interlocking and tangled fibers are challenging to model and understand due in part to the complex interplay between fiber shape and contact mechanics. Much of our intuition about contact mechanics comes from the Hertzian description, which is based on interactions between convex bodies. However, fibers often form clasp shapes, which involve saddle-shaped contact surfaces; the ability for two interacting bodies to conform to each other along a saddle surface confounds many existing mechanical contact models. Following an observation that contact surfaces between fibers tend to look like minimal, constant mean-curvature surfaces, we seek to test this hypothesis and provide a direct link to geometric modeling methods. To do this, we leverage the medial axis transformation, which generalizes the notion of a Voronoi tessellation to generating curves and surfaces. Through computational studies on an orthogonal clasp and a simple knit structure, we find that the medial axis transformation provides a reasonable model for contact surfaces between identical curves. We also show that a generalization of the medial axis transformation based on radical Voronoi tessellations can be used to well-approximate contact surfaces between non-identical curves. We apply this ``radical axis transform'' to curves of different radii and demonstrate a trend for surfaces to adopt finite mean curvature. Our results may point the way towards more sophisticated geometric methods for modeling tangles.

authors.name: Kathryn Chain, Haoye Sun, Michael S. Dimitriyev

papers.title: Ni ordering in the van der Waals gap of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$: from disorder through $2\times2$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order to stripe order
papers.summary: We report a synchrotron x-ray diffraction study of Ni-intercalated 2H-NbS$_2$ over the range $0.18 \le x \le 0.57$, with Ni contents measured by energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy. Powder diffraction on the whole series shows that the NbS$_2$ host is preserved, while the Ni ions in the van der Waals gap evolve from a disordered arrangement to $2\times2$ order at $x=1/4$ and $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order at $x=1/3$, through a range where both motifs coexist, to an orthorhombic stripe-type order at $x=0.57$. The in-plane lattice parameter increases with Ni content, whereas the interlayer spacing remains nearly constant except for a pronounced minimum at $x=1/4$, which density-functional calculations reproduce for the ordered structure. Single-crystal diffraction on the two commensurate phases shows that the $x=1/4$ structure, with Ni on a single site and a trimerized Nb lattice, is free of stacking faults, whereas the chiral $x=1/3$ structure contains Ni on the nominally empty site, inversion twins and stacking faults of the Ni layers. The comparison between powders and crystals shows that grinding mainly degrades the stacking of the Ni layers. These results establish the structural phase diagram of Ni$_x$NbS$_2$ and the intercalant disorder to be taken into account in the interpretation of its magnetic properties.

authors.name: Naveen Singh Dhami, Ricardo Guillermo Torres Ramirez, Gaurav Pransu, Ivo Batisti\'c, Pierre Fertey, Erik Elkaim, El-Eulmi Bendeif, Bruno Gudac, Nikolina Peni\'c, Naveen Kumar Chogondahalli Muniraju, Neven Bari\v{s}i\'c, Petar Pop\v{c}evi\'c, Victor Bal\'edent

papers.title: Topological localization in unentangled random braids
papers.summary: In 2015, P. Serna, G. Bunin, and A. Nahum numerically investigated fluctuations in a bunch of unentangled random threads. They showed that fluctuations of an individual thread in a braid are qualitatively different from those of a thread embedded in a medium of fixed parallel lines. In particular, Serna et al. observed a logarithmic increase in the average transverse span, $\left$, of a thread with polymer length, $N$. This behavior highlights the collective nature of topological interactions, in which each polymer fluctuates and constrains the motion of the others. Studying this problem both numerically and analytically, we propose the following interpretation: the logarithmic regime is transient, and sufficiently long polymers exhibit topological localization, where $\left$ approaches a finite limit at $N\to\infty$. Unlike localization induced by quenched external disorder, this phenomenon arises solely from collective topological constraints. We study braids within a locally free approximation and support the localization by analytical investigation of Brownian bridges on the asymptotic Cayley graph of a locally free group. We further conjecture that topologically induced localization emerges as a phase transition: for a small number of threads, $n \sim 2\div 5$, the span, $\left$, grows algebraically, with the usual scaling $\left\sim N^{1/4}$ at $N\gg 1$; by contrast, for sufficiently large $n$, each thread in a long braid ($N\gg 1$) asymptotically localizes, approaching $\left\sim \mathrm{const}$.

authors.name: Daniil Fedotov, Pieter Hendrik Willem Van Der Hoek, Sergei Nechaev

papers.title: Shock-driven Jetting at HMX Crystal Surface Asperities
papers.summary: Shock-induced jetting and recompression are plausible mechanisms for hot spot formation in energetic materials, but remain poorly understood. To this end, we apply all-atom nonreactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of a shock-loaded sinusoidal surface asperity in the crystalline explosive HMX (octahydro-1,3,5,7-tetranitro-1,3,5,7-tetrazocine) to quantify the roles of shock strength, asperity geometry, system size, and crystallographic orientation in determining the jetting response. Our simulations span a shock pressure interval of $\approx$4-47 GPa, which captures responses in both detonation initiation and steady-state detonation regimes. We find that shock strength and asperity curvature exert strong influence on jet velocity, temperature, and morphology, while feature size and crystallographic orientation play more modest roles. Jet morphology correlates strongly with the HMX ambient-pressure phase diagram and the narrow temperature range associated with its liquid phase. Coherent jets form when focusing and dissipation are sufficient to drive local temperatures above the melting point, while formation of molecular plumes is seemingly connected to jet temperatures exceeding the liquid-vapor transition temperature. Formation of plumes is unlike the jetting responses seen in metals, which typically exhibit liquid phases that are stable over wider temperature intervals. This work proposes a simple hypothesis for the connection between jet morphology and ambient-pressure phase diagrams that can be readily tested in other explosives and metals. It also provides a foundation for ongoing nonreactive and reactive MD simulations of jet impact and recompression to quantify the role played by jets in forming hot spots in HMX-based explosives.

authors.name: Ethan Holbrook, Matthew P. Kroonblawd, H. Keo Springer, Alejandro Strachan

papers.title: Predictions of superconducting properties from chemical bonding interactions
papers.summary: The need for rapid estimates of superconducting critical temperatures, Tc s, is becoming increasingly urgent as first-principles and artificial intelligence based methods enable the exploration of ever-larger and more chemically complex materials spaces. In this context, chemical bonding based quantities have emerged as promising descriptors for predicting superconductivity. To date, these approaches have mainly been developed for hydride superconductors, notably through the networking value, a descriptor based upon the electron localization function, whose topological properties have been found to correlate with Tc . In this perspective, we review and consolidate the method's theory, and we discuss how the estimate of the Tc is achievable within a real-space view. We conclude by proposing a framework that enables Tc prediction for the broad family of conventional superconductors from easily computable intermediate physical quantities.

authors.name: Francesco Belli, Trinidad Novoa, Ion Errea, Eva Zurek

papers.title: Atomic-Scale Phonon Engineering for Enhanced Thermal Transport in Wafer-Scale-Bonded $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC Heterostructures
papers.summary: Bonding semiconductors to substrates with high thermal conductivity is a promising way to solve the heat-dissipation problem of materials that transport heat poorly, and it avoids the lattice-matching constraints of conventional epitaxy. However, the lattice mismatch remains, leaving the two materials with mismatched phonon states, while poor interface quality scatters phonons even more. Together, these effects block phonon transport across the bonded interface and make interfacial thermal resistance a critical bottleneck, calling for careful interface engineering. Here, $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC serves as a model system for a phonon-bridging strategy. A nanoscale crystalline Si interlayer is designed and fabricated by wafer bonding to bridge the mismatched phonon states of $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ and SiC. Spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy and molecular dynamics simulations show that this Si layer opens new channels for phonon transport across the interface. The engineered interface raises the interfacial thermal conductance to 165 MW m$^{-2}$ K$^{-1}$ -- the highest value yet reported for $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$/SiC interfaces. These results offer an effective way to manage heat in $\beta$-Ga$_{2}$O$_{3}$ devices and point to a general approach for building phonon-bridging interfaces that improve heat dissipation in heterogeneous systems.

authors.name: J. Liu, R. Mao, Z. Liu, Y. Yin, S. Li, F. Sun, B. Liu, Z. Wang, P. Gao

papers.title: Gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave source limited by thermal noise
papers.summary: Josephson junctions are compact on-chip sources of coherent microwave and terahertz radiation, but conventional radiators couple the emission frequency, output power and dissipation through a single bias voltage. Here we demonstrate a gate-reconfigurable Josephson microwave radiator based on a graphene weak link integrated with a separately gated graphene shunt resistor. The bias voltage sets the Josephson frequency, while the local gates tune the Josephson current and the total device resistance, enabling electrostatic control of emitted power at a chosen frequency. The device resolves Josephson harmonics up to fourth order, and its radiation power scales with source current and impedance as expected from a lumped-element circuit model. We further show that the emission linewidth is quantitatively described by Johnson-Nyquist noise at the electron temperature. The linewidth therefore provides an on-chip thermometer under bias, with the resistance-dependent heating captured by a minimal heat-balance model based on Wiedemann-Franz diffusion and electron-phonon coupling.

authors.name: Jayeon Kim, Seong Jang, Seunghan Lee, Dongsung T. Park, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Gil-Ho Lee

papers.title: Ferroelectricity and Peierls transition in MOI$_2$ (M=Ta, Nb): a first-principle analysis
papers.summary: The van der Waals ferroelectric NbOI$_2$ hosts a polar distortion that is commonly attributed to the Peierls dimerization of its Nb chains. Here we show, using first-principles calculations and a Landau-type energy, that the polar instability is in fact a distinct order parameter that does not stem from the Peierls mode condensation and that three main distinct modes are important in the whole MOI$_2$ family. They are a polar mode $P$, an antipolar mode $\eta$, and a Peierls mode $\delta$, whose stabilities and couplings strongly depend on the nature of the $M$ metal element, as evidenced by the fact that the isostructural, TaOI$_2$ system is not polar while possessing Peirls distortions.

authors.name: Carmel Dansou, Charles Paillard, Laurent Bellaiche

papers.title: Interplay between Spin Stripes and Pairing Crossover in the Bilayer Hubbard Model
papers.summary: Whether $d$-wave or $s_\pm$-wave pairing prevails in the bilayer nickelate \ce{La3Ni2O7} remains unresolved, and how its observed spin order and magnetic excitations relate to the pairing mechanism is unclear. Here, we use finite-temperature determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations of a minimal bilayer Hubbard model to investigate pairing competition at strong interlayer coupling, where intralayer and interlayer antiferromagnetic correlations have comparable strengths. We find that spin stripes develop spontaneously with increasing hole doping, accompanied by a crossover of the dominant pairing symmetry from $d$-wave to $s_\pm$-wave. The crossover tracks the changing relative strengths of the spin correlations, with the interlayer correlations overtaking their intralayer counterparts in magnitude. Concomitantly, the dynamical spin structure factor exhibits a momentum-dependent reorganization of the magnetic excitations, consistent with fluctuating spin stripes. Our results identify the structure of spin fluctuations as a key link between spin stripes and pairing competition, offering a minimal-model perspective for understanding \ce{La3Ni2O7}.

authors.name: Zixuan Jia, Xuelei Sui, Shijie Hu, Tianxing Ma, Haiqing Lin, Bing Huang

papers.title: Neural Networks with Exciton-Polariton Waveguides
papers.summary: We propose and numerically study a scheme for neural networks using exciton-polariton waveguide meshes. These enable arbitrary programmable interlayer couplings suited to a restricted Boltzmann machine architecture where polariton phases act as stochastic network variables. We show that such a network can be trained using unsupervised Hebbian and anti-Hebbian updates. This allows the implementation of an associative memory, where the network recovers learned patterns from imperfect inputs.

authors.name: Huawen Xu, Ruiqi Bao, Lingyu Tian, Yusong Gan, Junfeng Gao, Michal Matuszewski, Qihua Xiong, Timothy Liew

papers.title: Floquet-Volkov spin polarization in spin-degenerate Antiferromagnets
papers.summary: Periodic driving enables ultrafast control of electronic structures in solids through the formation of photon-dressed Floquet-Bloch states. However, the measured photoemission spectra are influenced not only by these states but also by their interference with Volkov-dressed outgoing photoelectrons. Here, we demonstrate that Floquet-Volkov interference can generate spin-polarized photoemission in a collinear antiferromagnetic Dirac model without spin-orbit coupling (SOC). An in-plane linearly polarized pump preserves $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetry, leaving the Floquet quasienergies spin degenerate. Under near-resonant driving, photon-dressed conduction and valence bands hybridize, producing spin-dependent relative phases that are converted into unequal spin-resolved photoemission intensities through interference between pathways reaching the same Volkov-dressed final state. We analytically identify this interference mechanism and verify it using nonequilibrium Green-function calculations under periodic driving and finite pump-probe pulses. We further demonstrate that rotating the probe polarization can suppress or reverse the spin polarization without modifying the Floquet bands. Our findings establish Floquet-Volkov interference as a route to spin-selective photoemission in driven antiferromagnets without Floquet spin splitting or SOC.

authors.name: Jiyang Fan, Dinghui Wang, Tongshuai Zhu

papers.title: Temperature-Dependent Ion Dynamics in Argyrodite Superionic Conductor Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl with Fine-Tuned MACE Foundation Model
papers.summary: The rapid growth of machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP), particularly the foundational models for materials chemistry, such as MACE, has significantly strengthened our capabilities in studying the complex dynamics of materials through statistical sampling. Here, by performing molecular dynamics with a fine-tuned MACE model, that are further combined with essential dynamics analysis, a tool that is commonly applied in (bio)molecular simulations, we examine the temperature-dependent ion dynamics in a prototypical inorganic solid superionic conductor, namely argyrodite Li$_{6}$PS$_{5}$Cl. Our analyses show clear localised phonon-like dynamics for Li$^+$ ions below 500 K with trajectories lying in a low-dimensional manifold that is highly nonlinear, which is opposite to the case in the high-temperature ($\sim$800 K) end. Between 500-700 K, the system exhibit strong competition in the dynamics between the Li$^+$ and framework ions, that are reflected in both the eigenspectrum and the projected low-dimensional embeddings characterising these dynamics not showing a simple monotonic dependency upon rising temperatures, and is further supported by investigations employing Langevin dynamics that systematically examine how damping the framework motions affects the dynamics of the Li$^+$ ions, thanks to the computational efficiency provided by MLIP. This work thus contributes towards the broader theoretical and data-driven framework for studying the lattice dynamics of solids.

authors.name: Jack Yang, Lei Ao, Sean Li

papers.title: Variational Monte Carlo Study of Superconductivity in a Correlated System with Broken Inversion Symmetry
papers.summary: Unconventional superconductivity in systems with broken inversion symmetry has attracted considerable interest because antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling (ASOC) can strongly affect the spin structure and stability of superconducting states. In this study, we investigate superconductivity in a correlated system with the symmetry of a honeycomb network using the variational Monte Carlo method. We consider a single-band Hubbard model including an on-site Coulomb interaction $U$ and ASOC with coupling strength $\lambda$, and compare several pairing states with different pairing symmetries. The trial wave functions are constructed from particle-number- and Gutzwiller-projected BCS states. To examine the energetic stability of each pairing state, we calculate the variational energy as a function of the gap amplitude, while optimizing the variational parameter $\mu$ and the Gutzwiller parameter $g$ for each gap amplitude. At $U/t = 10$, the $f$-wave state has the lowest variational energy for $\lambda/t = 0$, whereas the chiral $p$-wave state becomes the most energetically favorable for $\lambda/t = 0.1$. These results indicate that ASOC strongly affects the competition among superconducting pairing states in the presence of strong electron correlations.

authors.name: Tsuyoshi Imazu, Katsunori Kubo

papers.title: Frank Elastic Constants of Associating Rigid-Rodlike Systems
papers.summary: Frank elastic constants of associating rigid rodlike systems are investigated using a mean field theory combined with the Straley elastic free energy formalism. The aggregation equilibrium and orientational ordering are treated self-consistently to analyze the concentration and temperature dependences of the elastic constants. Both a monomer--dimer model and a fully polydisperse rodlike aggregate model are considered. We find that aggregation selectively enhances the bend elastic constant through the long-tail structure of the aggregate-size distribution. As a result, a pronounced elastic anisotropy, $K_{33}\gg K_{11}>K_{22}$, emerges in the nematic phase. Decreasing temperature or increasing concentration promotes the formation of long rodlike aggregates and induces a rapid increase in the bend elastic constant, while the relation $K_{11}=3K_{22}$ remains unchanged. The exceptionally large bend elastic constants predicted here should be regarded as upper-bound estimates for the rigid-aggregate limit.

authors.name: Akihiko Matsuyama

papers.title: Symmetry-Selective Shift Current in Polar Multidomain Superlattices
papers.summary: Periodic polar multidomain superlattices can act as symmetry-selective elements for shift-current generation. We demonstrate this using a two-dimensional Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with prescribed multidomain configurations. The distinct full-supercell symmetries of periodic head-to-head and head-to-tail arrangements impose different constraints on the shift-current tensor and thereby select complementary nonlinear-response channels, as confirmed by numerical calculations. A direct comparison with equal-area averages of the constituent single-domain spectra shows that an independent-domain average does not reproduce the detailed multidomain spectra. A bond-resolved contribution analysis further clarifies the real-space origin of the multidomain response. Widening each domain from one to ten primitive cells leaves the selection rules intact. On the photon-energy grid used here, the allowed head-to-tail response changes sign and grows by about an order of magnitude. These results provide a theoretical framework for the symmetry-based design of anisotropic optical rectification in polar multidomain superlattices.

authors.name: Tomoaki Kameda, Kosuke Nagashio, Katsunori Wakabayashi

papers.title: The quantized Hall effect knows which way the current flows: mirror covariance and rectification in a laterally asymmetric Hall bar
papers.summary: The quantized Hall effect is the textbook emblem of universality: a resistance fixed by $h/e^2$, apparently indifferent to the shape of the sample, to its edges and to the direction of the current. That indifference is only half true. The plateau value is universal; the plateau is not. In a gate-defined Hall bar with one hard and one soft edge, reversing the current moves the plateau edge, and exchanging the edges reverses the move. We identify the symmetry that forces this. Because a perpendicular field breaks time reversal, the relevant operation is the in-plane $C_2$ rotation; within the self-consistent screening model it gives the covariance relation $R_\alpha[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(x),I]=R_\alpha[B,V_{\mathrm{conf}}(-x),-I]$, exact deep in the nonlinear regime and independent of linear response or microscopic reversibility. It predicts a rectification that is odd under exchange of the gate voltages and reverses with the magnetic field. The field-reversal test leaves the frozen lateral disorder untouched, so it holds for a single sample; it has not yet been performed. A further measurement, collapsing one incompressible strip, discriminates between co-directed and chiral pictures of the current. Self-consistent calculations show the soft-edge strip widening from 69 to 106\,nm on current reversal, moving the Hall resistance from 0.940 to $0.999994\,h/2e^2$ within a bounded window in magnetic field. The effect is a gate-tunable vector-product nonreciprocity, not magnetochiral anisotropy.

authors.name: A. Siddiki

papers.title: Core Reactivity in Cs-Ba-O ternary system under pressure
papers.summary: High pressure can activate Cs $5p$ core electrons for covalent bonding. In this study, we investigate the Cs-Ba-O system at 150 and 250 GPa using first-principles structure searches. CsBa$_3$O$_8$ and CsBaO$_4$ both lie on the static-lattice convex hull at 250~GPa and exhibit mild Cs $5p$-O $2p$ bonding while retaining O$_2$ units with intermediate superoxide-peroxide character. Cs$_2$BaO$_3$ shows substantially stronger bonding but remains metastable with respect to CsO and BaO. A 1:1 Cs$_2$O-BaO$_2$ mixture provides a solid starting composition for investigating this chemistry, with core-reactive CsO among the predicted products at 250~GPa. Calculated Cs $L_3$-edge x-ray absorption near-edge spectra and powder diffraction patterns provide electronic and structural signatures to guide identification of the predicted phases in diamond anvil cell experiments.

authors.name: Samantha Ellis, Austin Ellis, Lansen Wyke, Christina Taylor, Maosheng Miao

papers.title: Thermodynamic signatures of the period-doubling route to chemical chaos
papers.summary: Chemical reaction networks can evolve from stable oscillations to chaos through successive period doublings. We investigate general properties of entropy-production fluctuations near the onset of chaos and within the chaotic regime in reversible, well-mixed reaction networks. Near an isolated supercritical period-doubling bifurcation, we find a one-sided divergence of the diffusion constant with exponent one. For chaotic attractors satisfying the stated conditions, the entropy variance per unit volume grows exponentially when the macroscopic limit is taken first. Its exponential growth rate is $2\lambda_{\max}$, where $\lambda_{\max}$ is the largest Lyapunov exponent, implying a divergent diffusion constant. We also discuss the volume dependence of the fluctuations and the underlying physical mechanisms.

authors.name: Kyota Tamano, Keiji Saito

papers.title: Spin Simulators based on Exciton-Polariton Waveguide Networks
papers.summary: Many NP-hard optimization problems can be mapped onto interacting spin systems, whose ground state encodes the optimal solution. Polaritonic implementations based on gain-dissipative dynamics have recently emerged as promising analog computing platforms owing to their intrinsic parallelism and ultrafast operation. However, existing approaches are hindered by two fundamental limitations: maintaining the homogeneous amplitudes required for faithful problem encoding remains challenging in realistic physical systems, and most architectures are restricted to nearest-neighbour interactions, severely limiting the variety of optimization problems that can be efficiently addressed. We introduce a feasible polaritonic XY simulator based on a reconfigurable waveguide platform that overcomes both limitations. Our approach guarantees amplitude homogeneity while enabling the implementa- tion of arbitrary symmetric coupling matrices, thereby allowing the direct encoding of a wide variety of XY Hamiltonians. These results establish a practical architecture for programmable polaritonic spin simulators and pave the way towards scalable optical hardware for analog optimisation.

authors.name: Kevin Dini, Simone Zanotti, Timothy C. H. Liew

papers.title: Electrostatics of Chern junctions in a magnetic field
papers.summary: Electrostatic control is central to the operation of semiconductor junctions made from conventional materials. Here, we theoretically investigate the electrostatic properties of lateral junctions between two-dimensional (2D) Chern semiconductors in a perpendicular magnetic field. The spectral asymmetry of a Chern semiconductor acts as a magnetic-field-induced effective dopant density that is dependent on the Chern number.
