As a consequence, two regions with different Chern numbers acquire different chemical potentials at charge neutrality, leading to a built-in potential of topological origin across the junction. Using this built-in potential as a boundary condition, we solve the 2D Poisson equation to obtain the electric potential and charge density profiles, as well as the capacitance, of Chern semiconductor junctions. Our results inform the interplay between electronic topology and electrostatics in devices made from 2D materials.

authors.name: Robin Durand, Pascal Simon, Ion Garate

papers.title: Spin swapping mediated by spin-orbital textures in centrosymmetric multiorbital materials
papers.summary: Spin swapping converts a primary spin current into a secondary one by interchanging its flow and spin-polarization directions, attributed to spin-orbit scattering or spin-band splitting. Here we uncover a fundamentally distinct route to spin swapping arising from the orbital degree of freedom in the spin pumping to centrosymmetric multiorbital materials \textit{without spin-band splitting}. When the dynamical proximity ferromagnet injects a longitudinal spin current flowing normal to the interface, spin-orbit-entangled orbital textures redirect the injected spins into longitudinal and transverse orbital currents. Their subsequent conversion back to the spin sector generates transverse spin currents with propagation and polarization directions swapped relative to the primary spin current. The swapping efficiency achieves $50\%$ for Ge and Si. Governed by a fourth-rank tensor constrained by crystalline symmetry and without requiring spin-orbit scattering or inversion symmetry breaking, our finding reveals spin-orbital textures as hidden intermediate channels of spin swapping with unexplored material choices and functionalities.

authors.name: Chengyuan Cai, Hanchen Wang, Rui-Chun Xiao, Tao Yu

papers.title: Quantitatively Probing the Tilt Angle Failures in 4D-STEM Polarisation Analysis
papers.summary: Four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is increasingly used to map polarisation in ferroic textures such as domain walls, vortices, merons and skyrmions. These textures are accompanied by local strain, lattice rotation and misorientation, which also modulate the diffraction features used to infer polar order. Even small deviations from the zone axis can therefore produce contrast that is indistinguishable from a polarisation signal. Here we quantify the tilt sensitivity of two polarisation-sensitive signals, diffraction disc intensity and Kikuchi band intensity, in three ferroelectrics with distinct polar distortions: PbTiO3, BaTiO3 and Cu3B7O13Cl boracite. We find that tilts of only 0.01-0.05 degrees reverse most Friedel-pair disc asymmetries, and even the most robust disc pairs reverse by 0.04 degrees in BaTiO3, 0.14 degrees in PbTiO3 and 0.18 degrees in boracite, producing contrast equal and opposite to that of the polarisation. Kikuchi band contrast is the only signal that reports absolute polarity without knowledge of the specimen thickness, but it does so only up to 0.09 degrees in PbTiO3, 0.015 degrees in BaTiO3 and 0.02 degrees in boracite. From these results we define tilt tolerances for each signal and material, and propose practical criteria for distinguishing polarisation contrast from misorientation. The analysis also applies to scanning electron microscopy-based diffraction, including electron backscatter diffraction.

authors.name: Fintan G. Hardy, Noah Schnitzer, Mariana Palos, Geri Topore, Aron Walsh, Michele Shelly Conroy

papers.title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
papers.summary: Resorcinol-formaldehyde (RF) aerogels are lightweight, ultra-porous thermal superinsulators whose complex amorphous structure has not yet been described at the all-atom level. Here, we build an all-atom model of the RF aerogel skeleton by combining density functional theory (DFT) and classical molecular dynamics (MD), validate it against experimental infrared and density measurements, and use it to study the incorporation of iron dopants. The RF base unit was optimized with Gaussian, DMol$^{3}$ and SIESTA, and its calculated infrared spectrum agreed with experiment. Comparing classical force fields with DFT for branched systems of two to four base units (140-278 atoms) led to the choice of COMPASS II. A 15,012-atom system of 54 branched RF units, not cross-linked to each other, aggregated into a single cluster in the canonical (NVT) ensemble and reached an equilibrium density of 1.296 g.cm$^{-3}$ in the isobaric-isothermal (NPT) ensemble, in agreement with the experimental skeletal density (1.3 g.cm$^{-3}$). Then, 5 wt$\%$ iron (109 atoms) was added to the equilibrated structure: during 1 ns of NPT simulation, the fraction of iron atoms embedded in the skeleton rose from 63$\%$ to 71$\%$, and the Fe-C radial distribution function peaked at 3 \AA. The model thus provides an experimentally supported starting point for screening fillers and dopants in RF gels, with prospective application to their thermoelectric functionalization, which we have previously demonstrated experimentally with basalt and PANOX fibres. Future extensions could address skeleton properties relevant to thermal insulation and the pyrolysis of RF gels into carbon and metal-doped carbon aerogels.

authors.name: Shoeb Athar, J\'er\'emy Guazzagaloppa, Philippe Jund

papers.title: A Construction Framework for Three-Dimensional Topological Magnetic Textures
papers.summary: Three-dimensional magnetic systems offer diverse possibilities for constructing complex topological textures from simpler magnetic configurations. Here, we present different routes for constructing complex three-dimensional magnetic textures from simpler parent configurations and discuss their impact on the topology of the resulting structures. We identify four construction principles: (i) adding transverse modulations, (ii) adding structures, (iii) entangling textures (e.g. braiding, or twisting), and (iv) introducing singularities. Using the skyrmion tube as an explicit parent configuration, we show how these principles give rise to several known three-dimensional magnetic textures. We then apply the same principles to predict novel textures derived from a meron tube, which are confirmed by micromagnetic simulations to be metastable in chiral magnets. Our results establish general principles for the systematic construction and discovery of complex three-dimensional magnetic textures.

authors.name: Maria Azhar, Sandra C. Shaju, Karin Everschor-Sitte

papers.title: Brownian gyrator model with stochastic resetting
papers.summary: The Brownian gyrator (BG) model provides a minimal yet experimentally relevant example of a system operating far from thermodynamic equilibrium, sustaining steady currents with nonzero vorticity and exhibiting stochastic rotational motion along elliptical orbits. In this paper, we study the response of the BG to a fundamentally non-equilibrium perturbation -- stochastic resetting at a constant rate -- either to a fixed point in the plane or to a randomly selected point on a circle. We determine analytically and numerically the steady-state position probability density function (PDF), together with its marginals and moments, which exhibit a resetting-induced non-monotonic dependence on the resetting rate. We also characterize the associated local probability currents and vorticity fields. Furthermore, we investigate the dependence of the mean angular momentum and mean angular velocity on the resetting rate, and numerically analyze the PDFs of these observables. This analysis fully quantifies the complex behavior arising from the competition between two non-equilibrium mechanisms with distinct spatial symmetries.

authors.name: Satya N. Majumdar, Gregory Schehr, Pascal Viot, Gleb Oshanin

papers.title: Strain control of magneto-optical properties of ultra-thin Ni-Mn-Ga films grown by magnetron sputtering
papers.summary: Ultra-thin epitaxial Ni-Mn-Ga films, 10-15 nm thick, were grown by magnetron sputtering on MgO(001), either directly on the substrate or on a Cr buffer, and studied by X-ray diffraction, magnetometry, and magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) spectroscopy. The films were austenitic, with the cubic cell tetragonally distorted in opposite directions. The film on bare MgO was stretched in-plane ($c/a=0.989$) and the film on Cr was compressed in-plane ($c/a=1.021$), while their unit-cell volumes differed by less than $0.3\%$. As the thermal expansion mismatch was expected to stretch the films in-plane in both cases, the opposite distortions were attributed to the lattice misfit. The room-temperature magnetization loops of the two films did not show significant differences, but their polar and longitudinal MOKE spectra differed in the amplitude, sign, and energy of the spectral structures over the whole 0.76-5 eV range. Magneto-optical simulations showed that the absence of the Cr buffer accounted only for the stronger low-energy polar MOKE rotation extremum of the film on MgO. We attributed the other changes to the strain-induced change of the electronic structure, consistent with theoretical predictions in which the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ sub-bands of the minority-spin Ni $e_g$ states exchange their order when the distortion changes sign. In parts of the spectrum, the two films showed Kerr rotation or ellipticity of opposite sign, so the choice of the growth template or a dynamically induced distortion can switch the sign of the magneto-optical response at a given photon energy.

authors.name: M. Make\v{s}, P. Ve\v{r}t\'{a}t, M. Rame\v{s}, J. Z\'{a}zvorka, F. M\'{a}ca, J. Zemen, O. Heczko, M. Veis

papers.title: Complex Martensitic Microstructures in ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$
papers.summary: We analyze the unusual microstructure resulting from the cubic to orthorhombic phase transformation in the shape-memory alloy ${\rm Ti}_{76}{\rm Nb}_{22}{\rm Al}_{2}$. This seems to represent an approximate experimental realization of a deformation having a finite number of incompatible deformation gradients, which has been known to exist only as a theoretical possibility. Because the middle eigenvalue $\gamma$ of the transformation strain is very close to 1, the phase transformation in this alloy takes place via nucleation of exact austenite-martensite interfaces rather than, as usual for other alloys, by classical austenite-martensite interfaces separating the austenite from a finely-twinned laminate of martensite. According to the moving mask approximation of Della Porta this leads to the question whether a microstructure can be formed from the set $H$ of the twelve matrices ${\mathbf V}_i$ on the martensite energy wells that are rank-one connected to the identity, even though these matrices are mutually incompatible. We show that when $\gamma=1$ and the transformation is volume preserving, such a microstructure is possible that does not deform the grain boundary. This is a consequence of $H$ forming a degenerate $T_{12}$ configuration in the sense of Kirchheim. In fact there are such microstructures supported on just 8 of the 12 matrices in $H$. However there is no deformation satisfying the same boundary condition whose gradient belongs to $H$ almost everywhere. An additional prediction, confirmed experimentally, is that the macroscopic deformation gradient equals the identity everywhere. We also analyse the approximate compatibility of the ${\mathbf V}_i$. Although mutually incompatible, they are nearly compatible, with some pairs much more nearly compatible than others, these pairs corresponding to interfaces that are more frequently observed.

authors.name: John M. Ball, Francesco Della Porta, Tomonari Inamura

papers.title: Hydrogen sublattice in LaH$_{12}$: structural stability and possible ordering motifs
papers.summary: Lanthanum polyhydrides, synthesized under extreme pressure, exhibit near-room-temperature superconductivity. Finding a precise arrangement of the hydrogen sublattice that is critical for understanding the strong electron-phonon coupling remains experimentally unresolved due to the small X-ray scattering form factor of hydrogen atoms. In this work, we attempt to computationally reconstruct hydrogen sublattices of the LaH$_{12}$ at 100-200 GPa combining unconstrained evolutionary searches and structure generation with fixed lanthanum sublattice. By implementing a similarity metric, we screen the computationally generated configurations against experimental powder X-ray diffraction data. We specifically identify the trigonal $R\bar{3}$-LaH$_{12}$ and pseudo-hexagonal $C222_1$-La$_2$H$_{24}$ phases, which demonstrate close agreement with the experimental X-ray diffraction data. First-principles calculations confirm the metallic and superconducting nature of these hydrides. Crucially, our lattice dynamics analysis using the stochastic self-consistent harmonic approximation (SSCHA) indicates that these structures are dynamically stable. We reveal the presence of molecular H$_2$ units and soft phonon modes in the trigonal LaH$_{12}$ that suppresses superconductivity ($T_c \ge 30$ K), while the hydrogen clathrate network in the $C222_1$ phase drives strong electron-phonon interactions, yielding the coupling parameters of $\lambda\approx 1.83$, $\omega_{\log} \approx 87.5$ meV and transition temperature of $T_c\approx 150$ K at 150 GPa.

authors.name: Khasan Akhmadiev, Di Zhou, Viktor V. Struzhkin, Alexander G. Kvashnin, Dmitrii V. Semenok

papers.title: Marginal Operator Deformations and Pseudocriticality in Baxter--Wu Models
papers.summary: Weak first-order transitions can exhibit extended pseudocritical scaling regimes that mimic genuine criticality. We show that the long-debated apparent criticality of the dilute Baxter--Wu model arises from a marginally relevant renormalization-group flow, which ultimately drives the system into a first-order regime with phase coexistence. By integrating conformal perturbation theory with symmetry-resolved tensor-network level spectroscopy, we parameterize a slowly running coupling in a numerically accessible form and construct a generic flow-based diagnostic. The renormalization-group trajectories of the dilute and self-dual Baxter--Wu models under marginal operator deformations collapse onto the multicritical phase diagram of the dilute four-state Potts model, exposing the flow structure on both the marginally relevant and irrelevant sides of the Potts point.

authors.name: Hyun-Yong Lee, Naoki Kawashima, Nikolaos G. Fytas, Dong-Hee Kim

papers.title: Steady states in asymmetric exclusion processes with reactions: Fluctuations and non-mean field behaviour
papers.summary: We study an totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP) in an open geometry. We couple TASEP with simple reactions in the form of production (birth) and degradation (death) due to over crowding taking place in the bulk. We investigate the steady states, which are generically space-dependent. Phase coexistences are also possible for some choices of the model parameters. We study the system by mean-field theories (MFT) supplemented by extensive Monte-Carlo simulations (MCS). Intriguingly, unlike oridinary TASEP and other related models, configuration-dependent bulk reactions in a TASEP model can make nearest-neighbour correlations quantitatively important even in an open driven system where mean-field theory would ordinarily be expected to provide a useful description. We attribute this to the correlation effects ignored in MFT. We numerically quantify this correlation effect.

authors.name: Rohn Chatterjee, Atri Goswami, Sudip Mukherjee

papers.title: Mutual linearity in semi-Markov networks
papers.summary: Despite their microscopic complexity, stochastic networks show a surprising degree of universal, parameter-independent properties. One example is mutual linearity, which has recently been characterized as a generic, pairwise-linear relation between observables of Markov processes under local perturbations, valid for both stationary dynamics and for transient dynamics in Laplace space. Here we show that mutual linearity arises if a certain global affine relation is satisfied. This allows us to demonstrate that mutual linearity also holds for a broad class of local perturbations in semi-Markov networks, which, unlike Markov networks, have memory in terms of the dwell time in the current state. However, exceptions exist, meaning that mutual linearity does not extend to all possible perturbations of semi-Markov networks. Strikingly, this restriction disappears for first-passage times. Thus, semi-Markov networks exhibit a fundamental asymmetry between occupation and first-passage statistics, different from Markov networks. Finally, we show that our results are directly applicable to stochastic resetting in semi-Markov networks, where the Laplace-space relations acquire a physical interpretation in terms of stationary occupations and the probability to reach a target before reset. This provides a natural setting in which the predicted affine relations can be probed.

authors.name: Julian B. Voits, Ulrich S. Schwarz

papers.title: Field evolution of the multi-$k$ magnetic states in NdB$_4$ revealed by neutron diffraction
papers.summary: We investigate the magnetic states of the Shastry-Sutherland-lattice magnet NdB$_4$ using single-crystal neutron diffraction. We focus on magnetic fields applied along the tetragonal $c$ axis, which stabilise the fractional 1/5~magnetisation plateau. In the low-temperature phase below 4.9 K, the transition into the plateau state at approximately 12 kOe is marked by a change in the propagation vectors from $(1/5,0,-2/5)$ and its double $(2/5,0,1/5)$ to $(0,0,1/5)$ and $(0,0,2/5)$. At the transition from the plateau to a nominally `field-polarised' state near 33 kOe, all magnetic reflections associated with non-integer propagation vectors disappear, whereas reflections corresponding to the $\mathbf{k}=0$ component persist throughout the entire field range. We conclude that that the in-plane components survive even in the high-field phase and that the polarisation is, in fact, incomplete. The observed field dependence provides direct support for a description of NdB$_4$ in terms of two coupled magnetic instabilities: all-in-all-out order of the in-plane moments and a spin-density wave of the out-of-plane components.

authors.name: D. Brunt, N. Qureshi, E. Chan, B. Ouladdiaf, G. Balakrishnan, D. D. Khalyavin, O. A. Petrenko

papers.title: Dynamically Reentrant Skyrmion Phase in Oscillating Magnetic Fields
papers.summary: We address a central open question in driven topological matter by investigating the nonequilibrium response of a two-dimensional magnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions subjected to a periodically oscillating magnetic field. Using extensive Monte Carlo simulations, we uncover a dynamically reentrant skyrmion phase that emerges within a finite window of field amplitudes and bias fields, sandwiched between the conventional skyrmion and polarized ferromagnetic phases. This phase has no equilibrium counterpart and originates from an imbalance between skyrmion creation and annihilation over a single field cycle, leading to a reversal of the period-averaged topological charge. We show that the re-entrant phase exists only in the dynamic response regime where the system can follow the drive, and is suppressed at higher driving frequencies. Our results establish periodic driving as a nonequilibrium control parameter for stabilizing and reversing skyrmion topology.

authors.name: Z. Demir Vatansever, E. Vatansever, A. Vasilopoulos, N. G. Fytas, A. Berger

papers.title: Finite-width shift of the edge of chaos in deep neural networks
papers.summary: Deep neural networks train best when they are initialised at the edge of chaos, the critical line in the plane of weight and bias variances on which the distance between two inputs neither grows nor shrinks with depth. The line is known for infinitely wide networks; at finite width it moves, and how it moves has been disputed. We treat the logarithm of the distance between two inputs through a network of width $N$ as a random walk and compute its drift and variance to order $1/N$. The edge of chaos moves to a larger weight variance, by $\Delta\sigma_w^2=-a_1/(N\,\partial_{\sigma_w^2}\ln\chi_1)$, about $8/N$ for $\tanh$ networks at a bias variance of $0.05$, confirmed by simulations of the exact finite-width recursion. The shift describes a typical network; the average over many networks is dominated by rare networks in which the distance grows, and its critical point moves the other way, which explains why calculations and simulations have disagreed. Backpropagation follows the same random walk, so the shift applies to gradients unchanged. Along the edge of chaos, the information about the similarity of two inputs is constant until the compression over the depth exceeds about one nat, which fixes where to sit on the line. The results give an initialisation rule, Crinit, that places a network on its finite-width edge of chaos without a search. On MNIST and Fashion-MNIST at width $64$ it is more accurate than the standard rules at their usual settings, by a small margin in shallow networks and a large one in deep networks, where most standard rules fail; it trains in fewer steps, and it matches or beats the standard rules with a tuned gain.

authors.name: Arn Caesar

papers.title: Anomalous thermal transport in isotope-enriched germanium carbide
papers.summary: Advances in modern electronics demand the dissipation of heat fluxes approaching 1000 W cm$^{-2}$, which drives an urgent need for materials with thermal conductivity ($\kappa$) exceeding 1000 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. Here, by solving the Boltzmann transport equation considering both three- and four-phonon interactions, we observe that isotopically pure cubic germanium carbide (GeC) exhibits a remarkable $\kappa$ of 1018 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at room temperature, which is further corroborated by state-of-the-art machine-learning molecular dynamics simulations. Two unique mechanisms underlie this anomalously high $\kappa$: a remarkably strong isotopic enhancement effect (289%) and a surprisingly modest suppression due to four-phonon scattering (22%)-despite the presence of a wide acoustic-optical phonon gap. Moreover, we find that GeC defies the conventional Leibfried-Schlomann formula and exhibits a non-monotonic variation of $\kappa$ with external hydrostatic pressure at elevated temperatures. Our findings establish isotope-enriched GeC as a material of ultrahigh $\kappa$ and an ideal platform for exploring exotic phonon physics.

authors.name: Wenjiang Zhou, Bai Song

papers.title: First-principles study of the formation of Group-IV--vacancy color centers in diamond
papers.summary: $XV$ ($X$ is Si, Ge, Sn, or Pb, and $V$ is the carbon vacancy) color centers are promising platforms for quantum computing and quantum information science due to their favorable optical and spin properties. They are commonly fabricated by ion implantation, which inevitably introduces vacancies and carbon self-interstitials (C$_i$) into the lattice. However, the microscopic formation mechanism remains unclear, limiting the yield and stability of $XV$ centers. Here, first-principles calculations are conducted to systematically investigate the roles of $V$ and C$_i$ in $XV$ formation. We find that $XV$ formation is energetically favorable, with large binding energies and low diffusion barriers. Nevertheless, $XV$ readily captures C$_i$ to form substitutional defect $X_s$, or captures an additional $V$ to form the complex $XV_2$. Charge transition levels show that oppositely charged reactants never meet in these reactions, and that Coulomb repulsion blocks them only when both reactants carry charges of the same sign, which for the capture of C$_i$ requires strongly n- or p-type conditions. These competing defect reactions destabilize the split-vacancy configuration and could account for the low formation yield of $XV$ centers, so that they appear at concentrations well below those expected from the implanted dose. Our results elucidate the microscopic origin of this intrinsic instability and suggest that Fermi-level control may suppress defect conversions and stabilize the split-vacancy configuration.

authors.name: Xiangru Han, Adam Gali

papers.title: Millikelvin magnetometry up to 30~T using a multi-cross micro-Hall sensor
papers.summary: We report a multi-cross micro-Hall sensor fabricated from an MBE-grown GaAs/AlGaAs heterostructure for high-sensitivity magnetometry. The device enables dc magnetization measurements at temperatures down to $\sim$15~mK and in dc magnetic fields up to 30 T. Bulk samples with dimensions ranging from 100~$\mu$m to 1~mm can be measured with a resolution better than 1$~\mu$T with a 1~$\mu$A excitation at 13.77 Hz. Test-of-performance measurements were carried out by probing the field-dependent magnetization plateaus of the triangular-lattice quantum magnet K$_{2}$Co$_{2}$(SeO$_{3}$)$_{3}$ at 20~mK, the antiferromagnetic transition of K${_3}$GdTe${_2}$O${_9}$ near 220 mK via temperature-dependent magnetization, and the quantum oscillations in a ruthenium single crystal. A simple and reliable sample-mounting setup that ensures reproducible magnetic measurements is provided.

authors.name: Bingbing Tong, Yinina Ma, Zhenhua Zhao, Shuyu Zheng, Li Lu, Peijie Sun, Gang Li

papers.title: Majorana-like Josephson branch structure in one-dimensional transport of cold atoms
papers.summary: We study phase-controlled transport through a one-dimensional channel of attractively interacting fermions connecting two three-dimensional BCS reservoirs. The competition between channel phase stiffness and pair tunnelling at the two contacts results in the emergence of two $4\pi$-periodic families of stationary states, characterised by symmetric or asymmetric phase drops at the boundaries. Advancing the reservoir phase difference by $2\pi$ exchanges these families so that the equilibrium energy remains $2\pi$ periodic, while the $4\pi $ periodicity might be attained in a diabatic regime. This structure admits a formal description in terms of two boundary Majorana operators, combining into a nonlocal fermion mode. Renormalization-group analysis shows that quantum fluctuations and phase slips are suppressed in the zero-temperature thermodynamic limit, preserving the branch crossings. The predicted branch exchange, metastable currents, and sweep-rate-dependent switching provide experimentally testable signatures of Majorana-like Josephson branch physics in a gapless interacting channel.

authors.name: Rory Whelan, Dimitri M. Gangardt, Igor V. Lerner

papers.title: Hidden entropic order of emergent charges in a classical Amp\`ere spin liquid
papers.summary: Classical spin liquids are characterized by an extensive number of ground-state configurations. Coulomb spin liquids have, in this ground-state manifold, a divergence-free local constraint, which gives dipolar correlations and pinch points in the structure factor. Recently, models with a complementary ground-state constraint, defined by a zero-circulation constraint (Amp\`ere's law), have been proposed. While classical Coulomb spin liquids forbid emergent charges, their Amp\`ere counterparts leave the charges unconstrained. Here we study an Ising Amp\`ere model on the octochlore lattice. The ground states obey a Gauss law for an antisymmetric rank-two field, i.e., three coupled two-dimensional Gauss laws, which are expected to produce pinch points in the structure factor. Nevertheless, maximal charges, vertices with all six arrows in or out, spontaneously accumulate on one of the two sublattices of the cubic lattice, with disordered signs. This order has a purely entropic origin; it washes out the pinch-point singularities at large scales, produces no magnetic Bragg peaks, and coexists with an extensive entropy. The system enters into this sublattice long-range ordered state through a continuous transition in what seems to be the three-dimensional Ising universality class. Moreover, the state has no magnetic order; it is even under time reversal: it is a hidden, entropic order within the Amp\`ere manifold. Thus, a system whose Gauss law would predict an algebraic spin liquid becomes, through a non-magnetic ordering transition, a partially ordered short-range spin liquid. Our study is based on a combination of the constraint-vector theory, exact bounds and enumeration, and Monte Carlo, Wang-Landau, and parallel-tempering simulations.

authors.name: H. Diego Rosales, Emma M. Bizot, Flavia A. G\'omez Albarrac\'in, Pierre Pujol

papers.title: Evolutionary Design of Interpretable Spatial Descriptors for Structure-Property Relationship Discovery
papers.summary: Structure property prediction is a classical task in machine learning, ranging from molecular activity and materials properties to local functional responses measured in microscopy. For image-based regression, two choices define the information available to the predictor: the size of the image neighborhood and the spatial resolution retained within it. A small neighborhood can omit relevant surrounding structure, whereas a large, finely sampled neighborhood can introduce redundant or irrelevant information. Here, we develop a framework for constructing spatial descriptors for prediction of local spectra and hysteresis loops. We benchmark regression models, use SHAP maps to examine their spatial attribution, and explore the effect of the patch size and compression to establish the relationship between predictive accuracy and descriptor dimensionality. We then use a genetic algorithm to optimize spatial partitions and the assignment of mean, minimum, and maximum pooling operations. Each retained region contributes an explicit measurement of the image, allowing the search to balance prediction error against the number of descriptor values. Cartesian and polar constructions provide complementary ways to organize this information. The resulting descriptors make it possible to examine where spatial detail is needed, where regional summaries are sufficient, and how these choices depend on the predictor and the measured response. The same approach can be used for molecules and solids once the genetic algorithm rules for these are established.

authors.name: Aditya Raghavan, Sergei V Kalinin

papers.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
papers.summary: The origin of the apparent metal-insulator transition in two-dimensional electron systems remains debated. Using temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on industry-relevant MoS$_2$ monolayer FETs with amorphous HfO$_2$ dielectrics, we establish classical percolation as the underlying mechanism. We report two complementary signatures of disorder-driven conduction onset: a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse as a function of absolute gate voltage and a vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density $n_{\mathrm{c}}$, identified as the percolation threshold. These findings identify dielectric-interface disorder, rather than channel quality alone, as the key parameter governing device turn-on. The extracted activation barriers reach values substantially exceeding room-temperature thermal energies, indicating that disorder-driven conduction onset remains relevant well beyond cryogenic transport.

authors.name: R. V. Upadya, M. Introna, X. Wu, C. J. L. de la Rosa, K. Banerjee, D. Lin, K. De Greve

papers.title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
papers.summary: Grain growth during heat treatment strongly affects the microstructure of polycrystalline materials and, consequently, their mechanical properties. Although numerical methods such as front-tracking or front-capturing simulations can accurately describe grain growth, their high computational cost limits their use for long or non-isothermal thermal cycles. In previous work, grain growth was successfully predicted under isothermal conditions by treating grain size distributions as time series and forecasting their evolution using recurrent neural networks, allowing complete grain growth trajectories to be generated in seconds rather than through costly PDE-based simulations. In the present work, this forecasting framework is reformulated to handle non-isothermal conditions by explicitly incorporating thermal information into the model architecture. Grain size distributions are encoded using a convolutional neural network, thermal descriptors are embedded through a dedicated multilayer perceptron, and temporal evolution is predicted using a recurrent network. Instantaneous temperature and thermal rate are provided at each time step, allowing the model to adapt its predictions to changing thermal conditions. The framework is trained and evaluated on datasets generated from validated front-tracking simulations across a wide range of non-isothermal thermal paths. The results show that the thermally conditioned model accurately reproduces grain growth dynamics under complex thermal histories, achieving, in k-fold cross-validation over all simulations, mean relative errors of 2.99% (one-hour cycles) and 4.51% (four-hour cycles) with coefficients of determination exceeding 0.99, and mean relative errors between 1.91% and 14.66% on ten simulations following four unseen thermal histories of increasing complexity.

authors.name: Eliane Younes, Elie Hachem, Marc Bernacki

papers.title: Longitudinal and Transverse Thermoelectric Properties in Topological Quantum Materials
papers.summary: Thermoelectric materials can be topologically trivial or non-trivial, enabling reversible interconversion of heat and electricity using a solid-state technology. Incidentally, few of the first experimentally discovered 3D topological materials, namely, Bi, Sb, Sn and Pb-based chalcogenides, were long known as good thermoelectric materials. In these compounds, the heavy atoms that give rise to strong spin-orbit coupling often become essential for band inversion and non-trivial band topology. They lead to low lattice thermal conductivity, linearly dispersing Dirac-like bands induce high electrical mobility, and a band-inverted electronic structure with multiple band extrema gives rise to high Seebeck coefficients. In materials, where the applied temperature gradient induces electrical voltage (Seebeck effect) in the same direction, they are termed as longitudinal thermoelectrics. On the other hand, when the generated electrical voltage and applied thermal current remain orthogonal to each other, the materials are termed as transverse thermoelectrics. The transverse response can be driven by an additional external magnetic field (ordinary Nernst effect), intrinsic remanent magnetisation, or non-zero Berry curvature of a material, which arises from their non-trivial topology (anomalous Nernst effect). We discuss another class of quantum materials, known as goniopolar materials, that exhibit axis-dependent conduction polarity and hence transverse thermoelectric effects, which are based on mechanisms of longitudinal thermoelectric properties. In this review, we cover both types of thermoelectricity, focusing on materials that possess non-trivial topological order. We make connections between their structures, topology and transport properties and suggest tunability of thermoelectric properties going beyond conventional mechanisms such as electron-phonon interactions.

authors.name: Jyoti Duhan, Anil Kumar B. M., Satya N. Guin, Koushik Pal

papers.title: Charged Three-Dimensional Solitons in a Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystal
papers.summary: Experimental observations and computer simulation of formation and structural properties of so far experimentally never seen electrically charged propagating 3D solitons are reported. The propagating solitons appear spontaneously without an external field in a ferroelectric nematic (NF) liquid crystal under rapid cooling from the antiferroelectric (SmZA) phase. The observed solitons propagate either parallel or antiparallel to the ferroelectric polarization and annihilate when they collide with each other. They are attributed to either positively or negatively charged propagating local polarization splay formed to screen excess negative or positive mobile charge lumps in the NF phase. The presence of mobile charge is attributed to a spatially periodic charge distribution present in the antiferroelectric phase that temporarily remains after the temperature is quenched through the antiferroelectric- ferroelectric phase transition.

authors.name: Netra Prasad Dhakal, Zakaria Siddiquee, Hiroya Nishikawa, Fumito Araoka, James Gleeson, Samuel Sprunt, Antal Jakli

papers.title: Exact Transport-Information Correspondence for Distribution-Adaptive Discretization
papers.summary: Discretization of continuous probability distributions is an operation on the sample space, and the structure induced by this operation cannot generally be determined solely from information geometry. In our recent work on unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), we established a non-arbitrary connection between the transport cost associated with discretization and the information-geometric indistinguishability of continuous probability distributions. Through the transport-information correspondence, the UCN quantify the information-theoretic cost due to discretization as the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence between nearby continuous distributions associated with the discretization geometry. In the original UCN construction, discretization is implemented by transporting the probability mass within each cell to its geometric centroid. The resulting transport-information correspondence, however, is derived under specific conditions involving the cell geometry, spatial coverage, and the vanishing-cell-scale limit. In this work, we introduce an alternative local-map discretization scheme in which the probability mass within each cell is transported to its own probability-weighted centroid. This change in the representative-point selection enables an exact expression for the transport cost of each cell in terms of the covariance matrix of its conditional probability distribution and the Fisher metric of the underlying continuous family. We establish an exact correspondence between the resulting transport cost and the expectation of the associated Fisher-induced quadratic form, without requiring uniform cell geometry, complete coverage of the sample space, or an infinitesimal cell-scale limit. The proposed construction thus generalizes the transport-information correspondence to finite-scale discretization using arbitrary collections of non-overlapping bounded convex sets.

authors.name: Koretaka Yuge

papers.title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
papers.summary: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.

authors.name: Mingjian Gu, Zhaoyu Fei, Xiaoguang Wang

papers.title: A local Yang-Baxter obstruction for the hard-square model
papers.summary: Many exact solutions of two-dimensional lattice models rest on an analytic family of weights satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation. The hard-hexagon model was solved in this way, while the neighbouring hard-square model has no known closed form. We determine the height alphabets that encode hard squares without hidden heights, and there are exactly two connected ones, the occupation variables themselves and the four heights of Andrews, Baxter and Forrester. Hard hexagons is integrable on both, but no analytic Yang-Baxter family of face weights passes through hard squares at nonzero activity on either. The difference lies in the exclusion rule, which for hard squares turns a few Yang-Baxter equations into polynomial identities that force auxiliary weights to vanish. A closed form for hard squares is not excluded, but a solution by this route would have to leave these encodings or go beyond a single analytic family through the model. Encodings with hidden heights remain open.

authors.name: Gabriel Ortega, Eliecer Pe\~na-Ancavil

papers.title: Mean-Field Study of Normal Metal-Quantum Dot-Superconductor System in the Presence of External Magnetic Field
papers.summary: In this paper, we have analyzed the spectral and transport properties of a weakly correlated single-level quantum dot hybridized with one normal conducting and another Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) superconducting lead (N-QD-S system) in the presence of an external magnetic field. We have employed Green's function equation of motion (EOM) approach within a self-consistent Hartree-Fock (HF) mean-field approximation to analyze the Hamiltonian. We studied the effect of on-dot Coulomb correlation and an external magnetic field on the sub-gap Andreev levels of a quantum dot, strongly coupled to a conventional s-wave superconductor as a function of impurity parameters. We have shown that for a finite magnetic field, the Andreev bound states (ABSs) split into a spin-up and spin-down contribution (i.e. Zeeman splitting) and cross the Fermi energy level, resulting in a quantum phase transition, which is an indication of a change in the fermion parity of the ground state. Further, within the non-linear regime, we discuss the total electrical conductance for various values of Zeeman energy and on-dot Coulomb interactions. We have compared our results with the existing experimental and theoretical results.

authors.name: Pujita Das, Sachin Verma, Ajay

papers.title: Tunneling spectroscopy of topological insulator Josephson junctions
papers.summary: In the seminal proposal by Fu and Kane, the superconducting proximity effect is used to realize topological superconductivity in the topological surface state (TSS) of a 3D topological insulator (TI). In a Josephson junction made on the TI surface, the spin-momentum locking of the TSS guarantees the existence of spin nondegenerate, perfectly transmitted Andreev modes. These modes lead to gap closing as a function of the superconducting phase difference $\varphi$. Here, we report the observation of highly transmissive Andreev modes in a TI Josephson junction, probed via tunnel contacts and $\varphi$ controlled by a flux loop. Within our experimental resolution, they could indicate a gap closing and reopening. This phenomenon is observed for a wide range of chemical potentials, supporting its TSS origin. Under an applied magnetic field, highly transmissive modes are observed locally, matching theoretical predictions for Josephson vortices in the TSS. Our results support the fundamental role of spin-momentum locking in the Andreev physics in the TSS.

authors.name: Jakob Schluck, Ella Nikodem, Anton Montag, Alexander Ziesen, Mahasweta Bagchi, Fabian Hassler, Yoichi Ando

papers.title: Helicons in multi-Weyl semimetals
papers.summary: Helicons are low-frequency, circularly polarized transverse electromagnetic modes that propagate in three-dimensional conducting systems in the presence of a static magnetic field. Here, we investigate helicon excitations in gapless multi-Weyl semimetals (mWSMs) with topological charge \(J=1,2,\) and \(3\) using semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory. We incorporate both Berry-curvature and orbital-magnetic-moment corrections into the quasiparticle dynamics and determine the optical-conductivity tensor in the presence of a weak static magnetic field. The longitudinal conductivity is obtained analytically for single-, double and triple-Weyl systems, whereas the transverse conductivity is evaluated numerically in the low-frequency regime relevant to helicon propagation. We find that the cyclotron frequency acquires a nontrivial dependence on the topological charge and on the magnetic field. The resulting helicon dispersion retains the characteristic quadratic dependence on the wave vector, while the axion-electrodynamics contribution generates an additional linear term. We further show that the axion term lifts the degeneracy of the gapped collective modes at zero wave vector, with the resulting mode frequencies determined by the \(J\)-dependent plasma frequencies. These results demonstrate that the helicon response provides a probe of the distinct electrodynamic properties of multi-Weyl semimetals.

authors.name: Shiv Kumar Ram, Amit Gupta

papers.title: Lifetime of bimerons and antibimerons in two-dimensional magnets
papers.summary: Soliton-based computing architectures have recently emerged as a promising avenue to overcome fundamental limitations of conventional information technologies, the von Neumann bottleneck. In this context, magnetic skyrmions have been widely considered for in-situ processing devices due to their mobility and enhanced lifetime in materials with broken inversion symmetry. However, modern applications in non-volatile reservoir or neuromorphic computing raise the additional demand for non-linear inter-soliton interactions. Here, we report that solitons in easy-plane magnets, such as bimerons and antibimerons, show greater versatility and potential for non-linear interactions than skyrmions and antiskyrmions, making them superior candidates for this class of applications. Using first-principles and transition state theory, we predict the coexistence of degenerate bimerons and antibimerons at zero field in a van der Waals heterostructure Fe$_3$GeTe$_2$/Cr$_2$Ge$_2$Te$_6$ -- an experimentally feasible system. We demonstrate that, owing to their distinct structural symmetry, bimerons exhibit fundamentally different behavior from skyrmions and cannot be regarded as their in-plane counterparts, as is often assumed. This distinction leads to unique properties of bimerons and antibimerons, which arise from the unbroken rotational symmetry in easy-plane magnets. These range from anisotropic soliton-soliton interactions to strong entropic effects on their lifetime, driven by the non-local nature of thermal excitations. Our findings reveal a broader richness of solitons in easy-plane magnets and underline their unique potential for spintronic devices.

authors.name: Moritz A. Goerzen, Tim Drevelow, Soumyajyoti Haldar, Hendrik Schrautzer, Stefan Heinze, Dongzhe Li

papers.title: Chiral and Topological Phonons in the Square-Octagon Lattice
papers.summary: Controlling chirality and topology in phonon systems requires microscopic routes to reshape optical modes, open symmetry-governed gaps, and understand the robustness of the resulting chiral vibrational structure against disorder. The square-octagon lattice provides a natural platform for this purpose because its four-site basis generates internal optical modes and symmetry-allowed band crossings that are sensitive to the range of elastic couplings. We show that extended interactions, mass imbalance, and time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking provide an effective means to control these features. In particular, third-nearest-neighbor coupling releases otherwise nearly frozen optical branches, demonstrating that longer-range restoring pathways are essential for activating internal motions of the multi-site basis. Once TRS is broken, the symmetry-allowed line crossings are converted into avoided crossings, producing phonon modes with finite circular polarization. The resulting Berry curvature is concentrated near these gapped regions, and the relevant bands acquire opposite Chern numbers, identifying a topological chiral-phonon phase. We further find that the chiral sector remains most robust under mass disorder and is more strongly suppressed by spring disorder, while local chiral motion and the spectral identity of the chiral sector survive more strongly than the coherent global chiral response.

authors.name: Ravi Kiran, A. Taraphder

papers.title: Ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals: temperature-tunable electrocaloric fluids with large strength at low fields
papers.summary: The electrocaloric (EC) effect offers a promising energy-efficient and clean cooling technology. We present the first direct measurements of EC temperature change in a new family of EC fluids, ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals (FNLCs), demonstrating in two such materials temperature jumps of $|{\Delta}T_j|$ ~ 0.2 K for field changes as low as ${\Delta}E$ ~ 0.1 $V {\mu}m^{-1}$. Indirect measurements of adiabatic temperature change $|{\Delta}T|$ confirm that these direct measurements are an underestimate and that ${\Delta}E$ = 2 $V {\mu}m^{-1}$ can induce up to $|{\Delta}T|$ ~ 1.6 K, yielding EC strengths $|{\Delta}T/{\Delta}E|$ up to 100% higher than incumbent materials. For temperature spans of 5-10 K, we predict a coefficient of performance of ~21-40. We find $|{\Delta}T|$ ~ 1 K for >100 FNLCs that collectively span all temperatures between $0{^\circ}$C and $100{^\circ}$C. This, together with the new device concepts conceivable with fluid EC materials, offers huge potential for cooling applications.

authors.name: Diana I. Nikolova, Rachel Tuffin, Mengfan Guo, Neil D. Mathur, Xavier Moya, Peter Tipping, Richard J. Mandle, Helen F. Gleeson

papers.title: Colloquium: A critique on van der Waals and two-dimensional magnets
papers.summary: Magnetic two-dimensional (2D) crystals were isolated about a decade ago, triggering a tremendous research activity worldwide. This colloquium raises a stiff question: what is really new about them? At first sight, they seem to be purer implementations of 2D spin models than traditional systems such as ultra-thin films. Yet, they partly realized their promises so far, and whether they give fresh perspectives on long-standing predictions in statistical physics is still an open question. Undoubtedly, they are uniquely amenable to electric-field effect, susceptible to mechanical deformation, and sensitive to moir\'{e}s, for example. They represent interesting platforms for exploring, challenging, or simply revisiting a wide range of phenomena in condensed matter magnetism. This colloquium intends to offer a critical, yet not necessarily skeptical, overview of the field, clarifying what we believe could be unique with 2D magnets, related quasi-2D van der Waals magnets, and their heterostructures.

authors.name: Johann Coraux, Nicolas Rougemaille, Cedric Robert, Cl\'ement Faugeras, Andr\`es Saul, Beno\^it Gr\'emaud, Luis Hueso, F\'elix Casanova, Aur\'elien Manchon

papers.title: Inverse Chiral Phonon Zeeman Effect in Noncentrosymmetric Crystals
papers.summary: We present a quantized effective theory of the inverse chiral phonon Zeeman effect in noncentrosymmetric crystals. Within micropolar elasticity, coupled translational displacements and microrotations give rise to intrinsically chiral phonons, which generate an elliptically polarized internal magnetic field through dynamical piezoelectricity. Provided that electronic screening is incomplete, this field acts as an effective longitudinal Zeeman field on electronic spins, driving a Floquet response for localized states and a stationary adiabatic band splitting for itinerant electrons, leading to macroscopic spin polarization. In contrast to earlier discussions based on nearly degenerate axial optical modes or externally driven circular lattice motion, the present mechanism relies on finite-wave-number truly chiral phonons whose counter-rotating branches are intrinsically split by crystal chirality. Quantization is introduced to define the single-phonon magnetic-field scale, coherent-state enhancement, and magnetic chirality in a controlled manner. The results establish a purely lattice-driven mechanism for the inverse chiral phonon Zeeman effect in noncentrosymmetric crystals.

authors.name: Jun-ichiro Kishine, A. S. Ovchinnikov, Masahiro Sato, G. N. Makarov, A. D. Lyakhov

papers.title: Time Reversal Symmetry Breaking and {\it Fragile Magnetic Superconductors}
papers.summary: Roughly twenty reports (as of 2025) of time-reversal-symmetry breaking (TRSB) states in low critical temperature (T$_c$) superconducting (SC), otherwise conventional Fermi liquid, metals have emerged primarily from muon spin relaxation ($\mu$SR) data. The detected fields, inferred from the current interpretation of depolarization data, are similar in magnitude and not far above the lower limit of detection, corresponding to magnetizations of no more than 10$^{-3}$ $\mu_B$/atom. These materials comprise a new class of {\it fragile magnetic superconductors} modeled as triplet pairing. The measured SC state properties, excepting only the fields detected below T$_c$, are representative of low T$_c$ singlet BCS SCs, not showing unusual coherence lengths or critical fields. While it is recognized that the muon does affect the sample by displacing nearby atoms and impacting magnetic interaction parameters, the measurement process, changing the system from sample $\rightarrow$ sample+$\mu^+$ thereby breaking TRS, may deserve further scrutiny. This overview provides a survey of the environment of the muon, from the normal state to the superfluid state, where the induced supercurrent and Yu-Shiba-Rusinov gap states provide coupling of the muon moment to the superfluid. The unusual topological superconductor LaNiGa$_2$, currently modeled as non-unitary triplet, is used as a case study. Supposing that the prevailing $\mu$SR inference of a small spontaneous field within the bulk of theSC obtains, the current picture of (possibly non-unitary) triplet pairing is discussed and an attractive alternative for LaNiGa$_2$ is noted.

authors.name: Warren E. Pickett

papers.title: Topological Gyromorphs
papers.summary: Gyromorphs are a new class of disordered systems that combine an amorphous-like absence of translational order with quasi-long-range rotational order. Gyromorphs can outperform quasicrystals or hyperuniform arrangements in forming isotropic band gaps, suggesting an avenue to realize robust disordered topological phases. However, gyromorphs lack exact rotational symmetry, which is only realized on average, posing an obstacle for existing real-space invariants to correctly diagnose topological gyromorphs. In this work we show that gyromorphs can host higher-order topological insulating (HOTI) phases protected by average rotational symmetry, and we develop and systematically compare tools for diagnosing topological phases protected by such symmetry. We introduce symmetry indicators of the effective Hamiltonian based on average rotational symmetries which, when combined with the spectral localizer and a scattering invariant, draw a consistent topological phase diagram. Our work unlocks gyromorphs as a novel platform to study topological phases beyond crystals, quasicrystals, and amorphous materials.

authors.name: Laura G\'omez Paz, Justin Schirmann, Adam Yanis Chaou, Isidora Araya Day, Adolfo G. Grushin

papers.title: Successive single- and double-q $\Gamma_3$ quadrupole orders on the diamond structure
papers.summary: We investigate field-dependent quadrupolar ordering at the L points of the diamond-structure Brillouin zone using classical Monte Carlo simulations of an effective $\Gamma_3$ quadrupole model. We demonstrate that competition between the magnetic field and quadrupole anisotropy leads to a rich phase diagram for magnetic fields applied parallel to [001], which includes switching between a single-q state and a double-q state. We also examine the effects of a symmetry-allowed biquadratic intersite interaction, corresponding to a hexadecapole interaction, on the stability of the double-q state under a magnetic field.

authors.name: Kaito Sasa, Kazumasa Hattori

papers.title: Deterministic Electrical Switching in Altermagnets via Surface Antisymmetry Groups
papers.summary: A surface antisymmetry group framework is developed to establish design rules for deterministic electrical switching of the N\'eel vector in a film of a collinear bipartite antiferromagnet. In centrosymmetric altermagnets, where linear current-induced spin-orbit torques vanish in the bulk, staggered effective fields can nevertheless exist as a macroscopic interfacial response, whose allowed tensor form is determined by the surface antisymmetry point group for the given surface orientation. Such effective fields do not require sublattice equivalence to be broken by the surface and can arise via the Edelstein mechanism driven by sublattice-odd interfacial spin-orbit coupling. General symmetry obstructions to bipolar switching that are valid to all orders in torque angular harmonics are also derived. Separately, the structure of the spin conductivity tensor determines which surface orientations allow transverse spin current generation via the nonrelativistic spin-splitter effect. Taken together, these symmetry-enforced properties establish which surface orientations of $d$-wave altermagnets can serve as deterministically switchable spin current sources in spin-torque heterostructures. Because the design rules are based solely on the surface antisymmetry point group, the symmetry-allowed staggered effective fields are robust against averaging over equilibrium surface roughness.

authors.name: K. D. Belashchenko

papers.title: The multichannel Dyson equation for double ionisation spectroscopies
papers.summary: Several photoemission spectroscopies and, in particular, Auger spectroscopy, involve double-ionization processes. For the numerical simulation of these spectroscopies it is convenient to use the particle-particle channel of the two-body Green's functions since its poles correspond to excitation energies in which the final state has two more particles (holes or electrons) than the initial state. In standard approaches it is approximated within the random phase approximation. As a consequence only the quasiparticles of the photoemission spectrum are captured but none of the satellites features. In this work, we go beyond this approximation by employing the multichannel Dyson equation. By coupling the particle-particle two-body Green's function to the 3-hole-1-electron and 3-electron-1-hole channels of the four-body Green's function, the multichannel Dyson equation incorporates correlations beyond the RPA in a straightforward way. We are thus able to describe both quasiparticles and satellites in the photoemission spectra.

authors.name: Pierre Selli\'e, J. Arjan Berger, Pina Romaniello

papers.title: On flat band engineering and graphene nanomesh magnonics
papers.summary: Graph-theoretic topological frustration is a peculiar situation on a finite piece of the honeycomb lattice that prevents a full pairwise coupling of the lattice sites via nearest neighbor links, even when the total number of sites is an even number and the structure possesses no sublattice imbalance. This type of frustration is inherent for organic molecules that are classified as concealed non-Kekulean hydrocarbons, representing peculiar diradicals. Here we show that this topological frustration persists in two-dimensional systems based on the honeycomb lattice. Such systems exhibit fully flat electronic energy bands located at the Fermi level. Therefore, two-dimensional ultimately flat bands can be systematically and predictably constructed for graphene monolayer nanomeshes. These systems are prone to antiferromagnetic ordering and hybrid spin-wave excitations mixing weak ferromagnetic and strong antiferromagnetic features, which could pave the way towards low-power, compact, and ultrafast organic spintronics with near room-temperature operation.

authors.name: Vasil A. Saroka

papers.title: Adiabatic self-vibrations generated by inelastic Andreev tunneling in a movable Cooper-pair box
papers.summary: Self-sustained oscillators produce stable periodic motion robust to dissipation. Such motion is usually achieved by work fed back into the oscillator, but its performance is often limited by frequency-dependent operation. Here we propose a scheme for self-sustained vibrations without external feedback. We consider a movable Cooper-pair box attached to the free end of a voltage-biased normal-metal pillar. The Cooper-pair box carries an Andreev current subject to an electric field applied perpendicular to the current. In the adiabatic limit, where the Cooper-pair box state follows its motion, vibrational instability occurs, pumped by inelastic Andreev tunneling. Nonlinearity of the Josephson coupling saturates the vibrational amplitude, resulting in two-dimensional self-vibrations. We discuss the advantage of this adiabatic scheme in comparison with feedback-induced self-oscillation.

authors.name: Sunghun Park, Anton V. Parafilo, Leonid Y. Gorelik, Robert I. Shekhter

papers.title: Structural effects of liquid infiltration of 3Y-Zirconia with Sc, Mg and Y
papers.summary: The current work has investigated the effect of co-doping 3Y-Zirconia (3YSZ) with Sc, Mg and Y by liquid infiltration. Pre-sintered porous discs of 3YSZ were immersed in diluted nitric acid solutions containing Sc, Mg or Y, and combinations of the three, trapping liquid within the porosities of the samples. Upon drying, the cations are maintained inside the pellet, making the basis for the co-doping. After sintering, mass increase confirms the co-doping effect. Rietveld refinements of X-ray diffraction data show that the liquid-infiltrated samples contain the tetragonal t, t'' and cubic c-phase in various fractions depending on the doping elements. The phases are compared with 3YSZ and 5YSZ sintered for 0 hours and 2 hours at 1500 {\deg}C. To evaluate the material properties in an application-based perspective, the Knoop hardness, translucency and grain size was measured. We conclude that liquid infiltration is a viable route to perform co-doping of Zirconia.

authors.name: Asbj{\o}rn Slagtern Fjellv{\aa}g, {\O}ystein Slagtern Fjellv{\aa}g, Amund Ruud

papers.title: Shapiro steps of superfluid Fermi gases in a ring trap across the BCS--BEC crossover
papers.summary: We investigate the transport properties of a superfluid Fermi gas confined in a ring trap with a moving potential barrier across the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) to Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) crossover. Employing time-dependent Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) equations, we simulate the dynamics of a Josephson junction biased by both DC and AC currents. Over a wide range of interaction strengths, the barrier-velocity dependence of the chemical potential difference exhibits low-order plateau structures, consistent with Shapiro steps, with fitted levels close to integer multiples of $\hbar\omega/2$ within the phase-coherent regime. This factor of $1/2$ reflects our convention of defining the chemical potential per single fermion in the BdG framework. Microscopic analysis reveals that these fundamental steps originate from synchronized phase slips mediated by periodic soliton generation at the barrier. Our findings clarify the role of interaction regimes in the nonequilibrium phase dynamics of ring-trapped fermionic superfluids and provide microscopic insights relevant to future studies of atomtronic systems with nontrivial topology.

authors.name: Hikaru Kuriki, Masaya Kunimi, Tetsuro Nikuni

papers.title: High temperature Jahn-Teller distortion and short-range order in CsCuCl$_3$
papers.summary: CsCuCl$_3$, chiral and Jahn-Teller distorted at room temperature, takes a more symmetric structure above 423 K. Describing this 'simpler' high temperature structure is far from simple and has been the subject of many, sometimes contradicting, studies. Here we reinvestigate the high temperature structure of CsCuCl$_3$, its thermal stability, and its effect on room temperature chirality. In situ pair distribution function data from powder neutron diffraction confirms that CsCuCl$_3$ is Jahn-Teller distorted both below and above $T_\mathrm{c}$, and provides a quantitative view of short-range order in the high temperature structure. In situ powder x-ray diffraction shows that CsCuCl$_3$ does not undergo any additional structural changes above 423 K and is congruently melting. In situ single crystal x-ray diffraction experiments reveal that the phase transition induces domains of mixed handedness in originally homochiral crystals. These findings contribute to a better understanding of phase transitions in Jahn-Teller distorted compounds, and highlight the potential use of phase transitions to control chiral domains.

authors.name: Emma A. Pappas, Toby Woods, Jue Liu, Daniel P. Shoemaker

papers.title: Criticality and Quench Dynamics at the Anderson Transition of a Chern Insulator
papers.summary: We study the critical properties and non-equilibrium dynamics of the topological Anderson phase transition in a strongly disordered Chern insulator. We show that a critical length scale emerges in the real-space profile of the local Chern marker and matches the corresponding correlation-length critical exponent found in the literature. We further determine the dynamical critical exponent from the frequency-dependent conductivity, finding values consistent with those of non-interacting models in the integer quantum Hall universality class. We then ramp the disorder strength across the phase transition and investigate the ensuing non-equilibrium dynamics. In contrast to clean topological systems, the spectral gap is closed due to localized states and consequently the generation of excitations does not exhibit Kibble-Zurek scaling. Despite this, we find that the non-equilibrium length scale extracted from the local Chern marker shows signatures of the Kibble-Zurek scaling. Our results demonstrate that the non-equilibrium dynamics of the topological Anderson transition features decoupling between the excitations and the emergent length scale as known from clean systems, and establish the local Chern marker as a probe of the emergent length scale during the quench.

authors.name: Lara Ul\v{c}akar, Jernej Mravlje, Gal Lemut, Toma\v{z} Rejec

papers.title: Why dimensional analysis works: general classification of self-similarity based on scale-invariance
papers.summary: In this work, we formulate self-similarity from the perspective of scale invariance, where a self-similar form is understood as the transformation of a function into a form invariant under scale transformations. By applying this formulation to physical parameters, which consist of numerical values and units, it is demonstrated that dimensional analysis works for physical problems because scale invariance is partially shared between units and physical parameters. This naturally leads to the distinction between similarity of the first kind and similarity of the second kind according to whether the scale functions induced by units and those associated with physical parameters are equivalent or not. Self-similar solutions of the second kind can be further classified according to whether the power exponents of the similarity parameters include functions of dimensionless numbers. This leads to the conclusion that there are three kinds of self-similar solutions. The present work provides a unified framework for understanding dimensional analysis and a universal classification of self-similarity in physical problems.

authors.name: Hirokazu Maruoka

papers.title: Rare Events Govern Defect Formation under Weak Symmetry Breaking
papers.summary: Crossing a continuous phase transition out of equilibrium typically generates topological defects whose density obeys a universal power-law scaling predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism. Recent numerical studies have revealed systematic deviations from this scaling in the presence of weak explicit symmetry breaking, manifested as an additional exponential suppression of defect formation. However, the origin of this correction and a general theoretical framework to describe it have remained elusive. Here, using large-deviation theory, we show that defect formation under weak symmetry breaking is controlled by rare fluctuations that drive local regions into the disfavored symmetry-broken state. Within mean-field theory, this mechanism yields a closed-form expression for the defect density in arbitrary dimensions, valid in the weak-field and weak-noise limits. These theoretical predictions are verified through direct simulations of stochastic Ginzburg-Landau models in one and two spatial dimensions.

authors.name: Jiang Liu, Peng Yang, Matteo Baggioli

papers.title: Quantum Tunneling-induced Hybridization and Coherent Dynamics of Jackiw-Rebbi Zero Modes in a Modified Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Chain
papers.summary: We investigate analytically and numerically the tunneling-induced hybridization and coherent dynamics of Jackiw-Rebbi zero modes in a modified Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. Unlike the conventional SSH model, this modified system possess two bulk gap-closing points, namely the quadratic-type gap-closing point at momenta $k_0=0$ and the Dirac-type gap-closing points at $k_0=\pm\pi/4a$. Although the quadratic point does not support a topological domain wall due to the absence of mass inversion, the low-energy Dirac theory around $k_0=\pm\pi/4a$ predicts an effective mass that changes sign at two spatially separated domain walls under a kink profile, generating a pair of JR bound states with each states localized at one of those domain walls. We show that the finite spatial overlap between the JR zero modes lifts the zero-energy degeneracy through quantum tunneling, producing symmetric-antisymmetric hybridized states. Using an effective two-level description, we demonstrate that hybridized JR modes undergo coherent tunneling oscillations between the two domain walls, accompanied by periodic transfer of sublattice polarization between the (A,C) and (B,D) sectors. Our results establish a unified framework connecting JR zero modes, quantum tunneling, and coherent dynamics in modified SSH systems, offering a promising platform for controllable topological quantum-state transfer in engineered lattice structures.

authors.name: Surajit Mandal

papers.title: Oxygen-nonstoichiometry-driven phase transition in $\mathrm{Sr}_{1-x}\mathrm{Nd}_{x}\mathrm{CoO}_{3-\delta}$ ($x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$) perovskites
papers.summary: We report a systematic study of the interplay between oxygen nonstoichiometry, crystal structure, and magnetic/electrotransport properties in $\mathrm{Sr}_{1-x}\mathrm{Nd}_{x}\mathrm{CoO}_{3-\delta}$ ($x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3$). High-resolution neutron powder diffraction combined with synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction reveals that increasing the oxygen content induces a structural transition from a layered $I4/mmm$ ($2a_p \times 2a_p \times 4a_p$) to an oxygen-deficient orthorhombic $Pmmm$ ($a_p \times a_p \times 2a_p$) phases with preferential oxygen-vacancy occupation. This transition is accompanied by a crossover from G-type antiferromagnetic with a weak ferromagnetic component to a ferromagnetic state, and a drastic decay in resistivity. The evolution of the magnetic and transport properties is discussed in terms of changes in the Co spin state, enhanced Co $3d$ - O $2p$ orbital overlap upon oxygen uptake, and a magnetically inhomogeneous ferromagnetic state associated with residual oxygen vacancies and mixed $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}/\mathrm{Co}^{4+}$ valence. Our findings experimentally confirm that the stabilization of the layered "314" structure is driven by the presence and ordering of oxygen vacancies rather than A-site cation ordering, whereas the oxygen-deficient oxidized compounds represent an intermediate orthorhombic state preceding fully stoichiometric phases.

authors.name: Nina Tereshko, Roman Lanovsky, Olivier Toulemonde, Maxim Bushinsky, Stanislav Savvin, Vadim Sikolenko, Lingyan Xu, Aleksandr Nikitin

papers.title: Phonons under confinement: Finite Hilbert space, coarse-grained $U(1)$ charge and a new transport mechanism
papers.summary: An important feature of solid-state or cold atom systems in low dimensions is the restricted oscillations of ionic/atomic degrees of freedom in the confining directions, for which the conventional phonon from canonical quantization is not an ideal description. In this work we propose a general recipe to introduce this feature to otherwise unrestricted systems by mapping displacement fields to spin degrees of freedom, dubbed "soft-corization". In the strong-confinement limit $S=1/2$, we demonstrate the validity of the approach with a harmonic chain; the results lead to a gapped fermionic model showing the absence of acoustic modes as a signature of the confinement of the entire chain. Despite the non-conserved total particle number in the presence of nearest-neighbor parings, the model holds a coarse-grained $U(1)$ symmetry with conserved "polarization charge" in the absence of nearest-neighbor hopping. This enables a new transport mechanism via "dimer-tumbling" instead of single-particle hopping. We then introduce a short-range interaction via anharmonicity; for energy scales slightly above the gap, it leads to a (quantum) phase transition to a nonreciprocal state carrying dimer current and heat current with spontaneous time reversal symmetry breaking of the type $\hat{T}^2=+1$. The non-reciprocity can be probed by measuring the change of inductance due to gauge fields in and out of the ordered phase.

authors.name: Yuan Gao, K. A. Muttalib

papers.title: Electrical Control over Volatile Mott Switching through Non-Volatile Memory Effects
papers.summary: Vanadium Dioxide (VO2) and Vanadium Sesquioxide (V2O3) are Mott insulators that undergo an Insulator-to-Metal Transition (IMT) at ~340K and ~160K, respectively, manifested as an orders-of-magnitude reduction in their electrical resistance. These transitions provide the physical basis for their Volatile Resistive Switching (VRS) behavior, making them promising candidates for threshold-switching devices. Here, we show that the volatile switching in these materials can be strongly affected by non-volatile processes associated with the creation and annihilation of the conducting filament. These processes give rise to pronounced memory effects in which the initial switching voltage substantially exceeds that of subsequent cycles. We identify two distinct mechanisms underlying this behavior in different thermal regimes. In the phase-coexistence regime, a memory effect is observed in V2O3, arising from the spatial redistribution of metallic and insulating domains. Well below the hysteresis regime, an additional electroforming-like memory effect is observed in both VO2 and V2O3 which is attributed to the formation and/or migration of defects under the influence of a high electric field and a current surge associated with the IMT-driven switching. Using a protective internal resistor and a multi-step writing protocol, this normally destructive process can be harnessed to tune the switching voltage and power over a wide temperature range. These results demonstrate a route toward controlled programming of switching parameters in IMT-based resistive switching devices.

authors.name: Amihai Kronman (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Gil Levi (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Haifa, Israel), Yoav Kalcheim (Department of Materials Science and Engineering, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Haifa, Israel)

papers.title: Why Ammoniated Lithium Borohydrides Liquefy and Resolidify?
papers.summary: Ammonia (NH$_3$) absorption drives LiBH$_4\cdot x$NH$_3$ through a re-entrant ``solid--liquid--solid'' transition: LiBH$_4\cdot$NH$_3$ is a well-defined solid ammoniate, compositions near LiBH$_4\cdot 2$NH$_3$ are liquid-like or partially liquefied, whereas LiBH$_4\cdot 3$NH$_3$ returns to a more rigid non-liquid ammoniate state. However, the microscopic origin of this unintuitive response remains a long-lasting mystery. Here, we uncover its mechanism. Cross-database analysis identifies borohydrides as a particularly state-diverse and composition-responsive material family. Structure prediction and ab initio molecular simulations reveal that increasing NH$_3$ loading increases the direct Li--N coordination number while progressively decreasing BH$_4^-$-associated contacts in the local Li environment. Near $x \approx 2$, these contributions are most balanced among the simulated compositions, and the sampled Li--N/N$\cdots$B coordination landscape is broadest. Further ammoniation produces Li--N-dominant coordination and slower BH$_4^-$/NH$_3$ contact renewal, accompanying recovery of a more rigid ammoniate state. Pressure--composition isotherm, $^1$H and $^{11}$B nuclear magnetic resonance, and Raman measurements support this non-monotonic state evolution and associated BH$_4^-$/NH$_3$ reorganization. These findings transform ammonia-induced liquefaction from an empirical phase anomaly into a competition between native-network disruption, mixed-coordination frustration, and ligand-built network reconstruction, providing a framework for chemically switching between transport-favouring fluidity and stability-favouring rigidity in hydrogen-rich materials.

authors.name: Qian Wang, Zixin Xu, Ryuhei Sato, Yiming Lu, Hiroki Miyaoka, Takayuki Ichikawa, Eric Jianfeng Cheng, Shin-ichi Orimo, Fangqin Guo, Hao Li

papers.title: A Phase-Field Study of Desiccation Crack Pattern Maturation under Drying-Wetting Cycles
papers.summary: The characteristic intersection angle of the desiccation crack relaxes from near \ang{90} toward \ang{120} under repeated drying--wetting cycles. However, the theoretical understanding of this relaxation is insufficient, especially the modeling of the drying--wetting cycles. Here we introduce a phase-field model of desiccation fracture, extending the model proposed in previous studies by adding crack healing and a scar effect left by past cracks. By repeating drying--wetting cycles in a finite element simulation, we find that the angle distribution develops a growing peak near \ang{120} as the cycle number increases, consistent with experiments. The standard deviation of the intersection angle from \ang{120} relaxes exponentially with a characteristic time of about 2.85 cycles. These results are consistent with experiments, except that the characteristic time is slightly smaller than the experimental value. Crack energy dominates the total energy and also relaxes exponentially with nearly the same characteristic cycle as the angle relaxation. This decay is driven mainly by a shortening of the effective crack length rather than a change in effective fracture toughness.

authors.name: Hiroki Fukushima, Satoshi Yukawa
