papers.title: Thermodynamic Geometry of an Ideal Quon Gas
papers.summary: We investigate the equilibrium thermodynamics and thermodynamic Riemannian geometry of an ideal quon gas within the grand canonical ensemble. By incorporating the algebraic deformation parameter $q$, the system generalizes standard bosonic behavior while recovering the conventional ideal Bose gas in the undeformed limit. A rigorous examination of the ground-state occupation reveals two disconnected mathematical domains of the fugacity. By enforcing thermodynamic continuity, single-valuedness, and consistency with the high-temperature classical limit, we exclude the second mathematical branch and establish the lower interval as the unique physically admissible state space. This identifies the deformation parameter as an intrinsic, generalized Bose--Einstein condensation threshold. Employing the Fisher-Rao metric on the equilibrium parameter manifold, we probe the thermodynamic scalar curvature across all temperature regimes. The scalar curvature remains strictly positive throughout the physical domain, confirming that the deformation preserves an effectively attractive statistical interaction without inducing fermionic tendencies. Near the critical condensation threshold, the curvature increases sharply and exhibits a definitive divergence, providing an unambiguous geometric signature of macroscopic coherence and critical fluctuations. Below the transition temperature, the pinning of fugacity eliminates a fluctuating degree of freedom, collapsing the scalar curvature to zero.

authors.name: Leila Yousefzadeh, Hosein Mohammadzadeh, Habib Esmaili, Zahra Ebadi, Morteza Nattagh Najafi

papers.title: Activity-Induced Structural and Dynamical Heterogeneity in Colloidal Gels
papers.summary: Active gels are intrinsically non-equilibrium materials whose structural and dynamical heterogeneity emerges from the interplay of attractive interactions, thermal fluctuations, and self-propulsion. We investigate a model active gel, simulated using large-scale Brownian dynamics simulations, to explore the effects of temperature $T$, active force strength $f_0$, persistence timescale $\tau_p$, and active particle concentration $\rho_a$. We characterize the structure of the evolving gel network through morphological analysis, while dynamical changes are quantified by the relaxation timescale and dynamical heterogeneity (DH). We show that an optimal choice of activity parameters yields a percolating gel network with faster gelation and larger voids and clusters, enhancing mechanical stability. Conversely, the structural relaxation timescale and DH decrease with increasing activity, indicating enhanced particle rearrangements and reduced spatial correlations of mobile and immobile regions. An effective temperature ($T_\text{eff}$) framework for colloidal gels maps structural quantities and relaxation timescales in an active gel onto those of a passive gel. More interestingly, the growth of DH with increasing swim force can also be described by the same effective-temperature framework, in stark contrast to observations in active glasses. Our findings show that, in colloidal gels, temperature and active force compete, giving rise to similar structural ordering and, consequently, similar DH at the same $T_\text{eff}$. These findings highlight the crucial role of structural ordering in governing DH in active colloidal gels, as compared to active glasses.

authors.name: Santu Nath, Sudipta Mandal, Smarajit Karmakar

papers.title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ via $^{139}$La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the $Am2m$ Structure
papers.summary: The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. Within the $Am2m$ framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.

authors.name: Mitsuharu Yashima, Hongnam Lee, Takumi Ino, Nina Seto, Masataka Kakoi, Hiroya Sakurai, Yoshihiko Takano, Hidekazu Mukuda

papers.title: $d$-wave superconductivity in quintuple-layer bulk superconductor La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$
papers.summary: The recent realization of bulk superconductivity in the quintuple-layer nickelate La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ opens new opportunities to probe the pairing symmetry of the reduced Ruddlesden--Popper (RP) nickelate family. Using an effective five-layer Hubbard model and variational Monte Carlo calculations, we find that a spin-singlet $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave state is energetically favored, while extended $s$-wave pairing is strongly suppressed. Based on the optimized superconducting state, we further calculate several experimentally accessible observables. The tunneling density of states exhibits a characteristic V-shaped low-energy spectrum, the superfluid density shows a linear low-temperature depletion, the Knight shift decreases below $T_c$, and the spin-lattice relaxation rate follows $1/T_1T\propto T^2$, together providing consistent signatures of a clean nodal superconductor. Extending the same framework to related reduced RP nickelates, we find a robust $d$-wave tendency in infinite-layer LaNiO$_{2}$, while trilayer La$_4$Ni$_3$O$_{8}$ at its nominal filling lies close to the boundary between $d$-wave superconductivity and a non-superconducting state. These results establish bulk La$_6$Ni$_5$O$_{12}$ as a promising platform for determining the pairing symmetry of nickelate superconductors and suggest a common $d_{x^2-y^2}$-wave pairing tendency across the reduced RP nickelate family.

authors.name: Zhan Wang, Yuxin Wang, Hui-Ke Jin, Kun Jiang, Jiangping Hu

papers.title: Run-and-tumble particles in a harmonic external field: constructing the solution of the Fokker-Planck equation from the equations of motion
papers.summary: A method for integrating the Langevin equations of motion for run-and-tumble particles is introduced to compute the joint distribution of their position and active velocity, with and without a harmonic external force field. The key step is the construction of the moments of the distribution and the correlation functions, conditional on the particles being in a specific state at the final time. For one-dimensional run-and-tumble particles in a harmonic external potential, the exact steady-state distributions for the tumble state, as well as for the run state conditional on a specified velocity direction, are obtained. This enables us to demonstrate their equivalence to the exact solutions of the corresponding Fokker-Planck equations.

authors.name: Aoran Sun, Fangfu Ye, Jeff Z. Y. Chen

papers.title: Continuum neural wavefunctions for anyons on a torus: superfluidity in the semion gas
papers.summary: Mobile anyons in topologically ordered phases provide a setting to investigate how fractional exchange statistics shapes collective behavior at finite density. We introduce AnyFormer: a neural variational framework for continuum anyons on a torus that explicitly incorporates statistical interactions and global winding constraints. We construct a smooth orbital frame that enforces the matrix-valued torus boundary conditions, and supplement it with an analytic pair factor that supplies the regular collision behavior. The orbital geometry and many-body amplitudes are optimized in parallel by variational Monte Carlo. We apply AnyFormer to semions without an external field or interaction potential, isolating unique correlations generated solely by statistics. Our framework closely matches exact two-semion energies and yields lower variational energies than finite-cutoff exact diagonalization for $N = 4$ and $6$ semions. Scaling up to $N = 16$ semions, well beyond the limits of continuum diagonalization, we find a largely uniform liquid with pronounced correlation holes and an approximately linear structure factor at the smallest accessible wavevectors. The pair circulation reverses near the mean particle spacing, revealing chiral relative motion. We then identify paired superfluid behavior through spatially persistent coherence of compact semion pairs, carried by a counter-rotating pair channel. The ansatz is not biased toward pairing, so this result emerges from energy minimization alone. AnyFormer thus provides a scalable variational neural-net framework for microscopic studies of correlations, chiral motion, and collective phases of bulk anyonic matter.

authors.name: Ahmed Khalifa, Shubhayu Chatterjee

papers.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moir\'e Mott insulator
papers.summary: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moir\'e semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moir\'e Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. The stripe phases were revealed by electrical transport studies as a thermodynamic phase transition from a high temperature isotropic phase to a low-temperature anisotropic phase accompanied by a Fermi surface reconstruction. Near the stripe-to-superconductor transition, we also observed an additional thermodynamic phase transition from metallic stripes to pinned insulating stripes. The stripe-to-superconductor transition further exhibits an intriguing self-similarity that highlights the intimate relationship between the two orders. Our results pave the path for studying intertwined orders in moir\'e materials.

authors.name: Yichi Zhang, Yiyu Xia, Zhongdong Han, Jekwan Lee, Brandon Bauer, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Wenjin Zhao, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan

papers.title: Strain-Glass Dynamics in the Superionic Conductor Na$_3$PS$_4$
papers.summary: Ionic conduction in solid-state electrolytes is conventionally described by mobile cations migrating through a static host lattice. Yet the fastest conductors are often the most disordered, and how disorder enhances transport remains unresolved at the mesoscale, inaccessible to ensemble-averaged probes. We use Bragg X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy to measure nanoscale structural dynamics of a single ball-milled Na$_3$PS$_4$ particle. We find that the cubic phase behaves as a strain glass: a frustrated configuration of three degenerate tetragonal variants with short-range order. Its domain-wall motion is stress-driven, crossing over irreversibly to thermally activated dynamics on annealing as residual milling stress is depleted. Rearrangements follow scale-free avalanche statistics, matching ferroelastic martensites but without external driving. The tetragonal polymorph shows none of these features and relaxes fifty times more slowly. These dynamics occur on timescales comparable to estimated ionic diffusion across the particle, indicating the host structure cannot be assumed static on transport-relevant timescales.

authors.name: Erik S. Lamb, Nicol\`o D'Anna, Phillip Ridley, Nelson Hua, Ivan Zaluzhnyy, James Burrow, Emilio Escauriza, Robin Glefke, Boyan K. Stoychev, Mingze Wan, Zhe Ren, Fabian Westermeier, Michael Sprung, Alex Fra\~n\'o, Ying Shirley Meng, Oleg G. Shpyrko

papers.title: Statistical approach of random packing of polydisperse similar hyperspheres: with application to binomial and lognormal size distributions
papers.summary: This paper addresses the packing fraction of polydisperse similar hyperspheres with a discrete binomial and continuous lognormal particle size distribution. First, a closed form expression is derived of a mix consisting of multiple discrete particles in D-dimensional Euclidean space R^D with small size differences. A recently developed analytical model for binary packings with small size ratio u is used, here applying it to the statistically probable particle pairs in the multi-sized mix. The new model is subsequently applied to discretely sized particles with a binomial number distribution and a constant size ratio u between each subsequent particle size. By taking the limit of u -> 1 and an infinite number of particles sizes, the binomial particle distribution is transformed into a continuous lognormal distribution. The resulting expression for the packing fraction can be solved in closed form, resulting in an original expression for the packing fraction of mixtures of hyperparticles with a lognormal distribution. This explicit expression is governed by the standard deviation, the Euclidean dimension D, and the monosized packing fraction of the considered particle shape. For a number of particle shapes and their packing modes (from looser to denser) the scaled expression is thoroughly compared with data reported in the literature. They concern packed particles with small standard deviations and in Euclidean dimensions D = 2 and 3, and good agreement is found. For large standard deviations the scaled packing fraction approaches a limiting value, which appears not to depend on the Euclidean dimension. Based on the insight, a closed form expression is put forward for the packing fraction that matches the small standard deviation solution, and the large standard deviation asymptote, so covering arbitrary standard deviations, Euclidean dimensions, particle types, and their mode of packing.

authors.name: H. J. H. Brouwers

papers.title: Ta-based S-I-S junctions for integrated superconducting electronics
papers.summary: In this work, we have presented S-I-S Josephson junctions with $\rm\alpha$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ barrier. We grew base and top ${\alpha}$-Ta electrodes using seed layer engineering, showing both Nb and ${\rm TaN}_x$ are viable seed layer choices, and particularly emphasize that at room temperature a re-seed layer is required to nucleate $\rm\alpha$-Ta for the top electrode. However, we note that the choice of seed layer can have subtle implications on the electrical tunneling behavior of the junctions. We used room-temperature probing of variable junction areas, combined with Ambegaokar-Baratoff physics, to characterize the wafer scale critical current densities. For 0.4 $\mu$m$^2$ junctions, we found junction spreads as low as 2.0% across the 20 x 20 mm chip relevant for device performance. The entire process was carried out using standard industry foundry processing using 150 mm wafer tooling, which is an important step towards proving that Ta-based junctions can be implemented at scale. We have successfully fabricated and tested junctions with $\rm\alpha$-Ta electrodes and a ${\rm TaO}_x$ insulating tunnel barrier, demonstrating that this is a material platform which merits further investigation and studies for potential application in classical and quantum superconducting technologies.

authors.name: Trent Borman, Cameron Bullock, Cole Chason, Bradley Christensen, Jonathan Cochran, Emad Din, Evan Donohue, Jason Flagg, A. L. Graninger, Eric Jones, Robert Klaes, Shawn Keebaugh, Erin Kennedy, John Kula, Jason Lapano, Melissa Loving, Christopher Pasco, Devika Pathan, Tam Pham, Timothy Pillsbury, Robert Pownall, Paige Quarterman, Jacob Ruf, Jade Simmons, Nathan Siwak, Joel Strand, Yong Mo Yang

papers.title: Vortices in a two-dimensional fermionic superfluid
papers.summary: Quantized vortices are a hallmark of superfluidity. They have proven to be an indispensable probe for systems ranging from superfluid helium to type-II superconductors. In ultracold two-dimensional (2D) Fermi gases, where phase fluctuations are enhanced and the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) mechanism governs the superfluid transition, their observation has remained elusive. Here, we report on the controlled creation of quantized vortices in a homogeneous 2D gas in the BEC--BCS crossover. By continuously tuning the velocity of two moving obstacles, we observe quantized steps in the absolute vortex charge. Matter-wave interferometry reveals the characteristic phase winding, quantized in units of $2\pi$. Measurements on 2D and 3D gases show a striking difference: only in 2D does the vortex number grow with temperature, reflecting thermal activation of BKT vortex pairs. Our approach provides evidence of fermionic superfluidity in 2D and offers a means to study BKT physics, vortex-controlled transport and resistance, as well as to detect unconventional superfluidity in spin-imbalanced 2D gases.

authors.name: Artak Mkrtchyan, Hans Leonard Michel, Moritz von Usslar, Ren\'e Henke, Cesar R. Cabrera, Henning Moritz

papers.title: Designing tunable hyperuniformity in random organization through nonlocal noise
papers.summary: Hyperuniform fluids suppress density fluctuations at large length scales, but microscopic protocols for designing their asymptotic scaling remain limited. Here we show how effective driving noise generated by particle dynamics can select the hyperuniform exponent while preserving ordinary diffusion and pairwise center-of-mass conservation of the organized particles. We establish this connection through two protocols based on biased random organization (BRO). First, a two-dimensional BRO layer is nonreciprocally coupled to a three-dimensional Brownian gas through density-dependent kick amplitudes. Bulk density fluctuations generate spatially nonlocal noise with a $q^3$ power spectrum in the adiabatic limit, producing $S(q\to0)\sim q^1$. Second, we introduce reciprocal kicks whose lengths follow a Pareto-like distribution, $P(\ell)\sim\ell^{-1-b}$. For $2<b<4$, the finite second moment supports ordinary diffusion, while the divergent fourth moment changes the long-wavelength noise spectrum to $q^b$. The corresponding fluctuating density field theory predicts continuously tunable hyperuniform scaling, $S(q\to0)\sim q^{b-2}$, supported by particle simulations. Together, these results connect targeted hyperuniform scaling to explicit microscopic dynamics and provide a physical basis for designing collective density correlations in nonequilibrium particle systems.

authors.name: Yusheng Lei, Yuhan Peng, Ran Ni

papers.title: Twisting the pseudo-magnetic field lattice in periodically strained Graphene
papers.summary: Periodic deformations flatten electronic bands of graphene which could host strongly correlated electrons similar to those observed in twisted graphene bilayers. The most spectacular effects of strong correlations like superconductivity or magnetism have however not yet been observed despite several experimental attempts. Here, we use tight-binding calculations to investigate the effect of twisting the periodic strain lattice with respect to the atomic lattice. We find that misaligning the two lattices kills the band flattening. We also report on the universal behavior of the band flattening by periodic strain which is controlled by a single parameter, a pseudo-magnetic field flux. Our study strongly suggests that controlling the twist of the strain lattice is essential to unlock the potential of periodic strains in graphene.

authors.name: L-M. Benneka, T. Rhouma, C. B. Winkelmann, M. Zelsmann, G. Trambly de Laissardi\`ere, V. T. Renard

papers.title: Antiferromagnetic Long-Range Order in a Lattice Fermion Model
papers.summary: We study a lattice fermion model with antiferromagnetic interactions on the three-dimensional cubic lattice. The hopping term of the Hamiltonian has a Weyl-type dispersion. We prove that the model has reflection positivity. Moreover, by relying on the property, we prove the existence of the antiferromagnetic long-range order at low temperatures in a strong coupling regime.

authors.name: Yukimi Goto, Tohru Koma

papers.title: Factual recall in linear associative memories: sharp asymptotics and mechanistic insights
papers.summary: Large language models excel at factual recall, yet the fundamental limits of storing input--output associations with neural networks remain unclear. We study these limits in a minimal setting: a linear associative memory that maps $p$ input embeddings in $\mathbb{R}^d$ to their $d$-dimensional targets via a linear layer, requiring each mapped input to score its own target above all other outputs. Since all inputs compete for the same outputs, these constraints are strongly correlated, which makes the storage capacity $p_c$ --- the largest number of associations that can be stored --- hard to characterise. We address this in three steps. First, we introduce a decoupled model, in which each input competes with its own independent set of outputs, and provide numerical and analytical evidence that it is equivalent to the original model, both in capacity and in the structure of the learnt solution. Second, using tools from statistical physics, we show that the decoupled model has capacity $p_c \log p_c / d^2 = 1/2$, extend this computation to linear two-layer networks, and go beyond the capacity by predicting the spectrum of the learnt weights and the storage mechanism. The latter explains how the optimal solution outperforms a na\"ive Hebbian rule: rather than boosting input--output alignments with broad fluctuations, it raises the correct scores just above the extreme-value threshold set by the competing outputs. Third, we prove the decoupled model's capacity thresholds rigorously, including in the non-convex two-layer case; combined with a recent proof for the original model, this shows that both models have the same capacity for full-rank weights. These findings give a sharp characterisation of factual storage in linear networks, and suggest decoupling as a general tool for memorisation and learning problems in which each input must be matched to one of an extensive number of outputs.

authors.name: Alessio Giorlandino, Sebastian Goldt, Antoine Maillard

papers.title: Neural networks become centroid classifiers when trained on heavily corrupted inputs
papers.summary: Learning from imperfect data is a central theme in machine learning, connecting practical questions of robustness to fundamental questions of learnability. Here we examine attribute noise: learning from corrupted inputs while keeping the labels intact, a setting that has received considerably less analytical attention than its label-noise counterpart. We consider two types of corruption models: additive noise and replacement noise. Through experiments with multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) on corrupted classification datasets, we find that neural networks remain robust, maintaining well-above-chance accuracy even when inputs are >90% corrupted -- far beyond human recognition. To understand this robustness, we analyze infinite-width networks in the heavy-corruption regime using a mean-field-inspired approach and derive a leading-order decision rule for the classification outcome: the network implements a prototype rule, the nearest-class-mean, assigning each test point to the class whose training-set average it most closely resembles. This leading-order decision rule is universal across a broad range of MLP architectures, holding for any depth, as well as a wide class of activation functions and noise distributions. The same centroid mechanism closely matches finite-width network behavior in our experiments and provides an interpretable and analytically tractable account of why learning can succeed even when individual training examples carry almost no signal.

authors.name: Justin Tahmassebpur, Asadullah Bhuiyan, Hyejin Kim, Omri Lesser

papers.title: Data-Driven Stochastic LQR Control with Probabilistic Guarantees and Uncertainty Refinement
papers.summary: This paper presents a probabilistic framework for the direct, data-driven synthesis of the stochastic linear- quadratic output-feedback control for linear systems sub- ject to process and measurement noise. Using delayed input-output measurements, we derive a lifted parameter- ization together with an equivalent lifted linear quadratic cost, enabling controller synthesis without explicitly identi- fying the lifted dynamics. Two complementary closed-loop formulations, based on trajectory and covariance represen- tations, are then developed, whose uncertainties depend only on the realized but unknown lifted noise. We char- acterize the relative performance of the two formulations in finite-data regimes. High-probability uncertainty bounds are developed for realized noises, leading to a convex optimization solution to the problem, whose feasibility cer- tifies probabilistic mean-square stability (p-MSS) and per- formance guarantees. To reduce conservatism, Gaussian zonotopes are used to refine uncertainty sets by elimi- nating noise realizations inconsistent with measured data, and a novel intersection rule enables the consistent fusion of data-driven and physics-informed information. These components are integrated into an adaptive framework that unifies indirect (identification-based) and direct (control- oriented) data-driven linear-quadratic output-feedback con- trol. Unlike existing direct data-driven LQR methods that verify stability a posteriori, our by-construction approach achieves robust stability alongside reduced conservatism and superior performance. Simulation results show that the proposed controller approaches the ideal optimal solution while outperforming existing data-driven methods under noisy measurements.

authors.name: Amir Modares, Charalambous Themistoklis, Hamidreza Modares

papers.title: Barrier-State-Based Safe Navigation in Complex Environments Using Look-Ahead Safety Corridors
papers.summary: Safe navigation in cluttered environments requires a safety representation that captures the available motion space along the planned path. A single local safe region may restrict progress through narrow passages and continuous turns. This paper presents a planning-guided look-ahead safety corridor framework for barrier-state-based navigation. Local safe convex polytopes are constructed around collision-free seeds along the forward reference path. Their facet constraints are combined using softmin, and the local functions are fused using softmax with entropy-based adaptive compensation. The resulting safe set remains within the union of the local polytopes while reducing the shrinkage caused by fixed compensation. A Poisson boundary-value problem then defines a differentiable interior safety field while preserving the prescribed corridor boundary. This field is embedded into the robot dynamics through one geometric barrier state. We establish sufficient conditions for corridor invariance based on barrier-state boundedness and active-corridor validity. Navigation simulations cover cluttered layouts, narrow passages, and moving obstacles. A differential-drive ground vehicle further demonstrates navigation through narrow passages and among obstacles absent from the prior map.

authors.name: Yunlin Wei, Fangfei Li, Junhui Zhang

papers.title: CLRM: Cross-Layer Relation Modeling for Audio Deepfake Detection
papers.summary: Audio deepfake detection (ADD) aims to distinguish bonafide speech from synthetic or manipulated speech. Representations from different layers of self-supervised learning (SSL) speech encoders vary in their ability to distinguish bonafide from spoofed speech. Comparing representations of the same utterance across encoder depths may reveal useful spoofing cues, yet common layer-selection and aggregation methods do not provide these comparisons as detection inputs. We propose Cross-Layer Relation Modeling (\ours{}), which explicitly encodes cross-layer relations alongside layer-specific features, making both directly available for ADD. CLRM reuses the existing detector's SSL encoder and identifies informative layer pairs by combining speaker-relative representation geometry with source-domain detection performance. The resulting relation score is fused with the detector's original score, requiring only the training of compact relation heads and fusion parameters while keeping the existing detector frozen. Across five external datasets, CLRM reduces the mean equal error rate (EER) for all three evaluated detectors, achieving relative reductions of 7.8--16.7%. Controlled comparisons with identical layer summaries and approximately matched auxiliary-head parameter counts also show a lower mean EER for explicit relations than direct concatenation, both before and after score fusion. These findings support explicit cross-layer comparisons as useful detection inputs for SSL-based audio deepfake detectors.

authors.name: Yangyang Qu, Siqing Qin, Kong Aik Lee, Massimiliano Todisco

papers.title: Decentralized Impedance Specifications for Grid-Connected Converters: a Sequence-Domain Gershgorin Method, and a Frequency-Wise Framework for Combining Different Criteria
papers.summary: In complex grid scenarios, with many power electronics (PE) converters connected, having specifications for converters can ease the design process. A practical approach is to impose the specifications on the converter's small-signal impedance in the frequency domain. This is advantageous since impedance is a physical property that can be measured. This paper focuses on providing decentralized impedance specifications for each converter connected to an ac bus. With decentralized specifications, each converter has its own specifications, which are independent of other converters' impedance. This enables a competitive multi-vendor environment while guaranteeing system stability. Existing methods of imposing decentralized specifications, based on the small-gain, passivity and Gershgorin theorems, are formulated within a common frequency-domain framework. Building on this, two new solutions that reduce the conservativeness of the specifications are proposed. First, Gershgorin-based decentralized specifications are formulated in the modified sequence domain. Second, a framework for combining different specification types across frequency ranges is developed and mathematically proven. The methods are compared on examples covering sub-synchronous and harmonic-range interactions of grid-following converters, grid-forming converters, and a mixed grid-forming/grid-following system, using analytical models, black-box impedance measurements, and time-domain responses obtained from simulations and an experimental setup.

authors.name: Lazar Stojanovi\'c, Ru\v{z}ica Cvetanovi\'c, Paolo Mattavelli, Simone Buso

papers.title: Adaptive Virtual PIN-Button Recognition on Passive NFC Cards via Domain Adaptation and Uncertainty Quantification
papers.summary: Passive Near Field Communication (NFC) cards are widely used for access control and authentication but provide no native interface for reliable user input. Radio-frequency (RF)-based interaction recognition offers a way to enable input on these cards, but hardware-dependent signal variations across cards and readers limit recognition reliability. This paper presents a practical virtual input framework that enables reliable PIN-button entry on passive NFC cards using a 12-button interface without modifying the commercial NFC card or the ISO/IEC 15693 communication protocol. We develop a multi-domain adaptation framework that jointly learns interaction representations invariant to both card and reader variations. To improve decision reliability, we introduce a model-agnostic uncertainty quantification framework based on conformal prediction that estimates recognition confidence. When confidence is insufficient, the system requests re-input; otherwise, accepted inputs are immediately confirmed through reader feedback, enabling reliable user interaction. A Software-Defined Radio (SDR)-based ISO/IEC 15693 testbed is developed using multiple commercial NFC cards and reader configurations. Experimental results show that domain adaptation improves recognition accuracy from 93.75% to 95.42% for the deep learning (DL) model and from 85.00% to 89.11% for the Random Forest model. Conformal prediction further enables adaptive high-confidence recognition, achieving average recognition accuracies of 96.85% and 90.55% for the DL and Random Forest models, respectively, across diverse hardware configurations.

authors.name: Dickson Akuoko Sarpong, Hongzhi Guo

papers.title: Agentic Wireless Optimization: Workflow Automation, Algorithm Design, and Multi-Timescale Network Operations
papers.summary: Optimization is fundamental to wireless communications, from characterizing channel capacity and designing transmission schemes to allocating network resources. However, conventional workflows require substantial expertise and manual effort, particularly for high-dimensional or nonconvex problems, black-box objectives, and interdependent decisions across time scales. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI), particularly agents based on large language models (LLMs), offer new opportunities to address these challenges by integrating reasoning, tool use, and numerical feedback. This article presents an overview of agentic AI for wireless optimization, focusing on workflow automation, algorithm design, and multi-timescale network operations. First, LLM-based agents streamline optimization workflows by automating problem formulation, code generation, numerical solution, and result verification in a closed loop. Second, they facilitate algorithm design by combining and configuring existing numerical methods and refining learning-based optimizers, using numerical feedback to improve solution quality and computational efficiency for nonconvex and black-box problems. Third, they support multi-timescale network operations by decomposing coupled problems into interdependent subtasks and coordinating their solutions to satisfy network-level objectives and service requirements. A multicast beamforming case study demonstrates performance gains from agent-developed solvers, particularly in execution time, and a network energy-saving example illustrates how agents coordinate dynamic base station activation, user association, and beamforming across time scales. Finally, we discuss open challenges and research opportunities in agentic wireless optimization.

authors.name: Yuan Guo, Zixiang Ren, Ruihua Luo, Yilong Chen, Ya-Feng Liu, Xianghao Yu, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng, Jie Xu

papers.title: Continuous-Discrete Dual-Domain Co-Design for Optimized Digital Control of Power Converters
papers.summary: Optimizing digital control for power converters typically involves designing continuous-time controllers and discretizing them via Euler, Tustin, or Generalized Bilinear Transform (GBT) methods. However, the intrinsic coupling between continuous-domain control parameters and discrete-domain implementation parameters remains underexplored, often leading to suboptimal performance. To bridge this gap, this paper first establishes a Non-Uniqueness Theorem, elucidating the coupling mechanism between dual-domain parameters. Based on this, two co-design methodologies are proposed to derive optimized parameter sets: the Explicit Frequency-Domain Analytical Method (EFDAM) and the Implicit Computer-Aided Search Method (ICASM). The EFDAM derives closed-form solutions by maximizing the crossover frequency and resonant magnitude via logarithmic frequency stability criteria, while minimizing discretization errors using Taylor-series bounds. The ICASM formulates the search for optimized parameters as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem, balancing bandwidth, resonant magnitude, and fundamental magnitude. To solve ICASM efficiently, two algorithms are introduced: the Multi-Start COBYLA (MS-COBYLA), which employs Latin Hypercube Sampling for physics-informed initialization to escape local optima, and the PSO-COBYLA hybrid algorithm, which couples global particle swarm exploration with local refinement. Experimental results on a 5-kW single-phase inverter with a Proportional-Integral-Resonant (PIR) regulator validate that the proposed methods outperform the conventional benchmark, achieving a 43.3\% reduction in the peak-to-peak current ripple measured at the zero-active-power operating point and an 11.7\%--35.9\% decrease in THDi across various harmonic profiles.

authors.name: Shen Chen, Jinjun Liu, Xuancai Zhu, Yanlong Li, Jisong Wang, Shuaipo Guo, Zhipeng Song, Lijun Hang, Zeng Liu

papers.title: Frequency-Frame Covariance for Reactive-Power Scalarization
papers.summary: Measured voltage and current waveforms may be represented in a reference frame whose frequency differs from the physical fundamental frequency. Reactive-power readouts calculated from such frequency-shifted coordinates may change if their readout operators are not transformed consistently. This paper presents a frequency-frame covariance formulation for finite-spectrum, zero-mean periodic waveforms with complete harmonic information over one physical period. A necessary and sufficient covariance condition is derived, requiring the readout operator to transform consistently with the waveform representation. Consequently, frequency-dependent harmonic weights must be evaluated at physical harmonic orders rather than relative frame labels. In particular, the derivative/Iliovici readout equals a relative-derivative contribution plus an explicit reference contribution. The formulation also separates readout-operator errors from errors caused by changes in the physical components retained by waveform projections. Three analytical cases illustrate conditional carrier recovery for a memoryless resistor, physical-frequency weighting at relative zero in an RLC branch, and the possibility that an exact reactive-power scalar can coexist with a substantial waveform error after projection. The scope is deterministic calculation consistency in frequency-shifted coordinates rather than instrument measurement uncertainty.

authors.name: Kai Sun

papers.title: Conflict-Aware Impedance-Sensitivity-Based Tuning for Multi-Mode Damping Enhancement
papers.summary: Impedance-based eigenvalue sensitivity provides a practical way to relate converter parameters to poorly damped system modes, but tuning becomes nontrivial when one parameter improves one target mode while degrading another. This paper introduces a conflict-aware tuning strategy for simultaneous damping enhancement of multiple modes. The method converts impedance-derived eigenvalue sensitivities into normalized damping-ratio sensitivities, diagnoses opposing modal tuning directions, and selects either one parameter or a coordinated pair at each iteration. A low-dimensional max--min problem maximizes the predicted damping of the worst target mode subject to parameter limits, protected-mode constraints, and implementation-specific feasibility requirements. Each accepted update is verified on the full system model and the sensitivities are recomputed. Studies on a four-bus system and a modified IEEE 14-bus system demonstrate the value of pairwise coordination, including a case in which single-parameter tuning stops before the predefined damping target is reached.

authors.name: Quang Manh Hoang, Xuan Thanh Trinh, Sina Zarrabian, Akhtar Hussain, Van-Hai Bui

papers.title: Adaptive Grid-Mode-Aware Hybrid Energy Storage Control for AI Data Center Oscillation Mitigation
papers.summary: Oscillatory power components in AI data-center demand can produce large frequency deviations when they coincide with vulnerable grid modes. Mode-aware hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs) can selectively suppress these components, but their effectiveness degrades when the grid mode changes while the control target remains fixed. This paper proposes a closed-loop grid-mode-adaptive HESS control framework that integrates measurement-based modal identification with mode-selective control. A sliding-window N4SID estimator identifies the local grid dynamics from grid-side power and frequency measurements, and the resulting natural-frequency estimate is used to retune the modal suppression branch assigned to the supercapacitor. The framework is evaluated under a grid-mode shift from 0.50 to 1.35Hz while maintaining equal physical damping and approximately equal load excitation at both frequencies. Compared with the fixed-target controller, the adaptive method reduces the post-change grid-side modal power component from 8.78 to 2.02MW, corresponding to a 76.94% reduction, and substantially lowers the resulting frequency deviation.

authors.name: Quang Manh Hoang, Sina Mohammadi, Phi Long Nguyen, Wencong Su, Van-Hai Bui

papers.title: Transmission Expansion with Large, Discrete Data Center Realization Uncertainty
papers.summary: Large data center projects introduce a distinct transmission planning uncertainty because of their large scale, discrete project realization nature, and strong locational impacts on the transmission network. On the one hand, conventional deterministic treatments can either overbuild the network by assuming that all candidate projects materialize; on the other, they can leave the system underprepared by prematurely screening out projects. This paper develops a project-realization-based framework for systematically modeling, planning, and evaluating transmission expansion under uncertain data center realization. Candidate data center projects are represented through alternative realization scenarios and associated probabilities, enabling different planning strategies to be modeled and quantitatively assessed under a common framework. Within this framework, numerical case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and the benefits of stochastic planning approach. The results show that stochastic planning can use realization probabilities to hedge multiple plausible futures, providing a more balanced tradeoff between transmission investment and reliability exposure than deterministic approaches under correctly specified and misspecified realization probabilities.

authors.name: Lin Dong, Samuel Talkington, Le Xie

papers.title: Secrecy and Covertness Analysis of SWAN-Enabled Uplink EDMA-NOMA Systems
papers.summary: Environment division multiple access (EDMA) has recently emerged as a promising multiple-access paradigm by exploiting the wireless propagation environment for user separation, while physical-layer security, including secrecy and covert communication, is becoming increasingly important for protecting confidential information and user privacy. Motivated by these considerations, this paper proposes an EDMA-enabled non-orthogonal multiple access for secrecy and covert communications (EDMA-NOMA-SC) framework for uplink wireless systems. In the proposed framework, a segmented-waveguide-enabled pinching antenna system (SWAN) is employed, where a secrecy user and an intermittently active covert user share the same transmission resource through NOMA within each segment, while a malicious warden attempts to eavesdrop on the secrecy transmission and detect the presence of the covert communication. To capture practical operating conditions, distance-dependent blockage, inter-segment interference, in-waveguide attenuation, imperfect channel state information (ipCSI), and imperfect successive interference cancellation (ipSIC) are considered. Semi-analytical frameworks are developed to characterize the secrecy outage probability (SOP), average secrecy capacity (ASC), false alarm probability (FAP), missed detection probability (MDP), detection error probability (DEP), and covert rate (CR), with their accuracy verified through Monte Carlo simulations. Numerical results, including comparisons with conventional and EDMA-based benchmark schemes, show that the proposed framework generally achieves improved secrecy and covert-rate performance owing to reduced user-to-pinching-antenna propagation distances and in-waveguide attenuation. However, excessive segmentation can degrade performance when inter-segment interference outweighs these propagation benefits.

authors.name: Sagnik Bhattacharyya, Keshav Singh, Shiv Kumar, Chih-Peng Li

papers.title: Look Before You Move: Multimodal Sensing-Aided Trajectory and Beamforming Design for 6DMA
papers.summary: Six-dimensional movable antenna (6DMA) technology allows a base station (BS) to adjust the three-dimensional (3D) positions and 3D rotations, i.e., the 6D poses, of its surfaces. Many existing 6DMA designs select the poses based on prior channel knowledge. However, the channels at a new pose can be estimated only after the surfaces have moved to this pose, and the limited movement speeds of the surfaces restrict the poses reachable at the next time step. To address these challenges, we propose a learning-based multimodal sensing-aided trajectory and beamforming design for multiuser 6DMA systems with mobile users and surrounding objects. The BS observes the users and surrounding objects with RGB images, LiDAR point clouds, and GPS positions, independently of the poses of the surfaces. Since a surface may need several time steps to reach a favorable pose, the BS designs a 6DMA trajectory over several future time steps and executes only its first step, following receding-horizon control. We propose a neural network, in which user-centric cross-modal attention and temporal self-attention modules relate each user to the scene and its sensing history, and surface-to-user attention relates each surface to the users. A projection layer keeps the poses feasible under the geometric and kinematic constraints, and a graph attention module allocates the transmit power along the pilot-based beamforming directions. Performance evaluations using the CARLA driving simulator and Sionna ray tracing (RT) demonstrate significant minimum-rate gains of the proposed design over fixed-position antennas. Ablation studies validate the contributions of multimodal sensing and the proposed attention modules to these gains. The results further highlight the importance of designing the trajectory several time steps ahead, which is more beneficial under tighter speed limits of the surfaces.

authors.name: Zeyu Hao, Wentao Yu, Lutz Lampe, Vincent W. S. Wong

papers.title: SIM-Enabled Wave-Domain Processing in MIMO-OFDM Receivers: Architecture, Modeling, and Validation
papers.summary: This paper develops a wave-domain linear receiver for wideband MIMO-OFDM, where the main high-dimensional linear processing conventionally performed after sampling is physically shifted to propagation through stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs). The proposed receiver transforms receive-port waveforms into OFDM-domain symbols through three cascaded SIM-enabled functional sections. The first section, SIM_1, performs channel-memory processing and channel shortening in an energy-concentration sense, suppressing the out-of-cyclic-prefix (CP) effective tail before OFDM analysis. SIM_2 realizes CP removal and discrete Fourier transform (DFT) analysis as cyclic-windowed OFDM matched filtering by exploiting useful-window memory and analytical Fourier phase coding. SIM_3 implements residual virtual-subcarrier MIMO linear detection, completing the wave-domain linear receive chain up to symbol slicing. Synchronization, control, slicing, and decoding remain digital, while the dominant linear receive operations are moved to the wave domain. A staged configuration framework is developed: the numerology-dependent OFDM analyzer is compiled offline, whereas the channel-dependent memory processor and detector are configured over the coherence time using architecture-aware learning-assisted control. Numerical results validate both functional replacement and link performance, confirming nearly lossless replacement under CP-sufficient MIMO-OFDM conditions, with robustness to residual timing offsets and effective channel-delay-profile perturbations. Substantial gains under CP-insufficient channels are also demonstrated by suppressing out-of-CP leakage before OFDM analysis.

authors.name: Zheao Li, Jiancheng An, Chau Yuen

papers.title: Vertical Segmented Waveguide-Enabled Pinching Antenna (V-SWAN)-Assisted EDMA-NOMA Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems
papers.summary: This paper proposes a vertical segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (V-SWAN)-assisted downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) environmental division multiple access (EDMA) framework for simultaneously supporting multi-user communication and target sensing. In the proposed framework, multiple pinching antennas (PAs) are deployed along a segmented vertical dielectric waveguide to serve communication users (CUs), aerial users (AUs), and sensing target (ST). CUs are distributed on the ground, whereas AUs and ST are above the ground, where line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) propagation conditions coexist. In particular, SWAN provides an effective platform for realizing EDMA by reducing the effective propagation distance and in-waveguide attenuation, thereby suppressing co-channel interference and enabling efficient multi-user transmission. The communication and sensing model are formulated, followed by the corresponding SINR expressions. We formulate the statistical characterizations for the combination of LoS and NLoS propagation for CUs, and LoS propagation for AUs and sensing channels for generalized multi-user, multi-PA scenarios. Based on these statistical characterizations, the segment outage and sensing outage probabilities are derived and evaluated for the generalized framework. The asymptotic evaluation is also done at a high transmit signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to gain further insights. The results show that the proposed framework outperforms the conventional H-SWAN and single vertical pinching antenna system (V-PASS) in terms of segment outage probability, sensing outage probability, and segment sum rate. Monte Carlo simulation results closely match the analytical results, validating the accuracy of the derived expressions.

authors.name: Arnav Hari, Sagnik Bhattacharyya, Keshav Singh, Meng-Lin Ku, Brijesh Kumbhani

papers.title: AFDMA with Heterogeneous Post-Chirp Parameters: Supporting User-Specific Waveform Configurations
papers.summary: This paper investigates a downlink affine frequency division multiple access (AFDMA) framework supporting flexible user-specific waveform configurations with heterogeneous post-chirp parameters. The proposed framework is in sharp contrast to conventional disjoint chirp-subcarrier allocation, which may destroy inter-user orthogonality when users employ heterogeneous post-chirp parameters. Such a loss of orthogonality manifests as cross-basis leakage onto user-allocated chirp subcarriers, which we characterize by analyzing the cross-projection between user-specific discrete affine Fourier transform bases. Specifically, we express the cross-projection entries as quadratic Gauss sums whose quadratic coefficients depend on pairwise post-chirp differences. This yields a sufficient pairwise residue-class orthogonality rule that preserves inter-user orthogonality by satisfying the leakage-free condition. The resulting chirp-subcarrier allocation problem with pairwise modular constraints is reduced to the residue-class level. To solve this problem, we develop a two-stage framework that recursively searches for a feasible representative allocation and deterministically assigns the remaining residue classes. We prove that the problem is either infeasible or admits an optimal full-loading solution. Simulations show that the proposed allocation avoids the bit error rate (BER) floors and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) ceiling of conventional localized allocation, achieves near-single-user BER, and provides comparable BER while reducing receiver complexity compared with conventional common-maximum-post-chirp AFDMA.

authors.name: Hengyou Kong, Xiaoli Xu, Zilong Liu, Yanqun Tang, Yong Zeng

papers.title: Analyzing Simultaneous Charging Factors of Electric Vehicles Using Monte Carlo Simulation: A Case Study in Phu Quoc City, Vietnam
papers.summary: This study estimates the simultaneous charging factor (SCF) of electric vehicles (EVs) in Phu Quoc City, Vietnam, using a Monte Carlo simulation. Three planning scenarios (2030, 2035, and 2040) are developed from population-based EV uptake assumptions and vehicle-specific charging probability profiles over 24 hours, reflecting distinct operating patterns of motorbikes, cars, taxis, and buses. For each vehicle class and scenario, 1,000 simulation runs are performed to compute SCF and its uncertainty, reported via 95% confidence intervals. Results indicate that SCF decreases as EV penetration increases, implying more temporally dispersed charging demand and a reduced likelihood of extreme coincidence. For electric buses, SCF declines from 0.76 (2030) to 0.59 (2040), and other vehicle groups show similarly decreasing trends across the horizon. These SCF estimates provide practical inputs for grid-aware charging infrastructure planning, including diversity factors for sizing distribution transformers and feeders, identifying peak-hour stress, and informing demand management measures such as time of use tariffs and basic smart charging controls.

authors.name: Tien Khai Nguyen, Trong Nghia Le

papers.title: Multi-Period Bilevel Coordination of Primary and Secondary Frequency Regulation for Grid-Forming Battery Energy Storage
papers.summary: We study the coordination of primary and secondary frequency regulation by grid-forming battery energy storage systems in islanded microgrids. We formulate the coordination as a multi-period bilevel program, in which the upper level schedules secondary regulation setpoints and each lower level computes primary regulation decisions. Using the lower-level Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, we obtain an exact single-level reformulation with complementarity constraints. To address the numerical difficulties introduced by these constraints, we develop a continuation method that couples the complementarity relaxation parameter with the interior-point barrier parameter and warm-starts successive stages. Under the stated boundedness assumptions and with vanishing subproblem residuals, we prove that every accumulation point is feasible and satisfies a first-order stationarity condition for the reformulated problem (C-stationarity). Numerical results for an islanded microgrid show that the proposed method reduces solution time by 89.3% and peak frequency deviation by 0.53% relative to conventional Scholtes relaxation.

authors.name: Wenju Shang, Liangliang Hao, Jiangliang Jin, Yunjian Xu

papers.title: Eco-MP: Ecological Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control with Ecological Driving
papers.summary: Max-pressure (MP) traffic signal control provides a decentralized mechanism for urban networks, but conventional pressure states do not directly capture the propulsion burden generated by signal-induced stop-and-go traffic. Eco-driving, by contrast, typically relies on prespecified signal information and optimizes vehicle trajectories separately from the feedback among vehicle motion, traffic states, and signal decisions. This paper develops Ecological Max-Pressure (Eco-MP), a closed-loop framework that integrates ecological MP signal control with MP-adaptive ecological driving. At the signal layer, connected-vehicle observations are aggregated into a common movement state based on cumulative positive propulsion work, and the resulting upstream--downstream ecological pressure determines phase selection in mixed petrol and electric traffic. At the vehicle layer, a rolling signal interface translates the evolving Eco-MP process into near-term signal information, while each connected and automated vehicle solves a powertrain-independent finite-horizon trajectory problem subject to vehicle-dynamic, car-following, and signal-compliance constraints to reduce unnecessary stopping and acceleration effort. Under full-state information, a finite-storage Lyapunov analysis establishes strong stability for admissible demands satisfying a strict supportability condition and extends the result to the coupled signal--vehicle system. When ecological driving enlarges the admissible-flow sets, the coupled admissible demand region contains the signal-only region. Microscopic experiments on an Amsterdam arterial corridor show that, relative to queue-based MP, Eco-MP reduces mean positive propulsion work by 5.2%, vehicle delay by 20.8%, and stopping time by 39.0%. With only 15% of vehicles directly controlled, ecological driving further reduces positive propulsion work by 4.2% and stopping time by 19.6%......

authors.name: Haoran Wang, Shuoyuan Li, Chaopeng Tan, Hao Liu, Keshuang Tang, Jia Hu

papers.title: EEG-based listened-language classification
papers.summary: From an early age, individuals are continuously exposed to other languages beyond their native tongue; however, the brain s response to these auditory stimuli remains unclear. To investigate this, an experiment was designed to record electroencephalography (EEG) signals from subjects listening to sentences in five different languages, and a specific database was built to enable performing classification tests to distinguish between different languages, and varying levels of language comprehension. By analysing the energy difference between the EEG channels to characterize these signals, different classification tests were conducted using bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (bi-LSTM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) neural networks. The main objective is the analysis of the brain s response in two different scenarios: when the subject listens to sentences in different languages, and when the subject understands or misunderstands the meaning of a sentence. In tire multi-class classification involving sentences in five different languages, the accuracy attained is 36.37 %. However, in the multi-class classification between understood/understood part of the meaning/didn t understand, the accuracy attained reaches 81.36%. The results obtained for binary classification tests of understand native language or foreign language is 89.09 %. The bi-LSTM neural network achieved the overall best performance. These results demonstrate that the analysis of the EEG signals alone can give information regarding a person s language comprehension level, and can be used for monitoring the learning curve of a new language or to assess comprehension in patients with conditions such as aphasia.

authors.name: Isaac Ariza, Lorenzo J. Tard\'on, Ana M. Barbancho, Isabel Barbancho

papers.title: Sensing the Variation of Wireless Propagation Environment Based on Channel Knowledge Map
papers.summary: With the evolution of sixth-generation (6G) wireless systems, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has raised the demand for high-precision environmental perception. To address the limited capability of existing techniques in sensing environmental variations, this work proposes a novel channel knowledge map (CKM)-based sensing framework that enables structural change sensing in the wireless propagation environment. By leveraging historical CKM data and real?time user channel, a mathematical model is formulated to infer the changing reflectors which represents the environment variations. Specifically, we propose the Information Aggregation Based Robust Two-Stage Reflection Point Refinement (IA-TS-RPR) scheme for reflection point (RP) estimation, which first uses block coordinate descent (BCD) and Riemannian manifold optimization (RMO) for initial estimation, then applies virtual base station (VBS) clustering for information aggregation in the sensitive area (SA) to refine the estimation. Furthermore, we propose an Environment Variation Sensing scheme based on the Hausdorff-Nearest Neighbor Criterion and Time-Window Voting (EVS-HC-TWV). Specifically, the Hausdorff distance is used to match each user to its most relevant CKM grid point (GP), and a time-window-based multi-user voting mechanism is further employed to improve robustness against positional deviations. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed IA-TS-RPR scheme maintains sub-meter RP position estimation accuracy under user positioning errors, significantly outperforming the scheme based on time of arrival (ToA), linear minimum mean square error (LMMSE) and least squares (LS). The proposed scheme successfully senses and localizes dynamic reflectors, showing strong generalizability and robustness.

authors.name: Haohan Li, Wence Zhang, Xiaoyan Shao, Xu Bao, Jing Xia, Yong Zeng

papers.title: Continuous Wideband Multicarrier Rydberg Atomic Quantum Receiver
papers.summary: This paper investigates continuous wideband orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) reception using an auxiliary (AUX)-assisted five-level Rydberg atomic quantum receiver (RAQR) with a single microwave local oscillator (LO), without requiring additional atomic reception transitions or LO frequency combs. By exploiting Floquet theory, the proposed framework characterizes the dynamic atomic response at finite signal-LO detunings without relying on a quasi-static Taylor expansion around the LO operating point. Specifically, closed-form radio-frequency (RF)-to-electrical conversion expressions are derived from the Lindblad master equation under weak-probe and weak-signal approximations. Building on these expressions, an equivalent multicarrier communication model is established, revealing the inherent frequency selectivity of the atomic response and the resulting subcarrier-dependent amplitude and phase distortions. RAQR-aware zero-forcing (ZF) equalization is developed to enable reliable OFDM reception. Furthermore, analytical results reveal how LO and AUX driving influence the atomic response through dressed-state splitting and energy-level shifts. An upper bound on the LO-referenced half-power span is derived, and an approximately $18$-dB reduction in center-response power per bandwidth doubling is established in the AUX-free strong-LO regime. Simulation results validate the analytical response model and reveal pronounced subcarrier-dependent amplitude and phase variations across over $10$~MHz, highlighting the potential of RAQRs as wideband receiving front ends for future wireless communications.

authors.name: Qihao Peng, Qu Luo, Maged Elkashlan, Cunhua Pan, Pei Xiao, George K. Karagiannidis, Trung Q. Duong, Jiangzhou Wang

papers.title: Data-Driven Likelihood-Ratio Construction for Radar Detection via Bernstein Induction Operators
papers.summary: Accurate likelihood-ratio (LR) construction is challenging when clutter statistics are unknown. Prespecified clutter models may not adequately describe the observed data, and evaluating target-present densities may require computationally expensive marginalization. This paper proposes a data-driven LR construction framework based on a Bernstein polynomial model (BPM) and a Bernstein induction operator (BIO). The BPM weights are estimated from clutter-only samples, whereas the target-induced responses of the Bernstein basis densities are approximated offline in the same basis to construct column-stochastic matrices. These matrices map clutter-density weights to target-present density weights at specified signal-to-clutter ratios (SCRs), and mixtures of the matrices account for target fluctuations. For a fixed target model and basis representation, the matrix library is independent of the clutter-density weights and can be reused across clutter distributions. The resulting LR construction avoids repeated online evaluation of the physical-induction integrals. Simulations under analytical clutter models show close agreement with the reference LRs and detection probabilities, with lower online computation times in the non-Gaussian cases considered. Experiments using synthetic target echoes embedded in measured sea clutter further show improved detection probabilities relative to the evaluated baselines in the weak-target regime.

authors.name: Yuxin Xu, Jun Tang, Ting Bai

papers.title: ST-CGMDiff: Sparse-Conditioned Cross-Frequency Spatio-Temporal Latent Diffusion for Dynamic 3D Channel Gain Map Reconstruction
papers.summary: Accurate and efficient reconstruction of channel gain maps (CGMs) is essential for environment-aware wireless communications. Unlike prior works that focus on static CGMs at a single frequency band, this paper studies the construction of dynamic three-dimensional (3D) CGMs across multiple frequency bands over consecutive time slots, using limited channel measurements. Specifically, for a given transmitter (Tx) location, we represent the CGM at any given receiver (Rx) height as a two-dimensional (2D) grayscale image, where each pixel indicates the average channel gain over the corresponding Rx spatial grid cell. Accordingly, we propose ST-CGMDiff, a spatio-temporal latent diffusion framework that integrates sparse-observation conditioning and cross-frequency modeling to reconstruct dynamic 3D CGMs across multiple carrier frequencies and varying Rx heights within a unified model. In this framework, we jointly encode the input parameters, including the current sparse observations, observation masks, physical Tx and Rx z-coordinates, and carrier frequencies as spatial conditions. A frequency-conditioned convolutional gated recurrent unit (ConvGRU) then extracts causal information from previously constructed CGMs, while a spatially adaptive fusion mechanism balances historical information and current observations. Furthermore, bidirectional convolutional long short-term memory (BiConvLSTM) modules are introduced to capture the ordered dependencies among the selected Rx z-layers. Finally, we perform few-step latent diffusion followed by high-resolution residual refinement to generate the final CGM with improved spatial fidelity.

authors.name: Tianxiang Li, Yilong Chen, Han Hu, Yong Zeng, Jie Xu

papers.title: Ambiguity Elimination via Successive Estimation in ISAC Systems with Reference Signals
papers.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems can efficiently reuse 5G New Radio (NR) reference signals to enable joint communication and passive target detection. Among these, the Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) is widely adopted for high-performance sensing activities. However, the PRS configuration, given by the comb structure, introduces periodic ambiguities, resulting in ghost targets. Existing approaches mitigate this issue by combining PRS with additional reference signals, such as the DeModulation Reference Signal (DMRS), effectively removing ghosts but at the cost of higher complexity and sensing overhead. This paper proposes a low-complexity successive estimation strategy that initially allows ghost targets but progressively eliminates them using historical ambiguity-free estimations. The method comprises a matching process to associate current detections with historical real targets, and a pattern deviation detection mechanism to trigger a fallback to ambiguity-free estimation when the target set changes. We derive a sufficient condition that guarantees the correct matching as a function of target velocity, PRS comb size, subcarrier spacing, and sensing refresh rate. Using this condition, a parameter selection strategy is proposed to jointly improve sensing and communication performance. Numerical results demonstrate that our method achieves unambiguous detection while significantly reducing sensing resources, thus releasing more resources for communication compared to State-of-the-Art (SotA) approaches.

authors.name: Ali Al Khansa, Sami Mekki, Giyyarpuram Madhusudan

papers.title: One ISAC Array, Two Worst Cases: Hardware Impairments in Beamforming and AoA Estimation
papers.summary: In integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), the same base-station array beamforms toward users and estimates their angle of arrival (AoA). In this paper, we study how element-level gain, phase, and position errors affect both functions of a beam-scanning uniform linear array. Any array produces a correlation peak at the true angle, of finite height and width, surrounded by sidelobes. Impairments shift this peak, make it lower and wider, and raise the sidelobes relative to it. A single decomposition explains these three effects: the gain-weighted least-squares fit of the per-antenna phase errors splits them into a tilt, which shifts the peak, and a residual, whose power is taken from the peak and redistributed over the sidelobes according to its spatial spectrum. A beam steered toward the strongest direction suffers from the lower peak only, whereas the AoA estimate suffers from its shift even without noise, and also from the lowering and sidelobes with noise. The worst cases for the two ISAC functions are thus nearly disjoint, and we characterize both: the worst case for beamforming leaves the AoA estimate unbiased, and the worst case for localization loses little beamforming gain. The worst case for localization is a single defect at the junction between two subarrays, and its error, relative to the main-lobe width, does not decrease with the number of antennas. We also characterize random impairments and the effect of noise. In practical terms, our analysis shows that the calibration of a dual-function array must be assessed with respect to both functions.

authors.name: Xuan Chen (INSA Rennes, IETR), Luc Le Magoarou (INSA Rennes, IETR)

papers.title: Ghost Target Elimination in 5G Reference Signals ISAC via Multi-static Multilateration
papers.summary: Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems can reuse 5G New Radio (NR) reference signals to enable joint communication and environmental sensing. Among these signals, the Positioning Reference Signal (PRS) is particularly suitable for range and Doppler estimation. However, its comb structure introduces periodic ambiguities that generate ghost targets. Existing solutions resolve these ambiguities by combining PRS with additional signals such as the DeModulation Reference Signal (DMRS), which increases sensing overhead. This paper proposes a PRS-only sensing framework that resolves ambiguities using multi-static observations. Instead of removing ghosts locally at each receiver, the proposed method exploits spatial diversity and performs ambiguity resolution at a fusion anchor. The anchor jointly estimates target locations and ambiguity indices via multilateration across multiple sensing nodes. This approach eliminates the need for additional reference signals while maintaining low receiver complexity. Simulation results show that the proposed method reliably resolves ghost targets and achieves superior detection performance compared to benchmark methods across various scenarios, while significantly enhancing resource efficiency by enabling sensing using PRS-only transmissions.

authors.name: Ali Al Khansa, Sami Mekki

papers.title: Transversal Passivity: Dissipation Relative to Input and Output Manifolds
papers.summary: This paper introduces transversal passivity, a local dissipation property for regulating input and output signals to prescribed manifolds. Its supply rate is built from the transverse port errors induced by nearest-point projections, so that motion along the manifolds is not penalized. We give a necessary condition and a constructive sufficient condition for the property and relate it to existing passivity notions. For feedback interconnections through negative-adjoint linear channels, power conservation no longer cancels the transverse supply. The residual is governed by compatibility defects that depend only on the channels and the prescribed manifolds, so it can be assessed before any closed-loop analysis, and it falls into a hierarchy of exact compatibility, quadratic cancellation, and nonzero quadratic residuals. Since transversal storages are only positive semidefinite, port convergence is obtained by combining compact confinement, for instance by conserved quantities, with a dissipation margin, and we identify a geometric obstruction under which no quadratic margin is available near the feasible states. A federated learning case study with heterogeneous data shows that port convergence can be certified even though no server target is compatible with the interconnection, and that the obstruction arises for a natural choice of target.

authors.name: Feng-Yu Yue, Daniel Zelazo

papers.title: Virtual Microphone Array for Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Based on Fiber-Optic Position Sensing
papers.summary: This paper presents a virtual microphone array approach for estimating the direction of arrival of a sound source using a moving microphone and a stationary reference microphone. The method exploits the microphone motion to generate a time-varying array geometry, using fiber-optic position sensing to reconstruct the trajectory and determine the resulting virtual microphone configurations. For each configuration, the estimated time difference of arrival between the two microphone signals and the corresponding microphone geometry define a hyperboloid representing all possible sound source positions consistent with the time difference. By combining multiple hyperboloid constraints, the direction of arrival can be estimated in azimuth and elevation relative to the microphone coordinate system. In contrast to conventional arrays with fixed geometries and approaches based on predefined microphone trajectories, the proposed method derives the virtual array geometry directly from the measured microphone motion, enabling a spatially distributed virtual array to be formed using only two physical microphones and offering potential for size- and weight-constrained applications. The approach was experimentally evaluated under controlled low-reflection conditions for different source positions, source distances, and signal characteristics. The influence of microphone motion was further examined, and the method was tested with a moving sound source. The results demonstrate the feasibility of direction-of-arrival estimation using a virtual microphone array without requiring a predefined microphone trajectory.

authors.name: Sebastian Schwarze (Electronic Media Technology Group, Technische Universit\"at Ilmenau, Germany), Jiekai Wang (Nanofabrication and Nanomeasurement Technology Group, Technische Universit\"at Ilmenau, Germany), Thomas Kissinger (Nanofabrication and Nanomeasurement Technology Group, Technische Universit\"at Ilmenau, Germany), Stephan Werner (Electronic Media Technology Group, Technische Universit\"at Ilmenau, Germany)

papers.title: Speaker-Consistent Grounding for Confusion-Resilient LLM-Based Target Speech Extraction
papers.summary: Deterministic target-speaker extraction (TSE) tends to preserve observed linguistic content but may extract the interfering speaker. In contrast, autoregressive generative TSE improves perceptual quality, but is prone to content hallucination and speaker identity drift, which can be mitigated by model grounding with the evidence from the deterministic TSE. However, grounding such a generative TSE model with speaker-confused evidence may therefore reinforce the error. To address this gap, we proposed a repair-before-grounding framework with a training-free evidence-repair stage. Conditioning-diverse candidate selection (CDCS) selects target speaker-consistent evidence from complementary frozen TSE outputs. The selected waveform can then be used by code-space grounding (CSG) to constrain LLM-based TSE decoding. On Libri2Mix, CDCS reduces wrong-speaker extraction errors from 6.87% to 0.75% on clean mixtures and from 18.95% to 10.46% under noise. With the LLM-based TSE checkpoint unchanged, CSG further reduces noisy content- and acoustic-switch rates from 12.79% and 1.68% to 9.10% and 0.51%, respectively. Despite this stronger grounding, generative TSE retains its predicted perceptual-quality advantage over direct deterministic extraction. These results show that repairing evidence identity before grounding improves the reliability of generative TSE. Audio demos and code are available at https://hanyu-meng.github.io/LLM-TSE-Grounding-Demo/.

authors.name: Hanyu Meng, Hao Shi, Zhanhong He, Qiquan Zhang, Yang Xiao, Sungwoo Cho, Haowei Lou, Haizhou Li

papers.title: Topology Identification of Directed Signed Networks via Repelling Laplacians
papers.summary: We address the problem of simultaneously identifying the interaction topology and synchronizing a network interconnected over a directed graph that exhibits both cooperative and antagonistic interactions, modeled via a repelling Laplacian matrix. We propose an adaptive control protocol built on a node-centric regressor formulation, in which the network is driven to track a persistently exciting auxiliary network. We then propose a time-varying adaptive gain to remove the need for global knowledge of the network. We establish uniform semiglobal practical asymptotic stability of the estimation errors when the excitation depends only on measurable errors. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical results.

authors.name: Muhammad Ahsan Razaq, Pelin Sekercioglu, Angela Fontan, Dimos V. Dimarogonas, Claudio Altafini

papers.title: The Hearpiece Database of Binaural Room Impulse Responses and Driver Responses on KEMAR
papers.summary: This document describes the measurement setup, signal processing, data organization, and MATLAB file format of a database of acoustic responses measured on a Knowles Electronics Manikin for Acoustic Research (KEMAR) using the Hearpiece, a multi-microphone, multi-driver in-ear research device. The data include binaural room impulse responses (BRIRs) and Hearpiece driver responses, together with center-microphone room impulse responses and a loopback impulse response of the playback and recording system. The BRIRs cover two Hearpiece configurations, three room conditions, three independent insertions per configuration, and 24 horizontal source directions. The database supports reproducible research on binaural and hearing-device signal processing, with potential applications in speech enhancement, spatial filtering and source separation, dereverberation, active noise and occlusion control, and acoustic feedback cancellation. The database, MATLAB loading script, and technical documentation are publicly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23667308.

authors.name: Tong Xiao, Reinhild Roden, Matthias Blau, Simon Doclo

papers.title: Interference-Aware Instantaneous Frequency and Amplitude Estimator for Multicomponent Signals
